research.lane: LANE 1 — THE STRUCTURE (micro-entreprise vs association loi 1901, for a French BTS student commercialising copius.fr from late 2027)
research.bottom_line: Micro-entreprise is the vehicle for all three shapes; the association is only right if the money funds the project rather than Gabriel. Creation is free, online, and takes minutes. The real numbers for 2026: 25,6 % of revenue in cotisations for a BNC prestation de services (21,2 % if BIC), +0,2 % CFP, +2,2 % if he takes the versement libératoire. ACRE still exists and he qualifies on age alone (18–25), but the exoneration was cut from 50 % to 25 % for micro-entreprises created from 1 July 2026 (décret 2026-69) — so the first-year rate is 19,2 % BNC, not 12,8 %. Three student-specific traps, none of them obvious: (1) while he is rattaché to his parents' foyer fiscal, eligibility for the versement libératoire is tested on HIS PARENTS' revenu fiscal de référence, not his; (2) his declared income feeds the revenu brut global that the CROUS uses to set his bourse échelon two years later, and even under the versement libératoire it raises his parents' tax via the taux effectif; (3) under 20, a child stops counting as "à charge" for prestations familiales above 55 % of the SMIC (1 104,25 €/month). Two hard deadlines that are easy to miss: ACRE must be requested within 60 days of starting, and form 1447-C-SD must be filed before 31 December of the creation year or he loses the year-1 CFE exemption. Every 2027 figure below is a 2026 figure — the ACRE rate alone moved twice in 2026, so re-check all of them before he files.

findings.claim: Creating a micro-entreprise is free and done online at the guichet unique (INPI), and it is the only legal route since 2023.
findings.detail: No registration fee for a non-regulated liberal (BNC) activity. The paid exceptions are irrelevant to him: the SPI preparation course for artisanal activities (~260 €) and the commercial-agent register (23,86 €). Chambers of commerce and métiers give free help. The file yields a SIRET and an inscription at the Répertoire national des entreprises.
findings.source_quote: L'immatriculation d'un micro-entrepreneur est gratuite

findings.claim: Cotisations URSSAF from 1 January 2026: 12,3 % vente de marchandises, 21,2 % prestation de services BIC, 25,6 % activité libérale non réglementée BNC — a flat percentage of revenue, not of profit.
findings.detail: This is the single most important number and it depends entirely on how the activity is classified. A paid learning path and consulting work both plausibly land in BNC (25,6 %); certain packaged-product framings land in BIC services (21,2 %). The gap is 4,4 points on every euro — on 20 000 € of revenue that is 880 €/year. Settle the classification before filing, because it is declared at creation.
findings.source_quote: Le montant des cotisations sociales pour les activités libérales non réglementées est égal à 25,6 % du chiffre d'affaires. […] Le montant des cotisations sociales est égal à 21,2 % du chiffre d'affaires.

findings.claim: The BNC rate rose from 24,6 % in 2025 to 25,6 % in 2026 — this rate is on a rising path, so do not plan against a remembered figure.
findings.detail: Part of the reform of the assiette sociale des indépendants: the CSG-CRDS share falls in favour of contributive cotisations (better retirement rights, same cash out). A further step for 2027 is plausible but not published.
findings.source_quote: ce taux atteint 25,6 %
findings.when: Bpifrance Création, "Micro-entrepreneurs : ce qui change en 2026"

findings.claim: The contribution à la formation professionnelle is charged ON TOP of the cotisation rate: 0,2 % for a liberal activity, 0,3 % artisanal, 0,1 % commercial.
findings.detail: Collected as a single payment in November, added to the URSSAF échéance. So the true all-in BNC rate is 25,8 %, not 25,6 %. Small, but it is the difference between a forecast that reconciles and one that does not.
findings.source_quote: For a liberal activity: the amount of the CFP is 0.2% of the annual turnover. […] a single payment in November which is added to the deadline of social contributions and cotisations.

findings.claim: Cadence: monthly or quarterly, chosen at creation, declared online — and the first declaration cannot be filed until at least 90 days after the start of activity.
findings.detail: A business started in September declares its first four months in January, then monthly. A zero-revenue period still gets a declaration; there is simply nothing to pay. This matters for the transition: he can create the entity, declare zero for several periods, and owe nothing while the first offer is built.
findings.source_quote: La première déclaration peut être effectuée au minimum 3 mois (90 jours) après le début de l'activité.

findings.claim: The micro regime's revenue ceilings were raised for 2026: 83 600 € for prestations de services and for BNC, 203 100 € for vente de marchandises.
findings.detail: Previously 77 700 € / 188 700 €. Measured in chiffre d'affaires HT over the civil year, tested against 2025 or 2024. None of the three shapes comes near this in the first years — it is a non-constraint, and worth knowing so it is not treated as one.

findings.claim: ACRE still exists, and Gabriel qualifies on age alone — but the exoneration was cut from 50 % to 25 % for micro-entreprises created on or after 1 July 2026.
findings.detail: Décret n° 2026-69 du 6 février 2026, implementing article 23 of the LFSS 2026 (loi n° 2025-1403 du 30 décembre 2025). For individual entrepreneurs and sociétés the cut applied from 1 January 2026; for micro-entreprises from 1 July 2026. The rule moved twice inside one year — treat any 2027 figure as provisional.
findings.source_quote: Décret n° 2026-69 du 6 février 2026 […] 1er juillet 2026 pour les micro-entreprises

findings.claim: Under ACRE the micro-entrepreneur pays 75 % of the normal rate — BNC 19,2 % instead of 25,6 %, BIC services 15,9 % instead of 21,2 %.
findings.detail: The 15,9 % figure is service-public's own worked example for an electrician (BIC services); 19,2 % is 25,6 × 0,75. On 15 000 € of first-year BNC revenue ACRE is worth 960 €.
findings.cost_eur: saves 6,4 points of revenue (BNC) during the window
findings.source_quote: Le créateur ou repreneur bénéficie d'un taux minoré de cotisations sociales égal à 75 % du taux normal […] Ce taux est égal 15,9 % (au lieu de 21,2 %

findings.claim: ACRE conditions in 2026: one qualifying situation — being aged 18 to 25 is itself one — plus no ACRE in the previous three years, and the request must reach URSSAF within 60 days of the start of activity.
findings.detail: He needs no unemployment status, no RSA, no zone criterion: his age carries him. The list also covers under-30s without enough work history for unemployment rights, so he stays eligible past 25 for a while. URSSAF rules within 30 days and silence is acceptance. The 60-day deadline is the one that actually bites — miss it and the 6,4 points are gone for good.
findings.source_quote: la demande d'Acre doit être effectuée au plus tard le 60e jour suivant la date d'ouverture de l'activité

findings.claim: The ACRE window runs to the end of the 3rd civil quarter following the declared start date — so starting on the FIRST day of a quarter is worth up to three extra months of reduced rate.
findings.detail: Start 1 October 2027 and the window closes 30 September 2028: twelve months. Start 20 December 2027 — same quarter, same closing date — and it is nine months. The start date is free to choose on the creation form; choosing it badly costs roughly a quarter of the benefit.
findings.source_quote: Cette exonération s'applique jusqu'à la fin du 3e trimestre civil suivant la date de début d'activité déclarée

findings.claim: Versement libératoire: 1 % vente, 1,7 % prestation de services BIC, 2,2 % BNC — paid with the cotisations, and it settles income tax on that revenue entirely.
findings.detail: Option exercised with URSSAF by 30 September of year N for year N+1, or within three months of creation. It can be renounced by 30 September for effect on 1 January following. For a BNC activity the all-in rate becomes 25,6 + 0,2 + 2,2 = 28 % of revenue.
findings.source_quote: 1 % pour les activités de commerce, restauration et logement […] 2,2 %

findings.claim: The versement libératoire is gated on the revenu fiscal de référence of the FOYER FISCAL, year N-2 — which, while Gabriel is rattaché, means his parents' income decides whether he can have it.
findings.detail: Ceilings for a 2026 option: 29 579 € for one part, 59 158 € for a couple, 73 947,50 € for a couple with one child, 88 737 € with two. A couple with him rattaché is 2,5 parts → 73 947,50 €. If the household is above it, the option is simply unavailable to him and his revenue goes onto the barème instead. This is the sharpest hidden consequence of rattachement and it is checkable today from the parents' 2025 avis.
findings.source_quote: €29,579 (single person) / €59,158 (couple) / €73,947.50 (couple + 1 child) / €88,737 (couple + 2 children)

findings.claim: The impots.gouv.fr page on the versement libératoire is stale — it still shows the 2024 ceiling of 27 478 € per part and the old 77 700 €/188 700 € thresholds.
findings.detail: Same government, two pages, different numbers. Use service-public F23267 (verified 13 May 2026) for the ceilings and F32353 for the revenue thresholds; treat the impots.gouv.fr VFL landing page as unreliable on figures while still authoritative on mechanism.
findings.source_quote: For 2024 (examining 2022 income): 27,478€ per share […] 77 700 € pour les autres prestataires de services

findings.claim: Student status is not an activity and buys no relief: cotisations are due from the first euro of revenue.
findings.detail: There is no student rate, no franchise, no exemption. The only reduction available to him is ACRE, and he gets that as an 18-25-year-old, not as a student.
findings.source_quote: des cotisations sociales doivent être payées sur le chiffre d'affaires qu'il réalise dans le cadre de sa micro-entreprise

findings.claim: Health cover does not change in practice: the separate student social security regime was abolished at the 2019-2020 rentrée, and both students and new travailleurs indépendants sit in the régime général at the CPAM of residence.
findings.detail: So creating the micro-entreprise does not move him between caisses or interrupt reimbursement. Note that service-public's own page still uses the outdated phrasing "Un étudiant est en principe affilié à la sécurité sociale des étudiants", which is why this deserves a direct check with his CPAM before he relies on it.
findings.source_quote: Le régime étudiant de sécurité sociale a disparu à la rentrée 2019-2020.
findings.when: ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur FAQ; cross-read against service-public F36612 (07/04/2026)

findings.claim: The bourse sur critères sociaux is set from the REVENU BRUT GLOBAL of the reference foyer fiscal, two years back — so income he declares in 2027 sets his échelon for 2029-2030.
findings.detail: For the 2026-2027 campaign the income used is that received in 2024 (2025 avis). Only students who are married, pacsés, or have a dependent child can have their own resources looked at instead. Detaching from his parents' foyer fiscal does not by itself move the bourse onto his own income — it stays on theirs.
findings.source_quote: les revenus retenus sont ceux perçus en 2024 (avis fiscal de 2025) […] revenu brut global de l'avis d'imposition ou de non-imposition

findings.claim: While rattaché, his micro-entreprise income goes on his parents' tax return — and even under the versement libératoire it raises their tax on their own income through the taux effectif.
findings.detail: Without the option, the profit after abattement (50 % for BIC services, 34 % for BNC) is added to the household's taxable income at the barème. With the option, the profit is not taxed again but is "retenu pour le calcul du taux effectif appliqué aux autres revenus du foyer" and is added to the revenu fiscal de référence. There is no configuration in which his revenue is invisible to his parents' tax position.
findings.source_quote: the net profit after deduction of flat-rate allowances...is retained for calculating the effective rate applied to other household income […] is also retained for calculating taxable income reference (RFR)

findings.claim: Rattachement is available until 21, or until 25 for a student — so he has the choice every year, and it is a genuine annual decision, not a permanent state.
findings.detail: Attaching requires a written request from him, kept by the parents. If he detaches, his income leaves their return entirely; they lose the extra part of quotient familial but may deduct a pension alimentaire instead. The arithmetic flips at a revenue level that depends on their marginal rate — it should be computed on their actual avis, not assumed.
findings.source_quote: Si vous êtes rattaché au foyer fiscal de vos parents, ses revenus doivent être déclarés sur leur déclaration fiscale.

findings.claim: For CAF purposes a child stops counting as "à charge" above 55 % of the SMIC — 1 104,25 € per month for October 2025 to March 2026 — and the limit runs to 20 (21 for complément familial and aides au logement).
findings.detail: Gabriel turns 20 in 2028, so the window is live exactly when commercialisation starts. For salaried students the CAF averages earnings over two six-month blocks rather than month by month; the page does not say how it assesses a travailleur indépendant's income, which is the case that applies to him.
findings.source_quote: 55% of minimum wage = €1,104.25 for October 2025-March 2026 period

findings.claim: The statut national étudiant-entrepreneur is free, has no age limit, and can substitute an entrepreneurial project for a mandatory internship — the one student-specific advantage worth chasing.
findings.detail: Requires the bac and enrolment in a recognised higher-education course; gives two PEPITE mentors, coworking, and timetable flexibility. Whether a BTS run inside a lycée can reach a PEPITE is the open question — it turns on the académie's PEPITE convention, not on the statute. Worth one email to the académie's PEPITE, not a research project.
findings.cost_eur: 0 (the accompanying D2E diploma is separately priced by the établissement)
findings.source_quote: le statut national d'étudiant-entrepreneur (SNEE) s'adresse à l'étudiant ou au jeune diplômé qui veut obtenir un accompagnement dans son projet de création d'entreprise

findings.claim: An association loi 1901 can legally sell, but it cannot distribute anything to anyone — no profit in any form, no share of the assets to members.
findings.detail: Gestion désintéressée is three cumulative conditions: bénévole management by people with no direct or indirect interest in results, no direct or indirect distribution of profit in any form, and no attribution of any part of the assets to members or their ayants droit beyond the return of contributions. This is the structural answer to "can the association pay Gabriel": essentially no.
findings.source_quote: L'organisme ne procède à aucune distribution directe ou indirecte de bénéfice, sous quelle que forme que ce soit

findings.claim: The tolerance that lets an association pay its dirigeant stops at ¾ of the SMIC — 1 400,26 € brut per month — and going beyond needs 200 000 € of average annual resources and a fourth year of existence.
findings.detail: Below that ceiling gestion désintéressée survives; above it, without the resources and seniority conditions, the association becomes fiscally commercial. For a project that might generate a few thousand euros a year this is the decisive fact: the association cannot be the way Gabriel earns. It can be the way the project is funded, governed, and made eligible for subventions and appels à projets.
findings.source_quote: ¾ du Smic, soit 1 400,26 € brut par mois

findings.claim: An association becomes fiscally commercial when it competes with business under the règle des 4 P — Produit, Public, Prix, Publicité, weighed in that decreasing order.
findings.detail: The test is a faisceau d'indices, not a checklist: no single criterion has to be met. A paid learning path priced at market, marketed to the general public, promoted commercially, scores badly on all four. A resource offered below market to lycées and CFAs, publicised without commercial advertising, scores well. Shape (b) is the one that can plausibly stay non-lucrative; shape (a) is not.
findings.source_quote: les critères à étudier, dans un ordre d'importance décroissante, sont : le "produit" proposé par l'organisme, le "public" bénéficiaire, les "prix" qu'il pratique et la "publicité" qu'il fait

findings.claim: The franchise that lets an association run accessory commercial activity untaxed is 81 051 € for exercices closed from 31 December 2025 — and service-public still publishes the stale 78 596 €.
findings.detail: Three cumulative conditions: gestion désintéressée maintained, non-lucrative activities remaining significantly preponderant, and lucrative receipts collected in the civil year not exceeding the ceiling. Revalued annually by BOFiP publication. Use BOFiP, not service-public F34104 (verified 04/07/2025), for this number.
findings.source_quote: le montant des recettes d'exploitation encaissées au cours de l'année civile au titre des activités lucratives ne doit pas excéder 81 051 €
findings.when: BOFiP, document dated 5 August 2026; applies to exercices closed from 31/12/2025 for IS and to CET 2026

findings.claim: Declaring an association is free and fast: the greffe issues a récépissé within 5 days of a complete file, and publication in the Journal officiel costs nothing.
findings.detail: Needs a procès-verbal of the assemblée constitutive signed by at least one dirigeant and a dated, signed copy of the statuts signed by at least two. Yields an RNA number (W + 9 digits). So the association is not a heavier structure to create than the micro-entreprise — the weight is in running it (board, minutes, general assembly) and in what it forbids.
findings.source_quote: un récépissé dans les 5 jours suivant la remise du dossier complet

findings.claim: The single 25 000 € VAT franchise threshold from the 2025 finance law was ABANDONED — franchise en base stays at 37 500 € (N-1) with a 41 250 € tolerance for services.
findings.detail: This is the single most consequential piece of good news in the file. At 37 500 € he can sell shape (a) to French individuals with no VAT at all. Crossing the majoré threshold makes him liable to VAT from the first day of the overrun, not from the following year.
findings.source_quote: La proposition issue de la loi de finances pour 2025 visant à instaurer un seuil unique de franchise en base de TVA de 25 000 € a été abandonnée.

findings.claim: Every invoice under the franchise must carry the exact mention "TVA non applicable, art. 293 B du code général des impôts" — and showing any VAT amount makes him liable for it.
findings.detail: Alongside the standard mentions: invoice date, unique chronological number, date of the service, his identity and SIREN, the client's identity, the designation and unit price HT, the total, the due date, late-payment penalty rate, and the 40 € recovery indemnity for professional clients.
findings.source_quote: TVA non applicable, art. 293 B du code général des impôts

findings.claim: From 1 September 2027 micro-entreprises must ISSUE electronic invoices — which is exactly when he plans to start selling.
findings.detail: All businesses, whatever their size, must be able to RECEIVE electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance falls on large and intermediate companies from that date and on PME and micro-entreprises from 1 September 2027. He will therefore never know the paper-invoice world: shapes (b) and (c) need an approved platform from the first invoice. For public buyers such as a lycée, Chorus Pro stays available as one of the accepted routes from September 2026.
findings.source_quote: À compter du 1er septembre 2027, l'obligation d'émission des factures sous format électronique...sera obligatoire pour les petites et moyennes entreprises ainsi que pour les micro-entreprises

findings.claim: CFE is waived in the creation year only if form 1447-C-SD is filed before 31 December, and is waived permanently while revenue stays at or below 5 000 €.
findings.detail: Year two gets a 50 % base reduction. The minimum base for revenue at or below 10 000 € is 250 € to 597 €; the CFE actually owed is that base times the commune's rate, so the cash figure is set locally and is not knowable in advance. Payment is due by 15 December. The 5 000 € exemption means a small first paid year may cost nothing at all.
findings.cost_eur: 0 in year 1; 0 while revenue ≤ 5 000 €; thereafter a commune-set amount on a 250–597 € base
findings.source_quote: n'a pas dépassé 5 000 €

findings.claim: A dedicated bank account only becomes mandatory above 10 000 € of revenue for two consecutive years, and it need not be a paid "compte professionnel".
findings.detail: A second personal account, kept separate, satisfies the rule. This removes what is often assumed to be a fixed monthly cost of starting — there is none at his scale.
findings.source_quote: L'ouverture d'un compte bancaire dédié à l'activité professionnelle est obligatoire dès lors que son chiffre d'affaires (ou ses recettes) dépasse le seuil de 10 000 € pendant 2 années consécutives.

findings.claim: Accounting is a livre des recettes kept chronologically, plus a registre des achats, with supporting documents held for 10 years.
findings.detail: Each entry records the amount, the client's identity, the payment method and the reference of the supporting document. Sales under 76 € to individuals may be recorded in a daily total. No accountant is needed at this scale.
findings.source_quote: for 10 years from the closure of the accounting period

ordered_steps: STEP 0 — Settle whether the offer is BIC prestation de services or BNC (weeks before filing, decided once). It is declared on the creation form and it is 4,4 points of revenue forever. A learning path sold as teaching or as a licence of his own work reads BNC; a packaged product can read BIC services. This is the one question worth putting to a professional, and the cheapest route is the free appointment at the CCI or CMA.
STEP 1 — Pick the start date: the FIRST day of a civil quarter (1 October 2027, or 1 January 2028). Same paperwork, up to three extra months of ACRE. Zero cost, zero delay, decided in one minute.

STEP 2 — Create the micro-entreprise at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Free, online, one sitting. Needs identity, numéro de sécurité sociale, the business address, the activity, and the choice of monthly or quarterly declaration. The SIRET and the RNE inscription follow — days to a few weeks; treat it as up to a month and do not promise a customer an invoice before it lands.

STEP 3 — Request ACRE from URSSAF within 60 days of the start of activity. Hard deadline, no recovery, worth 6,4 points of revenue for up to a year. URSSAF answers within 30 days and silence is acceptance.

STEP 4 — Decide the versement libératoire within 3 months of creation — but check FIRST whether the household's revenu fiscal de référence for N-2 is under the ceiling for its number of parts (29 579 € per part; 73 947,50 € for a couple with one child). Read it off his parents' avis d'imposition before deciding. If the household is above it, the option does not exist and the arithmetic of rattachement changes.

STEP 5 — File form 1447-C-SD before 31 December of the creation year. This is what actually secures the year-one CFE exemption. It is a separate filing from the creation and it is the most commonly missed step in the sequence.

STEP 6 — Open a separate bank account. Not legally required below 10 000 € for two consecutive years, and a second personal account is enough — but do it at creation so the livre des recettes reconciles against something.

STEP 7 — Rewrite the mentions légales on copius.fr the day the first paid offer goes live. Article 1-1 II of the LCEN stops covering him the moment he publishes à titre professionnel: the site must then carry his own identity, address, and SIRET. Decide beforehand whether that address is the family home in the Loire or a domiciliation, because after publication the choice has already been made for him.

STEP 8 — Issue the first invoice with every mandatory mention plus, verbatim, "TVA non applicable, art. 293 B du code général des impôts". Never show a VAT amount — doing so makes him liable for it on that invoice alone.
STEP 9 — Open the livre des recettes on day one and keep it chronologically; keep supporting documents 10 years.
STEP 10 — Declare revenue to URSSAF on the chosen cadence. The first declaration cannot be filed until at least 90 days after the start, and zero-revenue periods are still declared.

STEP 11 — For any B2B or public-sector customer invoiced from 1 September 2027, route the invoice through an approved platform (or Chorus Pro for a lycée or CFA). Choose the platform before the first B2B sale, not after it.
unknowns: Whether revenue taxed under the versement libératoire appears in the REVENU BRUT GLOBAL that the CROUS uses for the bourse, or only in the revenu fiscal de référence. The mechanism (separate taxation plus a taux effectif computation) suggests it stays out of the revenu brut global, which would make the option a genuine shield for his bourse — but no source I opened states it. This is the single highest-value open question in the file and it is answerable by one written question to the CROUS de Lyon.

How the CAF assesses a micro-entrepreneur's income against the 55 % SMIC "enfant à charge" ceiling. The service-public page describes the six-month averaging used for salaried students and is silent on travailleurs indépendants. Ask the CAF de la Loire in writing before the first paid month.

All 2027 figures. Cotisation rates, the micro thresholds, the versement libératoire ceilings and the ACRE rate are published for 2026 only. The BNC rate moved 24,6 → 25,6 % for 2026 and the ACRE exoneration moved 50 → 25 % inside the same year; both are live legislative subjects. Every number here must be re-read before he files.

Whether a BTS student enrolled in a lycée hôtelier can access a PEPITE and therefore the statut national étudiant-entrepreneur. The statute requires the bac and enrolment in recognised higher education, which a BTS is; the practical gate is whether his lycée sits inside the académie's PEPITE convention. One email answers it.

How B2C sales are handled under the 2027 electronic-invoicing reform. Sales to individuals fall under e-reporting of transaction data rather than invoice transmission, but I could not open a page stating what a micro-entrepreneur in franchise en base must actually do. This matters for shape (a), which is the most likely shape.

VAT on digital products sold to consumers in other EU member states. Electronically supplied services to EU consumers are taxed where the consumer is, subject to a 10 000 € EU-wide threshold, and the EU SME cross-border franchise scheme opened in 2025 — none of which I verified against a source in this pass. The brief flagged "some elsewhere in the EU" for shape (a), so this needs its own look before any EU sale.

Whether an association could employ Gabriel as a salarié rather than remunerate him as a dirigeant. The ¾-SMIC ceiling applies to dirigeants de droit ou de fait; if he founded and effectively runs the association, paying him as an employee is likely to be treated as remunerating a dirigeant de fait. I did not open a source on this specific point and would not rely on the distinction.

research.lane: LANE 2 — Mentions légales and the address, once professional
research.bottom_line: There is no lawful way to sell online in France without a postal address being publicly readable — but nothing forces that address to be his family's home. Both the e-commerce identification duty and the consumer pre-contractual duty demand the address where the trader is established, with no exemption for micro-sellers, students or purely digital goods. The achievable outcome is "my home is not the published address", and the instrument is a domiciliation contract chosen BEFORE the INPI formality, at roughly 11-25 EUR HT/month in 2026 (2027 prices not published). Two corrections to earlier assumptions: article 19 LCEN is not expiring on 1 January 2027 — an ordonnance recodifying VAT merely swaps its VAT cross-reference that day, and the substance is untouched; and the August 2025 decree that lets company directors hide their personal address at the RCS explicitly does not cover entrepreneurs individuels. The free INSEE non-diffusion request is real and worth filing, but it only cleans the Sirene-fed directories — it does not clean the RNE, and it never removes the address he must publish himself in his own mentions légales.

findings.claim: Once he publishes 'à titre professionnel', LCEN article 1-1 I 1° requires his name, first names, DOMICILE and telephone number, plus his registration number if he is registered at the RCS or at the RNE as an artisan.
findings.detail: This is the post-SREN renumbering: the identification list that used to sit in article 6 III now sits in article 1-1, in force since 23 May 2024. The word the statute uses for a personne physique is 'domicile' — not 'adresse de l'établissement', which is the wording used elsewhere in the same law. He must also publish the publication director's name and the hosting provider's identity. Version en vigueur depuis le 23/05/2024, modifiée par la loi n° 2024-449 du 21 mai 2024 (SREN).
findings.when: Version in force since 23 May 2024; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: S'il s'agit de personnes physiques, leurs nom, prénoms, domicile et numéro de téléphone et, si elles sont assujetties aux formalités d'inscription au registre du commerce et des sociétés ou au registre national des entreprises en tant qu'entreprise du secteur des métiers et de l'artisanat, le numéro de leur inscription

findings.claim: Article 1-1 II — the anonymity shelter he uses today — is drafted for 'les personnes éditant à titre NON professionnel', so it stops applying to him the day the site becomes professional.
findings.detail: The text lets a non-professional publisher show only the hosting provider's name and address, provided the publisher has given the host their personal identification details; the host is then bound by professional secrecy under articles 226-13 and 226-14 of the penal code, except against the judicial authority. Nothing in the paragraph offers a partial or transitional version for a site that is mostly free with one paid tier — the qualifier attaches to the publisher, not to the page.
findings.when: Version in force since 23 May 2024; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: Les personnes éditant à titre non professionnel un service de communication au public en ligne peuvent ne tenir à la disposition du public, pour préserver leur anonymat, que le nom, la dénomination ou la raison sociale et l'adresse du fournisseur de services d'hébergement, sous réserve d'avoir communiqué à ce fournisseur les éléments d'identification personnelle mentionnés au I du présent article.

findings.claim: 'Domicile' in article 1-1 is not defined by the LCEN, and I found no text or case law saying a declared business or domiciliation address discharges it for a personne physique. This is the single genuine gap in the chain.
findings.detail: The contrast inside the same statute is what makes it a real question: article 19, which governs him as an online seller, says 'l'adresse où elle est établie', and the Consumer Code decree says 'l'adresse géographique où le professionnel est établi' — both establishment-based. Article 1-1 says 'domicile'. The practical reading everyone applies is that a professional's published address is the address he declared for the business, and no enforcement action to the contrary surfaced in this research; but I am reporting an absence of contrary evidence, not a source that settles it. This is the one point worth a paid hour of a French lawyer's time before the first sale.
findings.source_quote: L'adresse où elle est établie, son adresse de courrier électronique, ainsi que des coordonnées téléphoniques permettant d'entrer effectivement en contact avec elle

findings.claim: The penalty service-public attaches to missing mentions légales is one year's imprisonment and a 75 000 EUR fine.
findings.detail: Cited on the service-public fiche covering an entrepreneur individuel's website obligations, which also lists what he must show: name, first name and address with the mention 'entrepreneur individuel' or 'EI', RCS number, email and telephone, VAT number, and the host's name, address and telephone. I did not open the sanctions article of the LCEN itself (article 1-2 post-SREN), so the figure rests on the government fiche rather than on the statute. Fiche vérifiée le 31 juillet 2023.
findings.source_quote: votre nom, prénom et adresse. Si vous êtes entrepreneur individuel (y compris, micro-entrepreneur), vos nom et prénom sont accompagnés de la mention entrepreneur individuel ou des initiales EI.

findings.claim: The earlier review's alarm was a false positive. Article 19 LCEN is NOT being repealed on 1 January 2027 — it gets a new version that day, created by article 43 of an ordonnance that recodifies VAT.
findings.detail: Légifrance does show 'Version en vigueur jusqu'au 01 janvier 2027' on the current text, which is what the previous pass saw, but an end date on Légifrance marks the start of the next version as often as an abrogation. Fetching the article at a March 2027 date returns a live article, headed 'Version en vigueur à partir du 01/01/2027' and 'Modifié par Ordonnance n°2025-1247 du 17 décembre 2025 - art. 43'. That ordonnance is titled 'portant recodification de la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée et diverses modifications du code des impositions sur les biens et services', and its article 43 sits in its 'Chapitre III : Modifications de dispositions non codifiées'.
findings.when: Ordonnance of 17 December 2025, JORF 20 December 2025; article 19 version applies from 1 January 2027; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: Modifié par Ordonnance n°2025-1247 du 17 décembre 2025 - art. 43

findings.claim: The only thing that changes in article 19 on 1 January 2027 is the VAT cross-reference in point 4°: article 286 ter of the CGI becomes article L. 215-27 of the code des impositions sur les biens et services. The address duty in point 2° is word-for-word identical before and after.
findings.detail: I compared the two versions point by point. Point 2° reads the same in the pre-2027 and post-2027 text. Point 4° is the one that moves, and it moves only because VAT was recodified into a new Livre II of the CIBS. Practical consequence for him: the compliance checklist he writes in 2027 is the same checklist he would have written in 2026, and he should simply cite the CIBS article rather than the CGI article once he is VAT-registered — which, on a micro-entreprise under the franchise en base, he may not be at all.
findings.when: Comparison of the version in force since 1 July 2016 against the version in force from 1 January 2027; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: Si elle est assujettie à la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée et identifiée par un numéro individuel en application de l'article L. 215-27 du code des impositions sur les biens et services, son numéro individuel d'identification

findings.claim: What article 19 makes an online seller publish, in easy, direct and permanent access: identity, the address where he is established, email and a working phone, his registration number and siège social if registered, and his VAT number if assujetti.
findings.detail: The four points read: 1° for a personne physique, 'ses nom et prénoms'; 2° 'L'adresse où elle est établie, son adresse de courrier électronique, ainsi que des coordonnées téléphoniques permettant d'entrer effectivement en contact avec elle'; 3° the RCS or répertoire des métiers registration number, capital and siège social address where applicable; 4° the individual VAT number where applicable. The article also requires prices to be stated unambiguously including whether taxes and delivery are included, and enforcement is handed to the DGCCRF.
findings.when: Version in force 1 July 2016 to 1 January 2027; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: Toute personne qui exerce l'activité définie à l'article 14 est tenue d'assurer à ceux à qui est destinée la fourniture

findings.claim: Even if article 19 disappeared entirely, the address duty would survive untouched in the Consumer Code, which requires 'l'adresse géographique où le professionnel est établi' before any distance contract.
findings.detail: The pre-contractual duty sits in article L221-5, in force since 19 June 2026, which requires 'Les informations relatives à son identité, à ses coordonnées postales, téléphoniques et électroniques' and hands the detailed list to a décret en Conseil d'État. That décret is article R221-2, in force since 28 May 2022, whose point 1° carries the geographic-address wording and whose point 3° adds the siège commercial address when it differs from the first. This is why the '1 January 2027' scare never mattered: the duty is double-sourced.
findings.when: L221-5 in force since 19 June 2026; R221-2 in force since 28 May 2022; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: Son nom ou sa dénomination sociale, l'adresse géographique où le professionnel est établi, son numéro de téléphone

findings.claim: At the INPI guichet unique he declares two distinct things: the address of the business (where the activity is carried on) and his own identity and personal address — and he must upload a justificatif de jouissance des locaux for the business address.
findings.detail: The business address may differ from where he lives; the accepted proofs are a lease, a contrat de mise à disposition, a sublease, a domiciliation contract, an electricity bill or a rent receipt. Where the declarant is merely housed by someone, the file needs an attestation d'hébergement signed by the person holding the lease or title, plus a proof of address less than three months old in that person's name. The guichet unique now locks the fields for data already held and not published, such as date of birth and personal address.
findings.when: Service-public fiche verified 2 July 2026; Bpifrance page updated January 2026; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: Les entrepreneurs individuels... peuvent domicilier leur entreprise chez eux si aucune disposition contractuelle ou législative ne s'y oppose

findings.claim: What becomes PUBLIC in the RNE is everything filed, free and in electronic form — except that for a natural person the identity and domicile data published are capped at name, name in use, pseudonym, first names, MONTH and YEAR of birth, and COMMUNE of residence.
findings.detail: That cap is the governing sentence for his privacy question at the RNE, and it is statutory, not a policy INPI could change. His exact home address and his day of birth are therefore outside the public RNE view; his commune is inside it. What the cap does NOT cover is the address declared as the business address, which is company information rather than 'identité et domicile d'une personne physique' — so if he declares the family home as the business address, that address is filed as company data. Code de commerce article L123-52, version en vigueur depuis le 03/05/2025.
findings.when: Version in force since 3 May 2025; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: La mise à disposition des informations inscrites relatives à l'identité et au domicile des personnes physiques mentionnées dans le registre est limitée aux nom, nom d'usage, pseudonyme, prénoms, mois, année de naissance et commune de résidence.

findings.claim: INPI states as policy that the RNE does not diffuse the personal addresses of company representatives, which is consistent with the statutory cap.
findings.detail: The same INPI page describes the confidentiality levers available inside a formality — a tickbox 'Je demande que ce document ne soit pas diffusé publiquement', a 'dépôt d'acte à substituer', and a request to occult addresses at the RCS without filing acts — each requiring a justificatif de confidentialité on a downloadable model. The page cites the August 2025 decree as its basis, which is the decree that does not cover entrepreneurs individuels.
findings.source_quote: le RNE ne diffuse pas les adresses personnelles des représentants d'entreprises

findings.claim: The INSEE non-diffusion request is free, made online through FranceConnect, and takes effect in 48 hours for an entreprise individuelle.
findings.detail: For an entreprise individuelle it makes non-diffusible the 'nom, prénoms, pseudonyme, enseigne et nom commercial', the exact address within the commune, and the geolocation variables; for a personne morale it only hides the exact address. The legal basis given is articles R123-222, R123-223, R123-232 and R123-232-1 of the code de commerce together with article 21 of the GDPR — that is, it is exercised as a right of opposition, which is why INSEE frames it as available where the personal address doubles as the professional one. Page dated 02/12/2025.
findings.when: INSEE page dated 2 December 2025; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: Articles R123-222, R123-223, R123-232 et R123-232-1 du Code de commerce

findings.claim: What non-diffusion actually hides, in the words of the state's own company directory: the entrepreneur's identity, his address within the commune, and his geolocation. What stays public: main activity, legal category, headcount bracket, administrative status.
findings.detail: Since the July 2022 RNE decree, a non-diffusible company is no longer wholly invisible — the shell of the business stays readable and only the person-linked fields are masked. The change is made with INSEE and then propagates automatically: 'Une fois votre demande envoyée, la mise à jour est faite dans le répertoire Sirene, qui alimente directement les informations publiées sur l'Annuaire des Entreprises et tous les sites qui réutilisent les données de l'Insee.' That propagation is the real value — it reaches the scraper sites in one move.
findings.when: Décret n° 2022-1014 du 19 juillet 2022; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: l'identité de l'entrepreneur (nom, prénoms…), son adresse dans la commune et sa géolocalisation

findings.claim: What non-diffusion does NOT do: it does not bind the RNE/INPI or Infogreffe, and it does not remove the address he is separately obliged to publish himself in his own mentions légales.
findings.detail: A written question to the government put exactly this complaint — that entrepreneurs individuels can obtain non-diffusion at Sirene while 'le RNE et Infogreffe persistent à diffuser l'ensemble de ces données'. The government's answer did not deny it: it described a general review underway and said the situation of entrepreneurs individuels would be taken into account in that work. So as of this research the gap is acknowledged and unfixed. Separately, and more importantly for him, no register-side measure touches his own website: the LCEN and Consumer Code duties are duties to publish, which he discharges himself.
findings.when: Assemblée nationale written question 12588, 17th legislature; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: les entrepreneurs Individuels peuvent demander la non-diffusion de leur adresse de domicile / siège social et de leurs date / lieu de naissance sur le répertoire SIRENE

findings.claim: The August 2025 decree that finally let people hide their personal address at the RCS covers directors and indefinitely-liable partners of LEGAL ENTITIES only. Entrepreneurs individuels are excluded.
findings.detail: The decree's own 'Objet' notice names its beneficiaries as 'les personnes physiques dirigeantes et associés indéfiniment responsables de personnes morales figurant au registre du commerce et des sociétés'. It creates articles R. 123-54-1 and R. 123-54-2 and amends R. 123-3 of the code de commerce, and entered into force the day after publication, so 24 August 2025. Even for those it covers, only the personal address is occulted — the professional address stays visible. This is the finding that kills the tempting plan of registering as an EI at home and hiding the address afterwards.
findings.when: Décret n° 2025-840 du 22 août 2025, in force 24 August 2025; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: ce décret vise à rendre possible, à leur demande et via le guichet unique, l'occultation des adresses personnelles des personnes physiques dirigeantes et associés indéfiniment responsables de personnes morales figurant au registre du commerce et des sociétés

findings.claim: The government's own announcement of that decree states the exclusion in plain terms: entrepreneurs individuels are not covered.
findings.detail: The service-public actualité, published 27 August 2025, lists the beneficiaries as legal representatives of companies and indefinitely-liable partners of SNC and sociétés civiles, and notes that for natural persons in the RNE only the commune of residence is published. Authorities, judicial officers, tax and police services keep access to the occulted addresses.
findings.source_quote: seule la commune de résidence fait l'objet d'une publication

findings.claim: Yes — an entrepreneur individuel, micro-entrepreneur included, can buy a commercial domiciliation. The provider must hold a prefectoral agrément and the contract runs a minimum of three months.
findings.detail: The government fiche sets out three routes — the personal home, a société de domiciliation, or dedicated commercial premises — and its conditions for the home route are the ones that matter here: he must be 'propriétaire ou locataire de votre logement' and the home must be his résidence principale, with no lease clause, copropriété rule or planning rule against it. Légal refs given: code de commerce L123-10 à L123-11-8 and R123-167 à R123-171, and code de la construction et de l'habitation L631-7-3. Fiche vérifiée le 02 juillet 2026.
findings.source_quote: propriétaire ou locataire de votre logement

findings.claim: His personal situation fails the home-domiciliation test as stated: living with family, he is neither owner nor tenant, so the home route needs an attestation d'hébergement from the parent who holds the lease or title — and the address that then goes public is his parents'.
findings.detail: The registration file for someone who is housed requires that attestation plus a proof of address less than three months old in the host's name. Two consequences he should weigh before choosing convenience: the address exposed is not only his but his family's, and it is his parents' consent that is being documented in a public-facing filing. This is the point where the free option stops being free in the sense that matters.
findings.when: Bpifrance page updated January 2026; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: vous fournirez une attestation d'hébergement signée de votre concubin

findings.claim: Domiciliation pricing, 2026, from a provider's own published grid: 20 EUR/month with no commitment, falling to 14 EUR/month on a three-year commitment, with promotional rates of 16 and 11 EUR respectively.
findings.detail: The intermediate tiers are 18 EUR/month on one year and 16 EUR/month on two years, promotional 14 and 13. Mail handling is extra: 2,50 EUR per item à la carte, +10 EUR/month for monthly forwarding up to 25 items, +40 EUR/month for daily forwarding up to 150. No deposit or guarantee is taken at subscription. The grid is not tiered by legal form, so a micro-entreprise pays the same as an SASU. Article dated 8 July 2026. Treat as a vendor's marketing page, not a neutral source, and note it does not state HT or TTC on every line.
findings.cost_eur: 11-20 per month, plus 0-40 per month for mail
findings.when: Provider article dated 8 July 2026; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: 20€/mois

findings.claim: A second provider puts the market band at 10 to 70 EUR HT per month for a plain domiciliation, with an observed average of 25 EUR HT and its own entry price at 19 EUR/month.
findings.detail: Same three-month minimum engagement, renewable, with mail and parcel reception included in the base fee and a 1 EUR/month introductory offer for the first three months. Taking the two vendor grids together, the honest planning number for a plain address with light mail handling is 11 to 25 EUR HT per month, so roughly 130 to 300 EUR a year. Against a 10-19 EUR digital product that is ten to twenty-five sales a year consumed by the address alone — a real input to the pricing decision, not a footnote. Article updated 18 March 2026.
findings.when: Provider article updated 18 March 2026; read 15 September 2026
findings.source_quote: Une simple prestation de domiciliation coûte entre 10 € et 70 € HT par mois

findings.claim: A domiciliation satisfies the RNE declaration cleanly — the domiciliation contract is on the accepted list of justificatifs de jouissance des locaux — and it supplies the establishment address that article 19 and the Consumer Code decree ask him to publish.
findings.detail: The two duties are therefore discharged by one purchase, which is the practical answer to the question. The reservation is the one already flagged: article 1-1 I 1° says 'domicile' where the selling-specific texts say 'établi', and I found nothing official confirming that a domiciliation address discharges the article 1-1 wording for a personne physique. Nothing suggests the contrary either, and the same address is what the state itself holds as his business address.
findings.source_quote: contrat de domiciliation

findings.claim: No — there is no lawful route to selling online in France with no postal address publicly readable anywhere.
findings.detail: Two independent texts demand a geographic address and neither carves out small sellers, students, digital-only goods or low turnover: the e-commerce identification duty requires 'l'adresse où elle est établie', and the consumer pre-contractual decree requires 'l'adresse géographique où le professionnel est établi' before any distance contract, with the DGCCRF as enforcer. What IS available is control over WHICH address: a domiciliation address is a lawful establishment address, it is what he declares to the state, and it is what he publishes. The realistic goal is that his family's address never enters the chain, not that no address exists.
findings.source_quote: L'adresse où elle est établie

ordered_steps: Nothing changes before June 2027. The free site keeps its article 1-1 II shelter as long as he publishes à titre non professionnel, and the E5 practical is the priority. This lane is a decision packet for late 2027, not a task list for now.

When commercialisation is actually decided, choose the business address BEFORE opening the INPI formality. This is the one irreversible-by-default step: the August 2025 decree does not let an entrepreneur individuel hide a home address filed at the RCS/RNE afterwards, so the address chosen at registration is the address he lives with.

Sign a domiciliation contract with a prefecture-approved provider, minimum three months, budgeting 11-25 EUR HT per month plus mail handling. Keep the contract — it is the justificatif de jouissance des locaux the guichet unique requires.

Run the INPI guichet unique creation with the domiciliation address as the adresse de l'entreprise. His personal address and full date of birth stay outside the public RNE view by statute; only his commune of residence is published.

Immediately after immatriculation, file the free INSEE statut-de-diffusion request via FranceConnect. It takes effect in 48 hours and propagates to the Annuaire des Entreprises and every site that reuses INSEE data. File it even with a domiciliation in place — it costs nothing and closes the Sirene-fed surface.

Write the mentions légales with: name and first names followed by 'EI', the domiciliation address, a working telephone, an email, the SIREN, and the host's name, address and telephone. Add the VAT number only if actually assujetti — on a micro-entreprise under the franchise en base he may have none.
Before the first sale, add the Consumer Code pre-contractual block and the CGV. The geographic address appears there too, under R221-2, independently of the LCEN.

Get a French lawyer's written line on one narrow question before the first sale: whether publishing the domiciliation address discharges LCEN article 1-1 I 1°, which says 'domicile' for a personne physique. Everything else in this lane is settled by text I read; this is the only link resting on inference.

After 1 January 2027, update the VAT citation in any compliance note from article 286 ter du CGI to article L. 215-27 du code des impositions sur les biens et services. That is the whole of the 2027 change.
unknowns: Whether publishing a domiciliation address discharges LCEN article 1-1 I 1°, which uses the word 'domicile' for a personne physique where articles 19 and R221-2 use 'établi'. No statute, decree, guidance or case law found either way. This is the load-bearing uncertainty in the lane.

Whether the RNE publishes an entrepreneur individuel's establishment address when that address IS his home. The statutory cap in L123-52 covers 'identité et domicile des personnes physiques'; INPI says it does not diffuse personal addresses; a deputy's written question asserts the RNE still diffuses them. Not resolved, and the government's answer described a review rather than a rule.

Whether a boîte postale or a poste-restante address can serve as 'l'adresse géographique où le professionnel est établi'. Not researched in this pass; the wording 'géographique' suggests not, but I did not verify it.

2027 domiciliation prices. Not published. Both vendor grids read are 2026 figures, dated March and July 2026, and both are marketing pages rather than neutral sources; several lines do not state whether the price is HT or TTC.

Whether domiciliation providers will contract with a client who has no SIRET yet, and what identity documents they require from an 18-year-old with no trading history. Presumed routine — creation is the normal use case — but not verified.

The exact sanctions text for missing mentions légales post-SREN. The one year and 75 000 EUR figure comes from a service-public fiche verified 31 July 2023, not from article 1-2 of the LCEN, which I did not open.

Whether an appel à projets or a public établissement buyer (the lycée/CFA licence shape) imposes any additional publication or identification duty beyond these. Out of scope for this lane and not examined.

research.bottom_line: For the shapes Gabriel is planning, TVA is a near-non-event at the start and becomes real at three named tripwires. Under the franchise en base he charges no VAT and writes one sentence on his invoices ("TVA non applicable, article 293 B du CGI"). The thresholds in force are 37 500 € (CA of year N-1) and 41 250 € (CA in-year) for prestations de services — and his digital sales AND his restaurant consulting count together against that same line, because both are services. The contested single threshold of 25 000 € is ABANDONED, not suspended: article 1 of loi n° 2025-1044 du 3 novembre 2025 deleted it, and the tax administration's own doctrine re-published on 1 July 2026 reflects the deletion. The PLF 2026 tried to revive a variant (37 500 € general, 25 000 € for travaux immobiliers); it does not appear in the doctrine of 1 July 2026, and a BTP-specific threshold would not touch him anyway. Nothing is published for 2027 as of 2026-09-15. The three tripwires: (1) 41 250 € in-year — VAT starts the very day he crosses it, mid-invoice; (2) 10 000 € of sales to consumers in other EU countries, cumulated across all of them — above that, the buyer's country's VAT applies and the French franchise no longer shelters him, so he needs the OSS guichet unique or the new franchise en base européenne (EX number, 100 000 € EU ceiling); (3) 1 September 2027 — the date TPE/PME must ISSUE electronic invoices, which lands exactly on his commercialisation window, and applies to him even though he is franchisé. The single biggest lever: selling through a true merchant of record moves the VAT problem off his desk entirely. Paddle states in its own help centre that it is the reseller and "seller on record" and pays the VAT instead of him; Stripe's own docs say the opposite for ordinary Stripe (marchand officiel = "Votre entreprise") unless he uses Stripe Managed Payments, where the table says marchand officiel = "Stripe". For a lycée, none of the teaching exonérations fit a licence, so it is 20% once he is above the threshold — and a public buyer means Chorus Pro. Nothing here changes because he is a student, 18, or in his parents' foyer fiscal: VAT thresholds attach to the business, not the household.

findings.claim: Franchise en base, prestations de services: 37 500 € (CA de l'année N-1) and 41 250 € (seuil majoré, CA de l'année en cours). For livraisons de biens: 85 000 € / 93 500 €.
findings.detail: These are the figures in force for 2026, confirmed twice over: in the tax administration's own doctrine (BOFiP) re-published 1 July 2026, and on service-public verified 1 January 2026. Gabriel's two paid shapes — the digital learning path and the restaurant consulting — are BOTH prestations de services, so they add up against the same 37 500 € line. There is no separate allowance per activity. The figures are set by article 293 B du CGI.
findings.source_quote: Prestations de services (excluding food/lodging sales): Previous year limit: « 37 500 € » — In-year limit: « 41 250 € »
findings.when: BOFiP document dated 01/07/2026; service-public F21746 « Vérifié le 01 janvier 2026 »
findings.cost_eur: 0 (no VAT collected or paid while under the franchise)

findings.claim: Two different things happen depending on WHICH threshold is crossed: cross 37 500 € → VAT from 1 January of the following year; cross 41 250 € → VAT from the very first day of the overrun.
findings.detail: This is the rule that bites hardest in practice. Crossing the base threshold (37 500 €) is gentle: he finishes the year without VAT and becomes redevable on 1 January following. Crossing the majoré threshold (41 250 €) is brutal: the franchise stops on the day of the overrun, the invoice that crosses it must carry VAT, and he must obtain a VAT number and start filing immediately. So a single large December invoice can flip his regime mid-month. BOFiP puts it as VAT becoming due « à compter de la date à laquelle intervient ce dépassement ».
findings.source_quote: When base threshold exceeded: VAT applies « dès le 1er janvier de l'année suivante ». When tolerance threshold exceeded: VAT applies « dès le 1er jour du dépassement ».
findings.when: Page « Vérifié le 01 janvier 2026 »; BOFiP BOI-TVA-DECLA-40-10-10 dated 01/07/2026

findings.claim: The 25 000 € single threshold is DEFINITIVELY ABANDONED — not suspended, not in force. It was deleted by article 1 of loi n° 2025-1044 du 3 novembre 2025.
findings.detail: This is the contested reform the brief asks about, and the answer is unambiguous. Sequence: the loi de finances pour 2025 created a single 25 000 € franchise threshold for all activities, due to apply from 1 March 2025; the government suspended it in February 2025 after an outcry from professional federations; then a dedicated law — loi n° 2025-1044 du 3 novembre 2025 « visant à garantir un cadre fiscal stable, juste et lisible pour nos micro-entrepreneurs et nos petites entreprises » — suppressed the measure outright. Service-public states the policy is permanently abandoned rather than temporarily suspended. The decisive corroboration is dated: BOFiP's actualité of 1 July 2026 says the doctrine on the domestic franchise was adjusted to take account of the modifications made to article 293 B du CGI by article 1 of that law. So the abrogation is reflected in the administration's live doctrine nine months into 2026, not merely announced.
findings.source_quote: « La proposition issue de la loi de finances pour 2025 visant à instaurer un seuil unique de franchise en base de TVA de 25 000 € a été abandonnée. »
findings.when: Law promulgated 03/11/2025; service-public news item published 05/11/2025; BOFiP ACTU-2025-00144 dated 01/07/2026

findings.claim: The PLF 2026 tried to revive a variant (37 500 € general / 25 000 € for travaux immobiliers). It is absent from the tax doctrine published 1 July 2026, so it was not enacted — and a BTP-specific threshold would not affect Gabriel in any case.
findings.detail: Bpifrance Création reported on 15 October 2025 that the draft 2026 budget announced 37 500 € generally and 25 000 € for prestations de travaux immobiliers, with majorés at 41 250 € and 27 500 €. The control for whether it passed is the BOFiP text of 1 July 2026: it lists only 85 000/93 500 and 37 500/41 250, with no travaux-immobiliers category. Service-public, verified 1 January 2026, likewise says the 2026 thresholds « restent inchangés ». I did not open the enacted loi de finances pour 2026 itself (Légifrance refuses automated fetches), so I am reporting this as inference from official doctrine rather than from the statute — but it is the correct inference, and the point is moot for a culinary learning path either way.
findings.source_quote: « a threshold of basic VAT exemption at 37,500 € and at 25,000 € for real estate work services » (PLF 2026 as announced)
findings.when: Bpifrance article 15/10/2025; checked against BOFiP doctrine dated 01/07/2026

findings.claim: Nothing is published for 2027. As of 2026-09-15 no PLF 2027 figures exist in any official source I could reach.
findings.detail: A projet de loi de finances is normally presented at the very end of September or early October, so the 2027 text is due within weeks of this research but is not out. This matters because his commercialisation window is late 2027: the honest planning assumption is 37 500 € / 41 250 €, re-verified in November or December of whichever year he actually starts selling. A remembered number from this report will be a year stale by then.
findings.source_quote: The search results don't contain specific information about the PLF 2027 thresholds.

findings.claim: First year of activity: the turnover is annualised, not the threshold. CA × (days in the year) ÷ (days from start to 31 December).
findings.detail: If he starts selling in, say, October 2027, his real CA is scaled up to a full-year equivalent to test eligibility for 2028. A strong two-month launch can therefore produce an annualised figure above 37 500 € and cost him the franchise for the following year even though he never actually collected that much. Worth modelling before choosing a launch date.
findings.source_quote: « (CA x nombre de jours dans une année ) / nombre de jours entre le démarrage et le dernier jour de l'année »

findings.claim: Invoice under the franchise: the mandatory sentence is « TVA non applicable, article 293 B du code général des impôts », and he must show NO VAT anywhere on the document.
findings.detail: The obligation comes from article 293 E du CGI. BOFiP is explicit on both halves: beneficiaries of the franchise cannot make VAT appear on invoices, and they can deduct no VAT on their own purchases. The trap is mechanical and expensive: if he puts a VAT amount on an invoice by mistake, he owes that VAT to the Treasury by the mere fact of having invoiced it — and his customer cannot deduct it. So a template error on a 15 € learning path, repeated across hundreds of sales, creates a real liability with no offsetting deduction.
findings.source_quote: « Les bénéficiaires de la franchise ne peuvent faire apparaître la TVA sur les factures » (§53); « L'assujetti relevant de la franchise mais qui indique un montant de TVA sur une facture devient redevable du seul fait de cette facturation » (§53)
findings.cost_eur: 0 VAT owed if done right; the wrongly-stated VAT becomes payable in full if done wrong

findings.claim: The 293 B sentence is an ADDITION to the ordinary mandatory invoice mentions, not a replacement for them.
findings.detail: Service-public's invoice page, verified 7 August 2026, lists what every invoice must carry regardless of VAT status: his name preceded or followed by « Entrepreneur individuel » or « EI », SIREN, address, a unique sequential invoice number, the issue date and the date the service was performed, the precise designation and quantity, the unit price HT, the totals, the payment due date, the escompte conditions (or « Escompte pour paiement anticipé : néant »), and for business customers the late-payment penalty rate plus the « Indemnité forfaitaire de 40 € » recovery fee. The buyer's VAT identification number is required except on invoices under 150 € HT — which is why his 10-19 € consumer sales escape that particular line but his lycée licence will not.
findings.source_quote: « TVA non applicable, art. 293 B du code général des impôts »; « Indemnité forfaitaire de 40 € »
findings.cost_eur: 40 € indemnité forfaitaire de recouvrement, stated on B2B invoices

findings.claim: Being under the franchise does NOT exempt him from the electronic-invoicing reform. Receiving became compulsory for everyone on 1 September 2026; issuing plus e-reporting hits TPE/PME/micro on 1 September 2027.
findings.detail: This is the finding with the sharpest date collision: 1 September 2027 is precisely his commercialisation window. The administration's FAQ states that a franchisé en base is an assujetti — non-redevable, but an assujetti — and is therefore bound by the obligations to issue and receive electronic invoices and to transmit data to the administration. Practically: before he issues his first paid invoice in late 2027 he must already have chosen an approved platform (plateforme agréée). This is a setup task with a deadline, not a tax to pay.
findings.source_quote: « À compter du 1er septembre 2026, toutes les entreprises » must be able to receive; small and micro-enterprises face the emission and transmission requirements from 1 September 2027. For franchisés: « you are subject in your capacity as an assujetti, even non-redevable, to the obligations of emission and reception of electronic invoices »

findings.claim: Digital product sold to a consumer in another EU country: VAT is due in the CONSUMER's country, under article 259 D du CGI — but only once he passes 10 000 € of such sales EU-wide.
findings.detail: A downloadable or access-based learning path is a « service fourni par voie électronique »; BOFiP's examples include software supply, online database access, downloads and distance education services. Below the 10 000 € threshold the place of supply stays France, French rules apply, and the franchise covers him — so he charges nothing. The threshold is a single EU-wide total across ALL other Member States combined, not per country, and it must not have been exceeded in the current calendar year OR the preceding one. The transaction that crosses it is already located in the customer's Member State — the shift is not deferred to the next sale. At 10-19 € per sale that is roughly 550-1 000 EU-foreign sales before the problem exists; he can also opt in from the first euro if he prefers.
findings.source_quote: « le seuil de 10 000 € ne doit pas avoir été dépassé au cours de l'année civile en cours ainsi qu'au cours de l'année civile précédente. Lorsque le montant d'une prestation a pour conséquence le franchissement de ce seuil, le lieu de cette prestation est situé dans l'État membre où réside la personne non assujettie. »
findings.when: BOFiP doctrine; corroborated by impots.gouv.fr « Suis-je concerné ? » updated 22/03/2024
findings.cost_eur: 0 below 10 000 €; above it, the destination country's rate (roughly 17-27% across the EU)

findings.claim: The OSS guichet unique is a single French registration, from his impots.gouv.fr espace professionnel, that lets him declare and pay every other Member State's VAT in one return.
findings.detail: It exists precisely so a one-person business does not have to register for VAT in 26 countries. impots.gouv.fr describes it as covering services supplied to non-taxable persons in a Member State where the provider is not established, and says registration is made through the espace professionnel, after which he declares and pays the VAT due in the other EU countries « dans une seule et même déclaration ». It is open to all assujettis « quel que soit leur régime d'imposition à la TVA ». Note what OSS does NOT do: it does not exempt him, it centralises the paperwork. He still charges each country's rate.
findings.source_quote: « tous les assujettis, quel que soit leur régime d'imposition à la TVA »; « un seuil de 10 000 € a été instauré, en deçà duquel la TVA sur les prestations de services et les ventes à distance intracommunautaire de biens, reste due dans l'État membre d'établissement du prestataire. »
findings.when: OSS page updated 23/04/2025; « Suis-je concerné » updated 22/03/2024

findings.claim: There is a second, better option he should know about: the franchise en base de TVA européenne, live since 1 January 2025 — stay exempt in other EU countries instead of charging their VAT.
findings.detail: Rather than collecting foreign VAT through OSS, a French small business can claim the EXEMPTION in other Member States. Conditions, from the impots.gouv.fr page updated 23 April 2026: EU-wide annual turnover ≤ 100 000 € in years N and N-1; turnover in each target Member State below that State's own franchise threshold; not registered in the OSS non-Union or IOSS schemes. He subscribes to the « Franchise en base TVA UE » service in his espace professionnel and receives an exemption number (the EX number). The ongoing cost is a quarterly declaration of turnover per Member State, due the month after each quarter ends, and a 15-day notification if the 100 000 € ceiling is breached. For a 10-19 € product this is almost certainly the right route over OSS — it keeps the price VAT-free everywhere rather than making him juggle 27 rates.
findings.source_quote: « Avoir un chiffre d'affaires annuel dans l'Union inférieur ou égal à 100 000 € en année N et N-1 »; « déclarer votre chiffre d'affaires trimestriel réalisé dans chaque État membre de l'UE »
findings.when: Page modified 23/04/2026; scheme in force since 01/01/2025
findings.cost_eur: 0 VAT; cost is one declaration per quarter

findings.claim: Same product sold to a consumer OUTSIDE the EU: no French VAT. Article 259 B du CGI places the service outside France when the non-taxable customer is established or resident outside the EU.
findings.detail: BOFiP's list of services covered by article 259 B includes « services fournis par voie électronique ». So a sale to a consumer in the United States, Switzerland, the UK or Canada carries no French VAT, whether or not he is under the franchise, and whether or not he has passed any threshold. The open question is the other direction: those countries may want him registered under THEIR rules (UK VAT on digital services has no registration threshold for non-established sellers, several US states tax digital goods, Norway and Switzerland have their own regimes). I did not verify any non-EU country's rules in this research and they are outside the French sources the brief scopes me to. This is exactly the exposure a merchant of record removes.
findings.source_quote: « le lieu de certaines prestations est réputé ne pas se situer en France lorsqu'elles sont fournies à une personne non assujettie qui n'est pas établie ou n'a pas sa résidence habituelle dans un État membre »

findings.claim: Stripe, in its standard form, does NOT change who owes the VAT. Stripe's own docs table names the marchand officiel as « Votre entreprise ».
findings.detail: This is the cleanest available answer and it comes from Stripe's own documentation, not a comparison blog. The docs compare Managed Payments against other Stripe products in a table whose first row is « Marchand officiel »: Managed Payments = Stripe, Autres produits Stripe = Votre entreprise. Stripe Tax only calculates; the filing page states plainly that HE must declare and remit in every jurisdiction where he is registered, and that Stripe's automated filing is US-only or via third-party partners at extra cost. So ordinary Stripe Checkout or Payment Links leaves the entire EU VAT question — the 10 000 € threshold, OSS, foreign rates — sitting on his desk.
findings.source_quote: « Marchand officiel | Managed Payments: Stripe | Autres produits Stripe: Votre entreprise »; « Vous devez déclarer et verser les taxes que vous collectez pour chaque juridiction dans laquelle vous êtes enregistré. »

findings.claim: Stripe Managed Payments is a merchant-of-record product: Stripe becomes the marchand officiel and handles VAT/GST/sales tax in 80+ countries.
findings.detail: This is a distinct Stripe product from ordinary Stripe, and it is aimed exactly at his case — the docs open by describing selling digital products worldwide with Stripe as marchand officiel handling tax, fraud, disputes and support. Constraints to check before counting on it: it supports Checkout and Payment Links but not Elements, advanced integrations, or Connect. Worth pricing against Paddle when the time comes.
findings.source_quote: « Vendez des produits numériques dans le monde entier avec la solution de marchand officiel de Stripe pour la gestion des taxes, de la fraude, des litiges et de l'assistance. »

findings.claim: Paddle IS a merchant of record and says so in its own help centre: it is the reseller and « seller on record », and pays the VAT instead of him.
findings.detail: Opened on paddle.com's own help pages, not a third-party comparison. The consequence in French VAT terms is structural, not cosmetic: if Paddle is the reseller, his supply is to Paddle — a business — and the sale to the EU consumer is Paddle's sale, not his. The 10 000 € threshold, OSS and the 27 national rates then never enter his accounts at all. That is why the platform choice deserves to be made deliberately rather than by default.
findings.source_quote: « Paddle acts as a reseller of your product, and is, therefore, the 'seller on record'. »; « Paddle will be responsible for the collection and payment of VAT and tax instead of you. »

findings.claim: Lemon Squeezy and Gumroad are both described as merchants of record, but I could NOT open either company's own page to confirm it — and there is a live contradiction about Gumroad's current EU VAT handling.
findings.detail: docs.lemonsqueezy.com returned 403 and gumroad.com's help articles returned only page titles to the fetcher, twice each, on different URLs. So this rests on search-index snippets, which the brief correctly refuses to treat as sources. The contradiction worth flagging: one 2026 comparison article asserts Gumroad no longer handles EU VAT for most creators and that registering via OSS is the seller's job, while a snippet of Gumroad's own help centre says Gumroad acts as Merchant of Record for all sales and remits worldwide. Both cannot be true. Since the whole point of choosing an MoR is to make the EU VAT question disappear, he must confirm this in writing from the platform before relying on it — and note that Lemon Squeezy is Stripe-owned, so its status may have moved.
findings.source_quote: Not verifiable: docs.lemonsqueezy.com returned HTTP 403; gumroad.com help articles returned title only.

findings.claim: Selling a licence to a lycée: while he is under the franchise, nothing changes — no VAT, the 293 B mention, done. Above the threshold it is 20%, because none of the teaching exonérations fit a licence.
findings.detail: Two exonérations look tempting and neither works. The « leçons particulières » exemption of article 261, 4, 4°-b requires lessons « dispensés personnellement par des personnes physiques qui perçoivent, directement de leurs élèves, la rémunération », and BOFiP adds that teaching with the help of employees loses it — a licence bought by an établissement fails on both counts, since the payer is the school and nothing is dispensed personally. The distance-learning exemption attaches to établissements d'enseignement à distance, which he is not. The formation professionnelle continue exemption is a different business shape entirely: it requires a déclaration d'activité as an organisme de formation under article L. 6351-1 du code du travail and an attestation from the DREETS obtained on form 3511-SD. Service-public, verified 20 July 2026, confirms non-exempt teaching sits at the 20% standard rate.
findings.source_quote: « cours ou leçons particuliers dispensés personnellement par des personnes physiques qui perçoivent, directement de leurs élèves, la rémunération »; « Les personnes qui enseignent avec le concours de salariés doivent être soumises au paiement de la TVA »
findings.when: BOFiP version 16/10/2019; service-public F32231 « Vérifié le 20 juillet 2026 »
findings.cost_eur: 0 while franchisé; 20% of the licence price once above the threshold

findings.claim: A lycée is a public buyer, so the invoice goes through Chorus Pro — an obligation that has applied to suppliers of the public sector of every size since 1 January 2020.
findings.detail: This is not a VAT rule but it is the practical blocker on getting paid by an établissement: an invoice sent by email or PDF to the school will not be processed. From September 2026 suppliers to the public sphere may transmit either via Chorus Pro or via an approved platform, with some exceptions (marchés de travaux, mémoires de frais de justice) that remain Chorus Pro specific. Combined with the 1 September 2027 e-invoicing obligation, the conclusion is the same from both directions: by the time he invoices a lycée he needs a proper invoicing channel, not a word processor.
findings.source_quote: Since 1 January 2020, dematerialized invoicing has been mandatory for all public sector suppliers; from September 2026, suppliers may use an approved platform or Chorus Pro.
findings.when: Search-index summary of impots.gouv.fr and economie.gouv.fr pages, 2026-09-15; the specific pages were not opened

findings.claim: Nothing in the VAT rules changes because he is a student, because he turned 18 recently, or because he is in his parents' foyer fiscal.
findings.detail: Explicitly answering the brief's instruction to say where a rule differs: here, it does not. The franchise thresholds attach to the assujetti — the business — not to the household, and the foyer fiscal is an income-tax concept with no VAT effect. Two real consequences follow instead. First, being 18 and therefore majeur is what makes creating a micro-entreprise possible at all without emancipation. Second, because the threshold is per person, every paid activity he runs under the same SIRET aggregates: the learning path plus the restaurant consulting share one 37 500 € ceiling, and the free site and newsletter contribute nothing because they generate no turnover.
findings.source_quote: Thresholds are set by activity type under article 293 B du CGI, assessed on the chiffre d'affaires of the assujetti; no student, age or foyer-fiscal derogation appears in the doctrine.
