ordered_steps: Do nothing on VAT before June 2027 — this is already decided and the research confirms there is no early filing, registration or declaration that needs to exist before he has a first paying customer.
When he registers the micro-entreprise (late 2027), the franchise en base applies automatically. No option to exercise, no form to file. He simply must not charge VAT.

Put « TVA non applicable, article 293 B du code général des impôts » on every invoice from the first one, and make certain no VAT amount, rate or line appears anywhere on the document — a stated VAT becomes payable by the mere fact of having written it.

Before issuing that first invoice, choose an approved e-invoicing platform (plateforme agréée). The obligation to ISSUE electronically hits TPE/PME on 1 September 2027 and applies to him despite the franchise; this is a setup deadline, not a tax.

Keep one running total of services turnover — digital sales AND consulting together — against 37 500 € and 41 250 €, and watch it before signing any single large invoice, because crossing 41 250 € makes VAT due the same day.
Keep a SECOND, separate total of sales to consumers in other EU countries against 10 000 € cumulated EU-wide. Below it, nothing to do. Approaching it, act before the sale that crosses it, not after.

When that EU total starts to look reachable, compare the two routes deliberately: the franchise en base de TVA européenne (EX number, 100 000 € EU ceiling, quarterly declaration, stays VAT-free) against the OSS guichet unique (charges each country's rate, one return). For a 10-19 € product the European franchise is the more likely fit.

Decide the sales channel as a VAT decision, not just a fees decision. A genuine merchant of record — Paddle states it is the reseller and seller on record; Stripe Managed Payments names Stripe as marchand officiel — removes EU and non-EU VAT from his accounts entirely. Ordinary Stripe leaves all of it with him.

Before relying on Lemon Squeezy or Gumroad as merchant of record, get that confirmed in writing from the platform. Neither company's own page could be opened in this research, and the secondary reports on Gumroad's current EU VAT handling contradict each other.

For a lycée or CFA: invoice without VAT while franchisé, and expect to route the invoice through Chorus Pro rather than email. If he ever passes the threshold, the licence is 20% — do not assume a teaching exonération, because none of them fit a licence sold to an établissement.

Re-verify every figure in this report in November or December of the year he actually starts selling. The PLF 2027 was not published as of 15 September 2026, and thresholds are exactly the kind of number that moves in a budget.
unknowns: The contents of the PLF 2027 — not published as of 2026-09-15. Any 2027 threshold figure quoted to him before roughly October 2026 is speculation.

Whether the loi de finances pour 2026 as enacted left article 293 B untouched. Inferred from BOFiP doctrine dated 01/07/2026 showing only 37 500/41 250 and 85 000/93 500, and from service-public verified 01/01/2026; the statute itself could not be opened because Légifrance refuses automated fetches.
Whether a triennial revalorisation of the 37 500 € / 41 250 € figures is scheduled for the 2026-2028 window. Not found in the sources opened; do not assume the numbers are frozen to 2027.

Lemon Squeezy's and Gumroad's CURRENT merchant-of-record and EU VAT position. docs.lemonsqueezy.com returned 403 and Gumroad's help articles returned title-only, on repeated attempts. Secondary sources contradict each other on whether Gumroad still remits EU VAT for creators.

Whether selling through a merchant of record established abroad triggers a déclaration européenne de services (DES) obligation for him, since his own supply would then be B2B to that platform. Not researched; needs checking before a platform is chosen.

Whether the platform's commission, as a service received from a supplier established abroad, obliges him to self-assess French VAT (autoliquidation) and file a CA3 even while under the franchise. This is a known trap for franchisés buying foreign services and it was not verified here.

Whether an access-based learning path could ever qualify for the 5.5% livre numérique rate rather than 20%. Not researched; the safe planning assumption is 20%, and it only matters above the threshold.

Non-EU registration duties — UK VAT on digital services, US state-level sales tax, Norway, Switzerland. Out of scope of the French sources the brief scopes me to, and a real exposure that a merchant of record would absorb.
Whether article 259 C du CGI (use and enjoyment) could pull any of these services back into French VAT. BOFiP referenced the article only in a table footnote and did not detail it.

research.lane: LANE 4 — Consumer law for a digital product sold at a distance (France/EU), for copius.fr from ~late 2027
research.bottom_line: Nothing here blocks the plan, and all of it is cheap — the whole consumer-law layer costs about 30 EUR (a mediator subscription) plus one careful checkout page. Two things are genuinely load-bearing. First, the digital-content waiver (C. consom. art. L221-28, 13°) is all-or-nothing: three cumulative conditions plus a durable-medium confirmation kept as proof, and if any one is missing the buyer can withdraw for 14 days, keep the file, and owe nothing (art. L221-26). Second, the pictogram wording. "Original hand-drawn illustration" beside a price is a false statement about the mode de fabrication of the very thing being paid for; because it would be published online, art. L132-2 puts it in the 5-years / 750 000 EUR tier and art. L132-4 makes publication of any conviction mandatory, not optional. The evidence is served by his own site — anyone can read the SVG. Today the site is free and non-professional, so L121-2 does not bite; the day a price appears next to that sentence, it does. Selling to a lycée removes the consumer layer entirely (no rétractation, no médiateur, no L221-5) but NOT the misleading-practice exposure, which art. L121-5 extends to practices aimed at professionals and non-professionals; it swaps in public-procurement and Chorus Pro rules instead. One item is newer than most published advice: since 19 June 2026 an online "fonctionnalité de rétractation" button is mandatory for distance contracts concluded through an online interface (art. L221-21, art. D221-5) — though a properly waived instant-delivery product has no withdrawal right and so needs no button. And the EU ODR platform died on 20 July 2025: the boilerplate ODR link still found in most CGV templates now points at nothing.

findings.claim: (a) The pre-contractual list is art. L221-5 C. consom., 11 numbered items, fleshed out by art. R221-2 (15 further items). Most templates miss items 6°, 7°, 10° and 11°.
findings.detail: L221-5 I requires, before any sale of a bien/service/contenu numérique/service numérique: 1° essential characteristics; 2° price; 3° date or delay of delivery/supply; 4° identity, postal, telephone AND electronic contact details, termination terms, dispute-resolution modes, other contractual terms, cost of the distance technique, codes of conduct, financial guarantees; 5° legal guarantees, functionalities, compatibility and interoperability of the digital content plus any software-installation restriction; 6° the possibility of recourse to a consumer mediator; 7° where a withdrawal right exists, its conditions, period, modalities, the model withdrawal form AND (new) the existence and location of the withdrawal functionality of art. L221-21; 8° return costs; 9° charges payable if the consumer asks for early execution of a service; 10° WHERE THE WITHDRAWAL RIGHT CANNOT BE EXERCISED under L221-28, the information that the consumer does not have it, or the circumstances in which he loses it; 11° application of a personalised price based on automated decision-making. R221-2 adds, among others, the geographic address of establishment, an address for complaints, payment/delivery/execution modalities, complaint-handling modalities, the legal guarantee of conformity and hidden-defects regime, contract duration and termination, technical protection measures on the digital content, and 11° the contact details of the competent consumer mediator(s). L221-11 requires all of it to be given legibly and comprehensibly or made available by a means adapted to the distance technique; L221-12 sets the reduced core list where the medium is space-constrained.
findings.source_quote: « 10° Lorsque le droit de rétractation ne peut être exercé en application de l'article L. 221-28, l'information selon laquelle le consommateur ne bénéficie pas de ce droit ou, le cas échéant, les circonstances dans lesquelles il le perd ; 11° L'application d'un prix personnalisé sur la base d'une prise de décision automatisée, s'il y a lieu. »
findings.when: Code edition 2026-09-12, last modified 2026-08-20; L221-5 in its version from Ordonnance n°2026-2 du 5 janvier 2026, art. 2

findings.claim: (a) Breach of the L221-5 information list on a distance contract is an administrative fine of 15 000 EUR for a personne physique — five times the 3 000 EUR figure most blog posts quote, which is the in-store regime.
findings.detail: Two distinct sanction articles. Art. L131-1 covers failures on the general pre-contractual duty of art. L111-1: max 3 000 EUR (personne physique) / 15 000 EUR (personne morale). Art. L242-10 covers failures on the distance/off-premises articles L221-5, L221-6, L221-8, L221-11 to L221-14: max 15 000 EUR / 75 000 EUR. Selling online, he is squarely in L242-10. Art. L242-11 adds the same 15 000/75 000 for failing the durable-medium contract confirmation of L221-13. As an entrepreneur individuel he is a personne physique, so 15 000 EUR is his ceiling per manquement.
findings.source_quote: « Tout manquement aux obligations d'information prévues aux articles L. 221-5, L. 221-6, L. 221-8, L. 221-11, L. 221-12 à L. 221-14 est passible d'une amende administrative dont le montant ne peut excéder 15 000 euros pour une personne physique et 75 000 euros pour une personne morale. »
findings.when: Art. L242-10, version from Ordonnance n°2021-1734 du 22 décembre 2021, art. 9; code edition 2026-09-12

findings.claim: (a) The day he publishes 'à titre professionnel', the mentions légales must carry his name, first names and address, his SIREN, his VAT number, his phone and email, and his host's identity. Omitting them is a criminal offence: 1 year and 75 000 EUR for an entreprise individuelle.
findings.detail: This is the practical consequence of the LCEN art. 1-1 II lapse the brief already flags. The official e-commerce fiche lists, for an entreprise individuelle: name, first names and address; the unique identification number (Siren); email and telephone; VAT identification number; and the host's name or company name, address and telephone. For an 18-year-old living with his family in the Loire, 'adresse' means the declared business address — which, absent a domiciliation arrangement, is the family home, published on a site with ~3 700 indexed pages. That is a decision to take deliberately before the switch, not after.
findings.source_quote: « Le manquement à cette obligation d'information est puni d'1 an d'emprisonnement et 75 000 € d'amende pour les entreprises individuelles (dont micro-entrepreneur). »
findings.when: Page 'Faire du commerce en ligne (e-commerce) : règles à respecter', vérifié le 19 juin 2026

findings.claim: (b) 14 days, and for a service or digital content the clock starts at CONCLUSION of the contract, not at delivery.
findings.detail: Art. L221-18: fourteen days, no reason to give, no cost beyond arts. L221-23 to L221-25. The starting point is split: 1° the day the contract is concluded, for service contracts and those of art. L221-4; 2° receipt of the goods, for sales of goods. A downloadable learning path is in the first branch. Separately, art. L221-20 (not quoted here) extends the period by twelve months where the 7° information was never given — the extension rule referenced at L221-5 7°.
findings.source_quote: « Le consommateur dispose d'un délai de quatorze jours pour exercer son droit de rétractation d'un contrat conclu à distance, à la suite d'un démarchage téléphonique ou hors établissement, sans avoir à motiver sa décision ni à supporter d'autres coûts que ceux prévus aux articles L. 221-23 à L. 221-25. »

findings.claim: (b) THE EXACT WAIVER CONDITIONS — art. L221-28, 13°. Three cumulative conditions, all required, plus a fourth obligation on the seller under L221-13 al. 2.
findings.detail: The exception applies to 'la fourniture d'un contenu numérique sans support matériel dont l'exécution a commencé avant la fin du délai de rétractation et, si le contrat soumet le consommateur à une obligation de payer'. What the consumer must expressly do: (a) give prior express consent that execution begin before the withdrawal period expires; and (b) acknowledge that he WILL LOSE his right of withdrawal. What the seller must do and keep: (c) provide confirmation of the consumer's agreement under the second paragraph of art. L221-13 — that is, furnish the consumer, on a durable medium, in the same conditions and BEFORE the withdrawal period expires, confirmation of both his express agreement and his acknowledgment of the loss of the right. Concretely that means two separate unticked checkboxes at checkout, not one, plus an automatic order-confirmation email that repeats both statements — and an archived copy of that email, since art. L221-26 puts the burden of proof on him. 'Support durable' is defined at the liminary article 8° as an instrument allowing the consumer to store information addressed to him personally, refer back to it, and reproduce it unchanged: an email is fine, a page on his site is not.
findings.source_quote: « 13° De fourniture d'un contenu numérique sans support matériel dont l'exécution a commencé avant la fin du délai de rétractation et, si le contrat soumet le consommateur à une obligation de payer, lorsque : a) Il a donné préalablement son consentement exprès pour que l'exécution du contrat commence avant l'expiration du délai de rétractation ; et b) Il a reconnu qu'il perdra son droit de rétractation ; et c) Le professionnel a fourni une confirmation de l'accord du consommateur conformément aux dispositions du deuxième l'alinéa de l'article L. 221-13. »
findings.when: Art. L221-28, version from Ordonnance n°2021-1734 du 22 décembre 2021, art. 6; code edition 2026-09-12

findings.claim: (b) If the waiver is botched, the downside is total: the buyer withdraws within 14 days, keeps the downloaded content, and owes nothing. Art. L221-26.
findings.detail: Art. L221-26 says a consumer who withdraws from a contract for digital content without a material medium owes NO sum at all if either (1) the seller did not collect his prior express agreement plus proof that he acknowledged losing the right of withdrawal, or (2) the contract does not carry the mentions of L221-9 al. 3 and L221-13 al. 2. There is no pro-rata, unlike art. L221-25 for services. The counterweight is art. L221-27 V, which obliges a withdrawing consumer to stop using the content and not make it available to third parties — enforceable in theory, worthless in practice for a PDF. So the checkout wording is the entire defence.
findings.source_quote: « Le consommateur qui a exercé son droit de rétractation d'un contrat de fourniture de contenu numérique sans support matériel n'est redevable d'aucune somme si : 1° Le professionnel n'a pas recueilli son accord préalable exprès pour l'exécution du contrat avant la fin du délai de rétractation ainsi que la preuve que le consommateur a reconnu perdre son droit de rétractation […] »

findings.claim: (b) NEW and mostly unpublished in the guides he will find: since 19 June 2026 an online withdrawal button is mandatory for distance contracts concluded through an online interface. It does not apply to a product with a valid waiver.
findings.detail: Ordonnance n°2026-2 du 5 janvier 2026 (art. 3) added a third paragraph to art. L221-21: for distance contracts concluded via an online interface the professional must provide, free of charge, a functionality letting the consumer exercise his withdrawal right. Décret n°2026-3 du 5 janvier 2026 created art. D221-5, which prescribes the label ('renoncer au contrat ici' or an unambiguous equivalent), permanent visibility throughout the withdrawal period, the fields the declaration must let the consumer fill (name and first name, details identifying the contract, the electronic means for the acknowledgment), a confirmation control labelled 'confirmer la rétractation', and an acknowledgment of receipt sent on paper or another durable medium stating the content of the declaration and the date and time it was sent. Its origin is the EU financial-services distance-marketing directive, but France placed it in the general provisions so it covers all consumer distance contracts. The reason it probably does not touch shape (a): art. L221-5 7° requires disclosing the functionality only 'lorsque le droit de rétractation existe', and with a valid L221-28 13° waiver it does not. Breach is 15 000 / 75 000 EUR under art. L242-13.
findings.source_quote: « Pour l'application du dernier alinéa de l'article L. 221-21, la fonctionnalité de rétractation est identifiée, de manière lisible, par les mots " renoncer au contrat ici " ou par une formule analogue dénuée d'ambiguïté. » — art. D221-5. And: « À compter du 19 juin 2026, tout professionnel qui conclut des contrats à distance avec des consommateurs au moyen d'une interface en ligne devra mettre à leur disposition une fonction de rétractation dédiée »
findings.when: Art. L221-21 and D221-5, in force 19 June 2026; confirming commentary: Élodie Kalfon, Village de la Justice, 18 June 2026 (https://www.village-justice.com/articles/fonction-retractation-ligne-entre-vigueur-juin-2026-que-change-ordonnance-2026,57910.html)
findings.cost_eur: up to 15 000 EUR administrative fine (art. L242-13)

findings.claim: (c) CGV are not a code-mandated document, but the information they carry is mandatory and must reach the buyer BEFORE the contract. In practice the CGV is the only sane vehicle.
findings.detail: Nothing in the Code de la consommation says 'you must have CGV'. Arts. L221-5, L221-11, R221-2 say the information must be provided legibly and comprehensibly before conclusion; art. 1127-1 C. civ. says whoever offers goods or services professionally by electronic means must make the applicable contractual stipulations available in a way permitting their storage and reproduction. The official fiche states the seller has the obligation to furnish CGV to a consumer before the contract is concluded, that they may be given by any means on a durable medium, and that for a professional buyer they are not mandatory but must be communicated on request. Content required for a distance B2C contract, per the same fiche: essential characteristics, price, delivery date or delay, the professional's identification (SIREN, legal form, contact details), legal guarantees, access to consumer mediation, the existence of a 14-day withdrawal right and its modalities, withdrawal costs, contract duration and termination, and dispute-resolution modes.
findings.source_quote: « Le vendeur a l'obligation de fournir les CGV avant la conclusion du contrat » ; les CGV « peuvent être indiquées par tout moyen sur un support durable ».
findings.when: Fiche 'Conditions générales de vente (CGV)', vérifié le 1er juillet 2026

findings.claim: (c) YES — active acceptance is required, and it is art. 1119 of the Code civil that requires it, not the consumer code. A footer link alone does not bind the buyer.
findings.detail: Art. 1119 al. 1: general conditions relied on by one party have effect against the other only if they were brought to that party's knowledge AND that party accepted them. Two consequences. Knowledge: a link in the footer is not 'portées à la connaissance' — the checkout must present them at the point of order. Acceptance: it must be a positive act, i.e. an unticked box the buyer ticks. A pre-ticked box is not acceptance, and where it would add a payment art. L121-17 makes default consent refundable on demand, with a 3 000 / 15 000 EUR administrative fine under art. L132-22. Art. 1119 al. 3 also settles a practical point: where CGV and conditions particulières conflict, the particulières win. Unfair-terms control applies on top: art. L212-1 strikes clauses creating a significant imbalance in B2C contracts, art. L212-2 extends it to contracts with non-professionnels, and art. 1171 C. civ. does the same for any non-negotiable clause in a contrat d'adhésion.
findings.source_quote: « Les conditions générales invoquées par une partie n'ont effet à l'égard de l'autre que si elles ont été portées à la connaissance de celle-ci et si elle les a acceptées. »
findings.when: Art. 1119 C. civ.; Code civil edition 2026-09-12, last modified 2026-07-29

findings.claim: (d) The double-clic is two separate rules, and the second one — the button wording — is sanctioned by NULLITY of the contract, not a fine.
findings.detail: Rule one, art. 1127-2 al. 1 C. civ.: the contract is validly concluded only if the offeree was able to check the detail of his order and its total price and to correct errors before confirming it — a recap screen, then a confirmation. Al. 2 adds that the offeror must acknowledge receipt of the order electronically without unjustified delay. Rule two, art. L221-14 al. 2 C. consom.: the function used to validate the order must carry the clear and legible mention 'commande avec obligation de paiement' or an unambiguous analogous formula. Al. 1 requires a reminder of essential characteristics, price, contract duration and any minimum commitment immediately before ordering; al. 3 requires accepted payment means and any delivery restrictions to be shown clearly at the latest at the start of the order process. Sanction: art. L242-2 makes the second paragraph of L221-14 'prévu à peine de nullité du contrat conclu par voie électronique' — a buyer can unwind the sale outright. The 15 000 EUR administrative fine of L242-10 sits on top. Note art. 1127-3: these obligations may be derogated from in contracts between professionals, which matters for the lycée route.
findings.source_quote: « Le professionnel veille à ce que le consommateur, lors de sa commande, reconnaisse explicitement son obligation de paiement. A cette fin, la fonction utilisée par le consommateur pour valider sa commande comporte la mention claire et lisible : commande avec obligation de paiement ou une formule analogue, dénuée de toute ambiguïté […] » ; « Les dispositions du deuxième alinéa de l'article L. 221-14 sont prévues à peine de nullité du contrat conclu par voie électronique. »
findings.when: Arts. L221-14 and L242-2; code edition 2026-09-12
findings.cost_eur: nullity of the contract + up to 15 000 EUR

findings.claim: (e) What counts under art. L121-2: a practice is misleading when it rests on false or misleading claims about, among other things, the essential characteristics of the good — expressly including its 'qualités substantielles' and its 'mode et date de fabrication'.
findings.detail: Art. L121-2 2° b) lists the essential characteristics as 'ses qualités substantielles, sa composition, ses accessoires, son origine […] sa quantité, son mode et sa date de fabrication, les conditions de son utilisation et son aptitude à l'usage, ses propriétés et les résultats attendus de son utilisation'. Point e) adds 'la portée des engagements de l'annonceur […] la nature, le procédé ou le motif de la vente'. Art. L121-3 makes omission of substantial information equally misleading and deems substantial, in any invitation to purchase quoting a price, the main characteristics, the professional's address and identity, the all-taxes price, and the existence of a withdrawal right. Art. L121-1 frames the whole: a practice is unfair when contrary to professional diligence and capable of substantially altering the economic behaviour of a normally informed, reasonably attentive consumer. Art. L121-4 lists 26 practices deemed misleading in all circumstances; none covers handcrafting claims, so the pictogram question is decided under L121-2 on the facts.
findings.source_quote: « 2° Lorsqu'elle repose sur des allégations, indications ou présentations fausses ou de nature à induire en erreur et portant sur l'un ou plusieurs des éléments suivants : […] b) Les caractéristiques essentielles du bien ou du service, à savoir : ses qualités substantielles, sa composition […] son mode et sa date de fabrication […] »
findings.when: Art. L121-2, version from Ordonnance n°2021-1734 du 22 décembre 2021, art. 3; code edition 2026-09-12

findings.claim: (e) The penalty is a criminal offence, and because the sale would happen online the tier is 5 years and 750 000 EUR — not the 2 years / 300 000 EUR figure quoted everywhere. Publication of the conviction is mandatory.
findings.detail: Art. L132-2: misleading practices under L121-2 to L121-4 are punished by two years' imprisonment and a 300 000 EUR fine. The fine may be raised, proportionately to the benefit drawn from the offence, to 10% of average annual turnover over the last three known financial years, or to 50% of the expenditure incurred on the advertising or practice (80% for environmental claims). Then the decisive paragraph: where the offence is committed through an online public-communication service or by digital or electronic means, the penalties rise to five years and 750 000 EUR. Art. L132-2-1 raises imprisonment to three years where contracts followed. Art. L132-3 allows a professional ban of up to five years. Art. L132-4 is not discretionary — 'le tribunal ordonne' the display or dissemination of the whole or part of the decision, and may order corrective announcements at the convicted person's expense; failing to run them is itself punished by two years and 300 000 EUR (L132-5). Before any of that, the DGCCRF can, after an adversarial procedure, enjoin compliance with a daily penalty of up to 3 000 EUR capped at 300 000 EUR (art. L521-1, as amended by LOI n°2025-594 du 30 juin 2025) and publicise the injunction at his expense (art. L521-2).
findings.source_quote: « Les pratiques commerciales trompeuses mentionnées aux articles L. 121-2 à L. 121-4 sont punies d'un emprisonnement de deux ans et d'une amende de 300 000 euros. […] Lorsque l'infraction a été commise par l'utilisation d'un service de communication au public en ligne ou par le biais d'un support numérique ou électronique, les peines sont portées à cinq ans d'emprisonnement et à 750 000 euros d'amende. »
findings.when: Art. L132-2, version from LOI n°2024-420 du 10 mai 2024, art. 11; code edition 2026-09-12
findings.cost_eur: 5 years + 750 000 EUR maximum; DGCCRF astreinte up to 3 000 EUR/day capped at 300 000 EUR

findings.claim: (e) SPECIFIC CHECK — 'original hand-drawn illustration' beside a price is a false claim about the mode de fabrication of the thing being paid for. The exposure is the aggravated online tier, and the proof is served by his own site. 'Original' survives; 'hand-drawn' does not.
findings.detail: Three separate points. (1) It bites only once there is a price. A 'pratique commerciale' is defined at the liminary article 16° as an action or communication 'de la part d'un professionnel, en relation directe avec la promotion, la vente ou la fourniture d'un bien'. A free, non-professional atlas is outside L121-2; a paid tier, or a free page promoting one, is inside. That maps exactly onto his June 2027 line. (2) The claim is not borderline. 'Hand-drawn' is a statement about the mode de fabrication, which L121-2 2° b) names in terms; 1 838 files of 654–1 118 bytes sharing a single style block are machine-generated by any reading, and 'illustration' pointing at a pictogram compounds it under 'qualités substantielles'. There is no defensible reading in which a drawing made by a generator was drawn by a hand. (3) The evidence is public and self-proving. Every SVG is fetched by the browser from his own domain; a complainant, a competitor or a DGCCRF agent needs one right-click and the file size. Unlike most misleading-practice disputes there is nothing to investigate. Aggravating the picture: the claim would appear on an online service (L132-2 al. 4, five years / 750 000 EUR), would be followed by contracts (L132-2-1, three years), and any conviction would be published by order of the court (L132-4) under his own name — the durable cost for someone building a public brand at 19. The fix is free and takes one commit: say what is true. 'Illustrations vectorielles originales', 'pictogrammes dessinés pour Copius', 'schémas originaux' all hold — 'original' is accurate, since they are his own work and not copied. Drop 'hand-drawn', 'dessiné à la main', 'fait main' and 'artisanal' everywhere, including alt text, the PWA manifest, Open Graph tags and any future press kit. If any drawing genuinely was hand-made, claim it only for those and be able to show the source file.
findings.source_quote: « 16° Pratique commerciale : toute action, omission, conduite, démarche ou communication commerciale, y compris la publicité et le marketing, de la part d'un professionnel, en relation directe avec la promotion, la vente ou la fourniture d'un bien, d'un service, ou portant sur des droits et obligations »
findings.when: Article liminaire, version from LOI n°2024-364 du 22 avril 2024, art. 2; code edition 2026-09-12
findings.cost_eur: 0 to fix; 750 000 EUR ceiling if not fixed

findings.claim: (f) YES, naming a mediator is compulsory for any seller to consumers, with no size exemption. Art. L612-1 C. consom.
findings.detail: Art. L612-1: every consumer has the right to free recourse to a consumer mediator to settle a dispute with a professional, and 'à cet effet, le professionnel garantit au consommateur le recours effectif à un dispositif de médiation de la consommation'. Guaranteeing effective recourse means being signed up in advance — it is not something to arrange when a dispute arrives. Micro-entrepreneur status changes nothing; only not being a professional does. Art. L616-1 then requires him to communicate the competent mediator's contact details, and to repeat that information whenever a dispute has not been settled through a prior complaint to him directly. Art. R616-1 fixes where: visibly and legibly on his website, on his CGV, on his order forms, or failing those by any other appropriate means — and he must also state the mediator's own website address.
findings.source_quote: « Tout consommateur a le droit de recourir gratuitement à un médiateur de la consommation en vue de la résolution amiable du litige qui l'oppose à un professionnel. A cet effet, le professionnel garantit au consommateur le recours effectif à un dispositif de médiation de la consommation. »

findings.claim: (f) Cost: free for the buyer by law, and roughly 30 EUR for three years for him at his turnover — plus about 150 EUR HT per case that actually goes to mediation.
findings.detail: The consumer pays nothing (art. L612-1, 'gratuitement'); CM2C states the same on its own site, excepting the consumer's own lawyer or expert fees. The professional pays. Verified live tariff from one CECMC-referenced body, Société de la Médiation Professionnelle: fees effective 20 April 2026 — under 60 000 EUR turnover, 25 EUR HT for three years (30 EUR TTC total); 60 000 to 999 999 EUR, turnover divided by 2 000 as both entry fee and annual subscription; per case 150 EUR HT standard, 350 EUR HT complex. Published tariffs across the ~30 referenced bodies vary widely, so this is one dated data point, not a market rate. He should compare two or three before signing and check whether the per-case fee is capped.
findings.source_quote: Grille tarifaire, tarifs applicables au 20 avril 2026 : moins de 60 000 EUR de chiffre d'affaires, « 25€ht pour 3 ans » ; médiation « 150 € HT », médiation complexe « 350 € HT ».
findings.cost_eur: ~30 EUR TTC for 3 years + ~150 EUR HT per case (one body, 2026 tariff)

findings.claim: (f) Penalty for not having one: an administrative fine of up to 3 000 EUR for a personne physique, 15 000 EUR for a personne morale. Art. L641-1.
findings.detail: Art. L641-1 sanctions any breach of the information obligations of arts. L616-1 and L616-2. Note what this does and does not cover: it punishes failing to tell the consumer who the mediator is. The DGCCRF checks it by loading the site and reading the CGV, which makes it one of the easiest breaches in the code to detect and one of the most commonly fined. The relevant sector codes in the official CECMC directory are B01 'Vente en ligne, vente à distance' and O02 'Enseignement à distance'; 21 referenced bodies cover B01 and 9 cover O02, including ANM Consommation, Avenir Conso, CM2C, FEVAD, Médiation Solution, NotreAccord and SMP. Verified against the ministry's own directory file, updated 8 September 2026.
findings.source_quote: « Tout manquement aux obligations d'information mentionnées aux articles L. 616-1 et L. 616-2 est passible d'une amende administrative dont le montant ne peut excéder 3 000 euros pour une personne physique et 15 000 euros pour une personne morale […] »
findings.when: Art. L641-1; code edition 2026-09-12. Directory: https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/annuaire-des-mediateurs-de-la-consommation-1, updated 2026-09-08

findings.claim: (f) Do NOT copy the ODR-platform link from any CGV template. The European ODR platform was shut down on 20 July 2025, even though art. L616-2 still refers to the regulation that created it.
findings.detail: The Commission's own page states the platform is discontinued as of 20 July 2025, following Regulation (EU) 2024/3228; it stopped accepting new complaints on 20 March 2025. Art. L616-2 C. consom. still requires informing the consumer of steps taken to implement art. 14 of Regulation (EU) No 524/2013 — dead text France has not yet cleaned up. Practical effect: nearly every French CGV template in circulation carries a link to ec.europa.eu/consumers/odr that now goes nowhere. Publishing a dead redress route to consumers is a bad look in front of a DGCCRF agent and arguably an art. L121-3 omission. For cross-border EU buyers, the live replacement is the European Consumer Centre France plus the Commission's list of national dispute-resolution bodies.
findings.source_quote: « The European Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Platform is discontinued as of 20 July 2025 »
findings.when: European Commission, platform discontinued 20 July 2025; Regulation (EU) 2024/3228

findings.claim: (g) Selling to a lycée removes almost the entire consumer layer — a lycée is not a consumer. No 14-day withdrawal, no L221-5 regime, no mediator obligation.
findings.detail: The liminary article defines a consumer as 'toute personne physique qui agit à des fins qui n'entrent pas dans le cadre de son activité commerciale, industrielle, artisanale, libérale ou agricole'. A lycée is a personne morale, so it can never be a consumer, and every article keyed to 'consommateur' — L111-1, L221-5, L221-14, L221-18, L612-1 — drops away. The extension route does not rescue it either: art. L221-3 extends sections 2, 3 and 6 to professional-to-professional contracts only where they are concluded HORS ÉTABLISSEMENT, the object falls outside the solicited professional's main activity, and it has five employees or fewer. An online distance sale is not an off-premises contract, so the three conditions never even get tested. Practical consequence for shape (b): no waiver checkbox, no withdrawal button, no mediator line — but also no consumer-code safety net if the lycée disputes the invoice.
findings.source_quote: « 1° Consommateur : toute personne physique qui agit à des fins qui n'entrent pas dans le cadre de son activité commerciale, industrielle, artisanale, libérale ou agricole ; 2° Non-professionnel : toute personne morale qui n'agit pas à des fins professionnelles »
findings.when: Article liminaire and art. L221-3; code edition 2026-09-12

findings.claim: (g) But the misleading-practice exposure follows him into the B2B sale. Art. L121-5 extends arts. L121-2 to L121-4 to practices aimed at professionals and non-professionals.
findings.detail: One sentence decides it: 'Les dispositions des articles L. 121-2 à L. 121-4 sont également applicables aux pratiques qui visent les professionnels et les non-professionnels.' So the pictogram wording is exactly as dangerous in a licence proposal to a lycée as in a checkout page for an individual — and the 750 000 EUR online tier of L132-2 still applies if the claim sits on the website. Other survivals on the B2B route: art. L212-1 unfair-terms control, extended to non-professionnels by art. L212-2; art. 1112-1 C. civ., the general pre-contractual duty to disclose information of determining importance, which the parties may neither limit nor exclude and whose breach can void the contract; art. 1119 C. civ. on acceptance of general conditions; and art. 1171 C. civ., which strikes any non-negotiable clause creating a significant imbalance in a contrat d'adhésion. Whether an EPLE counts as a 'non-professionnel' (a personne morale not acting for professional ends) rather than a 'professionnel' is arguable and I found no case law on it — but it does not change the answer here, since L121-5 covers both categories.
findings.source_quote: « Les dispositions des articles L. 121-2 à L. 121-4 sont également applicables aux pratiques qui visent les professionnels et les non-professionnels. »
findings.when: Art. L121-5, version from LOI n°2017-203 du 21 février 2017, art. 6; code edition 2026-09-12

findings.claim: (g) What replaces consumer law: public procurement plus Chorus Pro. Below 60 000 EUR HT a lycée can buy from him with no publicity and no competitive tendering — a threshold raised from 40 000 EUR on 1 April 2026.
findings.detail: A lycée is a public buyer, so the Code de la commande publique governs. The official fiche, verified 21 August 2026, gives the low-value thresholds: supplies and services under 60 000 EUR HT, works under 100 000 EUR HT, non-school books under 90 000 EUR HT. The raise came from décret n°2025-1386 du 29 décembre 2025 and applies to consultations launched from 1 April 2026; between 1 January and 31 March 2026 the figure was still 40 000 EUR HT. A licence at any realistic price sits far under it, so a lycée may buy directly — subject to the standing duties to choose a relevant offer, make good use of public money, and not contract systematically with the same operator. Second requirement: invoicing. Electronic invoicing to the public sector has been mandatory for every company regardless of size since 2020; from September 2026 a public-sector supplier may transmit through an approved platform or through Chorus Pro. That means a SIRET is a hard precondition — a lycée's agent comptable cannot pay a natural person with no registration. Not researched here: whether a région's appel à projets is a subvention (different regime entirely) or a marché.
findings.source_quote: Marchés de faible montant : fournitures et services, « montant est inférieur à 60 000 € HT ».
findings.when: Fiche vérifiée le 21 août 2026; threshold from décret n°2025-1386 du 29 décembre 2025, applicable to consultations launched from 1 April 2026. Chorus Pro: https://www.impots.gouv.fr/actualite/chorus-pro-restera-la-plateforme-de-reference-pour-la-facturation-electronique-du-secteur (18 July 2025, modified 9 September 2025)

findings.claim: Student, age and foyer fiscal: none of this changes a line of consumer law. He is 18 and legally capable, and consumer law looks only at whether he acts professionally.
findings.detail: Three explicit checks the brief asked for. Being a BTS MHR student is irrelevant — the code keys on 'professionnel', defined at the liminary article 3° as any natural or legal person acting for purposes within a commercial, industrial, artisanal, liberal or agricultural activity; a student who sells a paid tier is a professionnel like any other. Being newly major is likewise neutral: the capacity question would only have arisen for a contract concluded while he was a minor, and he turned 18 before any sale. Remaining in his parents' foyer fiscal changes nothing in the Code de la consommation; it bites only on tax and social contributions, which is lane 3. The one place his personal situation genuinely bites is the mentions légales: art. 19 LCEN forces a personne physique to publish an address, and at 18 living with family that is his parents' home unless he arranges a domiciliation. That is a lane-1 entity decision with a lane-4 trigger.
findings.source_quote: « 3° Professionnel : toute personne physique ou morale, publique ou privée, qui agit à des fins entrant dans le cadre de son activité commerciale, industrielle, artisanale, libérale ou agricole […] »

findings.claim: Source-access note: legifrance.gouv.fr, economie.gouv.fr/DGCCRF and EUR-Lex all refused automated access. Every code article quoted above comes from the droit.org PDF mirror, which is built from the Legifrance API and which I downloaded and read in full.
findings.detail: The mirror's own header states: 'Traitements effectués à partir des données issues des APIs Legifrance et Judilibre', 'Code de la consommation — Dernière modification: 2026-08-20 — Edition : 2026-09-12, 2104 articles'. Each article also carries its source instrument (e.g. 'L. 221-28 — Ordonnance n°2021-1734 du 22 décembre 2021 - art. 6'), which is what lets the quotes be dated. economie.gouv.fr and its DGCCRF fiches returned Cloudflare 403 to every attempt, including the PDF fact sheets; EUR-Lex returned an AWS WAF challenge, so Directive 2011/83/EU and Directive (EU) 2023/2673 were not read at source — the EU-law statements above rest on the French transposition text plus the Commission's own consumer-redress page. Before acting on any figure, re-check it: this is a 2026 snapshot for a 2027 decision.
findings.source_quote: « Code de la consommation — Dernière modification: 2026-08-20 — Edition : 2026-09-12 — 2104 articles […] Traitements effectués à partir des données issues des APIs Legifrance et Judilibre. »

ordered_steps: NOW, free, one commit, no entity needed: purge 'hand-drawn' / 'dessiné à la main' / 'fait main' / 'artisanal' from the site, alt text, PWA manifest, Open Graph tags and any draft press kit. Replace with 'illustrations vectorielles originales' or 'pictogrammes dessinés pour Copius'. Doing it now, while the site is free and outside L121-2, costs nothing; doing it after a price appears is an admission.

NOW, free: decide where his published business address will be before, not after, he registers — because LCEN art. 19 will put it on 3 700 indexed pages. Options are the family home or a paid domiciliation. This is a lane-1 input, surfaced by lane 4.

At registration (~late 2027): subscribe to a CECMC-referenced mediator covering sector B01 'Vente en ligne, vente à distance' and, if the product is framed as a learning path, O02 'Enseignement à distance'. Compare two or three tariffs; one verified 2026 tariff is 25 EUR HT for three years under 60 000 EUR turnover plus ~150 EUR HT per case. Do this BEFORE the first sale — art. L612-1 requires guaranteeing recourse, not arranging it on demand.

Build the checkout as a single ordered screen, in this order: order recap with total price and an edit control (art. 1127-2 C. civ.) / the L221-14 al. 1 reminder of characteristics, price and duration / two SEPARATE unticked boxes — one for express consent to immediate execution, one for acknowledging loss of the withdrawal right (art. L221-28 13° a) and b)) / a validation button reading exactly 'Commande avec obligation de paiement' (art. L221-14 al. 2, nullity if wrong) / an automatic confirmation email repeating both acknowledgments and attaching the CGV (art. L221-13 al. 2), archived on his side as proof.

Write the CGV to carry the full art. L221-5 + R221-2 content, including the three items templates miss: 6° mediator recourse, 10° the statement that there is NO withdrawal right for instantly-delivered digital content with the reasons why, and the mediator's name plus website (art. R616-1). Present them at checkout behind a tick box, not only as a footer link — art. 1119 C. civ. requires knowledge AND acceptance.
Delete the ODR-platform link that every CGV template still carries. The platform closed on 20 July 2025. Point cross-border EU buyers at the European Consumer Centre France instead.

If and only if some product does carry a withdrawal right (a subscription, a drip-fed course, anything not fully delivered at purchase): build the art. D221-5 withdrawal functionality — a permanently visible 'renoncer au contrat ici' control, a declaration form, a 'confirmer la rétractation' confirmation, and an acknowledgment of receipt on a durable medium stating date and time. In force since 19 June 2026.

For the lycée route (shape b), build a different document set, not a trimmed consumer one: a commercial proposal with no rétractation and no mediator, an entity with a SIRET, and Chorus Pro or an approved platform for invoicing. Under 60 000 EUR HT the établissement can buy directly with no tendering. Keep the pictogram wording clean here too — art. L121-5 carries the misleading-practice rules into B2B.
unknowns: Whether an EPLE (lycée public) is legally a 'non-professionnel' under the liminary article 2° or a 'professionnel' under 3°. I found no case law and did not resolve it. It does not change the answers in (g) — L121-5 covers both and neither category gets rétractation or mediation — but it would decide whether art. L212-2 unfair-terms control applies to his licence terms.

Whether a région's appel à projets is a subvention or a marché public. Entirely different regimes (no procurement thresholds, but eligibility rules, a convention, and reporting). Not researched in this lane.

2027 figures. Every number here is a 2026 snapshot: the 60 000 EUR HT procurement threshold (raised 1 April 2026), the mediator tariffs (SMP, effective 20 April 2026), and the fine ceilings. Re-check all of them before the commercialisation decision — a remembered threshold is worse than none.

Whether the art. L221-21 withdrawal-functionality obligation could be read as applying even where no withdrawal right exists. I read art. L221-5 7° ('le cas échéant, l'existence et l'emplacement de la fonctionnalité') as confining it to cases where the right exists, and the décret is silent. The obligation is three months old and I found no administrative guidance. Medium confidence — worth one question to a mediator or a DGCCRF départemental service before launch, both of which answer for free.

Whether any French court has ruled on a 'fait main' / 'hand-made' claim under art. L121-2. I searched and found DGCCRF enforcement on 'origine France' claims but no decided handcrafting case. The textual hook ('son mode et sa date de fabrication') is explicit enough that this does not change the risk assessment.

Primary EU texts were not read at source — EUR-Lex refused automated access. Directive 2011/83/EU art. 16(m) and Directive (EU) 2023/2673 art. 11a are relied on through their French transposition and the Commission's consumer-redress page. For buyers elsewhere in the EU, the interaction of Rome I art. 6 with the fully-harmonised withdrawal exception was not verified against source and is not stated as a finding above.

research.lane: LANE 5 — Taking money, and RGPD as a seller (Stripe/MoR onboarding, registre, DPA, retention, privacy notice)
research.bottom_line: Stripe does not require a SIRET from a French individual — I pulled Stripe's own requirements endpoint for FR + individual + card_payments and the returned field list contains no `company.tax_id` and no `registration_number`, only personal identity, business_profile and a bank account. So the blocker is not Stripe, it is French law: selling repeatedly without immatriculation is "travail dissimulé par dissimulation d'activité", 3 ans / 45 000 € for a personne physique. Age is a non-issue — Stripe's Services Agreement admits 13+, requiring an adult representative only under 18, and he is already 18. The registre des traitements becomes mandatory the day he has customers, because CNIL's own text names "gestion des clients/prospects" as the example of a traitement non occasionnel that cancels the under-250-employees derogation. Retention does not actually pull in opposite directions: CNIL's commercial référentiel makes it sequential — base active for the contract's duration, then archivage intermédiaire on a different legal basis (art. 6.1.c) holding invoices the 10 years Code de commerce L123-22 demands, logically or physically separated with restricted access. The single most timeline-relevant thing I found: if he commercialises in late 2027 he lands exactly on 1 September 2027, when TPE/micro must both emit electronic invoices and e-report B2C turnover — and the e-reporting fiche names "franchise en base" as one of the régimes that merely sets the periodicity, so being under the VAT threshold does not exempt him.

findings.claim: Stripe requires no SIRET, no registration number and no tax ID from a French INDIVIDUAL account
findings.detail: I queried Stripe's own requirements endpoint with platformCountry=FR, accountCountry=FR, legalEntityType=individual, capabilities=card_payments. The complete returned field list is: business_profile.mcc, business_profile.url, business_profile.product_description, business_profile.support_phone, individual.first_name, individual.last_name, individual.address.line1/postal_code/city, individual.dob.day/month/year, individual.phone, individual.email, tos_acceptance.ip, tos_acceptance.date, external_account. No company.tax_id, no registration_number, no documents.* entry. Re-running the same query with the EU orrProgram=eu-2025 returned an identical field list. Note this is the field schema, not a promise Stripe's risk team will never ask for more at review: Stripe's KYC page says the information it must collect 'differs from country to country'. The widely repeated claim that Stripe France demands a SIRET and a professional RIB traces to commercial blogs, not to Stripe.
findings.source_quote: individual.first_name, individual.last_name, individual.address.line1, individual.dob.day, individual.email, tos_acceptance.ip, external_account

findings.claim: The real bar is French, not Stripe's: repeated selling with no immatriculation is a criminal offence
findings.detail: Service-Public Entreprendre defines dissimulation d'activité as the absence of any declaration of the activity, giving absence of immatriculation au RCS or au RNE as its own example. For a personne physique the penalty is up to 3 years' imprisonment and 45 000 €, articles L8224-1 to L8224-6 du Code du travail, aggravated to 5 ans / 75 000 € where a minor or a vulnerable person is involved. This is the answer to 'can an individual with no company use Stripe at all': the onboarding form will let him through; the activity itself is what is unlawful. A one-off, non-repeated sale is a different question I did not research.
findings.source_quote: Absence de déclaration d'une activité (par exemple : absence d'immatriculation au RCS ou au RNE)

findings.claim: Stripe's minimum age is 13, with an adult representative required only under 18 — he is clear
findings.detail: The Stripe Services Agreement served at stripe.com/fr/legal/ssa sets the floor at 13 and requires a user under 18 (or under the local age of majority) to add an adult representative, who may be a parent or legal guardian. Brazil is the only carve-out at a hard 18. Gabriel is 18 now and 19 during 2027, so he signs in his own name with no guardian involved and no French-specific age wrinkle. The 'legal_guardian' field visible in Stripe's requirement-row definitions is the mechanism behind that clause.
findings.source_quote: Only people 13 years of age or older may open a Stripe Account and use the Services and Stripe Technology.

findings.claim: Stripe's document rules are strict on form; the France-specific accepted-document row did NOT render and is unverified
findings.detail: The common requirements I did read: a direct copy of the original only (no copy of a copy), scans as PDF and photos as unprocessed JPEG/PNG, screenshots refused, colour required for photo ID, identity and legal-entity documents must not be expired, and one document cannot satisfy two requirements at once — so identity and proof of address must be two different documents. A passport is mandatory where the country of residence differs from the account country. The per-country accepted-document lists on that page are rendered client-side; both the HTML and the .md?country=FR variants returned placeholder 'Item 1/2/3' headings, so I could not read what France specifically accepts. Treat 'CNI or passport or permis de conduire' as probable but unconfirmed.
findings.source_quote: Les documents d'identité et d'entité juridique ne doivent pas être expirés

findings.claim: Stripe Identity covers French government documents and runs an anti-spoofing liveness check
findings.detail: Document checks are available for most government-issued documents — carte nationale d'identité, permis de conduire, passeport — and FR is in the supported-country list. Stripe states it uses computer vision and AI to confirm the user captured a real document rather than a stolen image or someone else's face, and warns the user in real time if the document has expired. This is the product Stripe applies to identity verification generally.
findings.source_quote: Les vérifications de document sont disponibles pour la plupart des documents émis par l'administration publique (carte nationale d'identité, permis de conduire et passeports)

findings.claim: Paddle waives business verification entirely for individuals and sole traders
findings.detail: Paddle's account verification has three legs: domain review, business verification, identity verification. The business leg — government-issued business registration documents plus a shareholder/ownership breakdown naming anyone over 25% — is explicitly not required for individuals or sole traders. The identity leg is run through Sumsub and asks for a government-issued ID plus a proof of address, with a short liveness video in some cases; typically instant, 1-3 business days on manual review. No age requirement is stated on that page. This makes Paddle the lowest-friction onboarding of the three I could open — but it does not cure the French immatriculation problem above.
findings.source_quote: Please note, this step is not required for individuals or sole traders.

findings.claim: Paddle: 5% + $0.50 per checkout transaction, and products under $10 are pushed to custom pricing
findings.detail: Paddle is merchant of record and states it provides full tax registration, filing and remittance, and total adherence to sales tax and VAT rules. The under-$10 note matters directly: his likely price point is 10-19 EUR, so the bottom of his range sits at or below Paddle's standard-pricing floor and would need a negotiated rate. On a 15 EUR sale the headline rate costs roughly 0.75 EUR + ~0.46 EUR ≈ 1.21 EUR, about 8%. No 'last updated' date is printed on the pricing page.
findings.source_quote: 5% + 50¢ per Checkout transaction
findings.when: page read 2026-09-15; no publication date shown

findings.claim: Polar: free tier 5% + 50¢, paid tiers buy the rate down, +1.5% on non-US cards
findings.detail: Published table: Starter free at 5% + 50¢; Pro $20/mo at 3.8% + 40¢; Growth $100/mo at 3.6% + 35¢; Scale $400/mo at 3.4% + 30¢. Surcharges: +1.5% for international (non-US) cards, +0.5% on subscription payments on the Early Member plan, $15 per dispute, and Stripe-side payout costs of $2/month plus 0.25% + $0.25 per payout plus 0.25% cross-border within the EU. Polar states it is the Merchant of Record and its worked example shows it charging Swedish 25% VAT, though the fees page does not itself spell out a VAT-compliance commitment. For a French seller every card is 'international' by Polar's definition, so read the effective free-tier rate as 6.5% + 50¢.
findings.source_quote: +1.5% for international cards (non-US)
findings.cost_eur: ~1.44 EUR on a 15 EUR sale on the free tier (~9.6%)

findings.claim: Gumroad: 10% + $0.50, merchant of record for tax since 1 January 2025
findings.detail: Direct sales are charged 10% + $0.50; listings surfaced through the Discover marketplace are charged 30%. Gumroad states that since 1 January 2025 it handles all tax obligations, managing sales tax collection and remittance worldwide, covering VAT, GST and other international requirements. Payout is by direct deposit or PayPal depending on country; the page states no currency-conversion fee and sets out no business-entity or country eligibility requirement. On a 15 EUR sale this is roughly 1.96 EUR, about 13% — the most expensive of the three and the hardest to justify at his price point.
findings.source_quote: Since January 1, 2025, Gumroad handles ALL your tax obligations.

findings.claim: FastSpring is a merchant of record but publishes no rate
findings.detail: FastSpring confirms the MoR role and that it collects and remits VAT and sales taxes on the seller's behalf and responds to VAT/sales-tax audits. It publishes no percentage and no fixed fee: pricing is described as flat-rate, negotiated with its sales team by transaction type and business volume. Unusable for a cost comparison at his scale without contacting them, and the sales-led motion is a poor fit for a sub-20-EUR digital product.
findings.source_quote: simple, flat-rate pricing based on transaction type and your volume of business

findings.claim: Lemon Squeezy's fees could NOT be verified — the pricing page refuses automated fetches
findings.detail: Every route I tried returned HTTP 403: lemonsqueezy.com/pricing, lemonsqueezy.com/pricing/, docs.lemonsqueezy.com/help/payments/fees and docs.lemonsqueezy.com/help/getting-started/fees. Search summaries consistently report 5% + $0.50 with stacking surcharges (+1.5% international, +1.5% PayPal, +0.5% subscriptions), but a search summary is not a source and I am not asserting it. Separately unverified: Lemon Squeezy was acquired by Stripe and I found no primary statement about whether it still onboards new sellers — check before spending any design effort on it.

findings.claim: The registre des traitements becomes mandatory the day he has his first customer — CNIL's own example kills the exemption
findings.detail: CNIL states the obligation concerns every organisation, public or private, of whatever size, that processes personal data. Businesses under 250 employees get a derogation, but it is cancelled for three categories, and the first is traitements non occasionnels — for which CNIL's stated example is 'gestion de la paie, gestion des clients/prospects et des fournisseurs'. A customer file is by definition non-occasional. So the answer to 'is a registre mandatory for someone this small' is yes, from the first paying customer, and the under-250 exemption never protects him. The other two cancelling categories — processing likely to risk rights and freedoms, and sensitive data — do not apply to a culinary learning path. Note his free newsletter list already arguably triggers this today.
findings.source_quote: les traitements non occasionnels (exemple : gestion de la paie, gestion des clients/prospects et des fournisseurs, etc.)

findings.claim: CNIL publishes a free simplified register template for small structures
findings.detail: CNIL distributes a modèle de registre simplifié as an .ods spreadsheet aimed at small businesses, SMEs, associations and small local authorities, with a tutorial sheet, a processing-list sheet, a blank template and a worked example. I found this only through the CNIL search listing and did not open the file itself, so treat the sheet composition as reported rather than confirmed. It is the obvious starting artefact rather than drafting a register from scratch.

findings.claim: He signs no DPA with Stripe — it is already part of the contract — and Stripe is BOTH his processor and an independent controller
findings.detail: Stripe's DPA states it is subject to and forms an integral part of the Services Agreement, so accepting the SSA accepts the DPA; there is nothing to negotiate or sign separately. The split it draws: Stripe acts as sous-traitant on his behalf for operating the Stripe platform and providing and giving access to Stripe's products and services; Stripe acts as an independent responsable de traitement wherever it has exclusive power to determine purposes and means — fraud detection and prevention, financial-loss mitigation and security-risk monitoring, internal processes enabling service delivery, legal compliance including AML and KYC controls, and product analysis and development. Version last updated 18 November 2025.
findings.source_quote: Le présent Contrat de traitement des données (« DPA ») est soumis au Contrat, dont il fait partie intégrante

findings.claim: He is the controller for his customer file; the provider is processor for the platform only — and with a merchant of record the roles change
findings.detail: CNIL defines a sous-traitant as the person or body that processes data on behalf of another organisation, the responsable de traitement, within a service or engagement. Applied to his case with Stripe: he decides why and how his buyer list exists, so he is responsable de traitement for it, and names Stripe as sous-traitant in his registre for that leg while recording separately that Stripe is an independent controller for its own AML/fraud purposes — a dual-role entry, not a single one. Important and not researched further: with a merchant of record the buyer's counterparty is Paddle/Polar/Gumroad, not him, which likely shifts the controller analysis for the transaction data itself. Confirm that in each provider's own DPA before relying on it.
findings.source_quote: Le sous-traitant est la personne physique ou morale (entreprise ou organisme public) qui traite des données pour le compte d'un autre organisme

findings.claim: Accounting retention is 10 years from the close of the financial year, under Code de commerce L123-22
findings.detail: Service-Public Entreprendre gives 10 years from the close of the exercice for factures clients et fournisseurs, for livres et registres comptables and for pièces justificatives, each citing Code de commerce article L123-22. A separate 10-year rule under Code de la consommation L213-1 and D213-1 to D213-2 covers contracts concluded electronically with a consumer, but only from 120 € upward, running from delivery or performance — his 10-19 EUR products fall below it, so only the accounting rule bites.
findings.source_quote: 10 ans à partir de la clôture de l'exercice (Code de commerce : article L123-22)

findings.claim: The 10-year duty and the minimisation duty do not actually collide — CNIL sequences them into two zones with different legal bases
findings.detail: CNIL's référentiel for commercial activities resolves it directly. Data needed to perform contracts is kept in base active for the duration of the contractual relationship. At the end of the contract it must move to archivage intermédiaire for a reasonable period where there is a legal obligation — accounting or tax is its stated example — or to preserve evidence in case of dispute, within the applicable limitation period, using a dedicated archive database or a logical separation inside the active base after sorting what is worth archiving. CNIL is explicit that archived data is then processed for a different purpose than performing the contract and must rest on a different legal basis, either legitimate interest under art. 6.1.f or legal obligation under art. 6.1.c. Its lifecycle page adds that archiving or deleting a datum in one processing does not forbid continuing to use it in another. So: purge the live customer record, keep the invoice in a separated archive for 10 years under 6.1.c, restrict access.
findings.source_quote: Au terme du contrat, elles doivent être conservées en archivage intermédiaire et pour un délai raisonnable, si le responsable du traitement en a l'obligation légale

findings.claim: Customer and prospect data for marketing: 3 years, and the clock is defined precisely
findings.detail: Same référentiel. Customer data used for commercial prospection may be kept during the commercial relationship then for three years from its end — CNIL's examples of that end are a purchase, a warranty expiry date, a service contract's term, or the customer's last contact. A non-customer prospect's data may be kept three years from collection or from the prospect's last contact, where clicking a link in an email counts as contact but merely opening the email does not. At three years he may ask whether they want to keep hearing from him; absent an explicit positive answer the data must be deleted or archived. Separately, for accounts users create and abandon, CNIL says two years of inactivity is a proportionate deletion trigger.
findings.source_quote: un délai de trois ans à compter de leur collecte par le responsable de traitement ou du dernier contact émanant du prospect

findings.claim: An identity document copy is kept only as long as the verification needs it — 6 years maximum, and never in the live base
findings.detail: CNIL's référentiel: the pièce d'identité is kept for the time needed to verify the person's identity; a copy may be kept for 6 years where that is necessary for evidence or to answer a legal obligation, and in that case reinforced security measures apply and the copy must not sit in base active but in archivage intermédiaire. Relevant if he ever collects ID himself; not relevant to the ID he gives Stripe or Sumsub, which they hold as controllers under their own AML duty.
findings.source_quote: ces informations ne doivent pas être conservées en base active mais doivent être stockées en base d'archivage intermédiaire

findings.claim: What changes in the privacy notice on day one of paying customers: five specific lines
findings.detail: CNIL's mandatory list is identity and contact details of the controller, purposes, legal basis, whether providing the data is obligatory or optional, recipients or categories of recipients, retention duration or the criteria setting it, data-subject rights, DPO contact details, and the right to complain to the CNIL — plus, where applicable, transfers outside the EU, automated decision-making or profiling, and the right to withdraw consent. Against a free-site notice, the five that actually change: (1) a new purpose, order and delivery management; (2) a new legal basis, performance of the contract, which is NOT consent and must not be presented as consent; (3) a new named recipient, the payment provider, plus the fact that it also acts on its own account for AML and fraud; (4) two-tier retention rather than one, contract duration then a 10-year accounting archive; (5) transfers outside the EU, since Stripe, Paddle and Polar all process in the US. CNIL adds that regular re-information serves transparency, particularly on substantial modifications. He needs no DPO.
findings.source_quote: Durée de conservation des données (ou critères permettant de la déterminer)

findings.claim: 2026 micro-entreprise ceilings: 203 100 € goods, 83 600 € services — his lane is the 83 600 €
findings.detail: Service-Public Entreprendre states the micro regime applies where chiffre d'affaires perçu en 2026 does not exceed 203 100 € for sales of goods or 83 600 € for prestations de services. Loss of the regime requires exceeding the ceiling in both N-1 and N-2, with the switch to régime réel on 1 January of the following year. All three of his likely shapes — a paid learning path, a licence to an établissement, consulting — are prestations de services, so 83 600 € is the only figure that matters. I did not find published 2027 figures; the micro ceilings are revalued on a three-year cycle, so the 2026 numbers should hold for 2027-2028, but that is my inference, not something I read.
findings.source_quote: chiffre d'affaires perçu en 2026 ne dépasse pas l'un des seuils suivants : 203 100 € pour les activités de vente de marchandises et 83 600 € pour les prestations de services
findings.cost_eur: immatriculation free (23,21 € only for agents commerciaux)

findings.claim: The 25 000 € single VAT threshold was ABANDONED — franchise en base for services is 37 500 € in 2026
findings.detail: Service-Public Entreprendre states that the proposal from the loi de finances pour 2025 to introduce a single franchise en base threshold of 25 000 € has been abandoned. The 2026 thresholds stand: 85 000 € base and 93 500 € tolerance for commercial and accommodation activities; 37 500 € base and 41 250 € tolerance for prestations de services and professions libérales; 50 000 € / 55 000 € for lawyers. Under franchise en base he charges no VAT and must print 'TVA non applicable, article 293 B du CGI' on invoices. This is worth knowing precisely, because a remembered '25 000 €' would have made him think the MoR route was near-compulsory when it is not.
findings.source_quote: La proposition issue de la loi de finances pour 2025 visant à instaurer un seuil unique de franchise en base de TVA de 25 000 € a été abandonnée.

findings.claim: Student and micro-entrepreneur are compatible; at 18+ every activity type is open to him
findings.detail: Service-Public Entreprendre: a major may carry on any activity — commerciale, libérale or artisanale — subject to qualification requirements for regulated ones. Emancipated minors aged 16-18 may do artisanal or liberal work but need a judge's authorisation for commercial activity; non-emancipated minors are barred from commercial activity entirely. Since he is already 18 none of that binds him. Two things that do: if he stays rattaché to his parents' foyer fiscal his micro-enterprise income is declared on their tax return, which moves their taxable income; and he keeps his student social security affiliation while paying contributions on micro-enterprise turnover under the régime micro-social. The ceiling for rattachement of a student under 25 and the effect on any bourse are not covered by this page and I did not verify them.
findings.source_quote: Étudiant majeur : toute activité — commerciale, libérale ou artisanale — sous réserve des qualifications requises

findings.claim: A dedicated bank account is required only above 10 000 € of turnover for 2 consecutive years, and need not be a professional account
findings.detail: Service-Public Entreprendre: the dedicated account becomes obligatory once turnover or receipts exceed 10 000 € for two consecutive years. It need not be a compte professionnel — a separate personal current account can serve — but it must carry the mention 'entrepreneur individuel' or 'EI', which in practice is what makes banks refuse an ordinary personal account for the purpose. At his likely first-year volumes he is well under and can defer the professional-account fees entirely.
findings.source_quote: obligatoire dès lors que son chiffre d'affaires (ou ses recettes) dépasse le seuil de 10 000 € pendant 2 années consécutives
findings.cost_eur: 0 EUR below the threshold; pro accounts typically billed monthly

findings.claim: His likely commercialisation date lands exactly on the e-invoicing emission deadline, 1 September 2027
findings.detail: The DGFiP fiche for TPEs, marked 'Mise à jour juin 2026', sets two dates. By 1 September 2026 at the latest every business must have chosen an approved platform and be able to RECEIVE electronic invoices from large and intermediate-sized companies. By 1 September 2027 at the latest a micro-entreprise or PME must be able to EMIT electronic invoices through an approved platform to professionals established in France. The fiche is explicit that being obliged to receive does not oblige you to emit: before 1 September 2027 a small business need not invoice a large customer electronically, and it is the supplier's job, not his, to know whether the supplier is obliged. This binds shape (b), the licence sold to a lycée or CFA, which is B2B.
findings.source_quote: Au plus tard le 1er septembre 2027 : vous devez être en capacité d'adresser à vos clients des factures électroniques
findings.when: document marked 'Mise à jour juin 2026'; fetched 2026-09-15
findings.cost_eur: cost of an approved platform — not researched

findings.claim: Selling to individuals triggers e-reporting from 1 September 2027, and franchise en base does NOT exempt him
findings.detail: DGFiP fiche 7, also marked 'Mise à jour juin 2026'. E-reporting de transaction catches sales and services to natural persons or to legal persons not liable for VAT — B2C, its examples being private individuals and non-profit associations — in France as abroad, and separately catches B2B transactions with parties established in or outside the EU. From 1 September 2027 the data must be sent to the administration on a periodicity set by the seller's VAT regime, and the fiche names 'franchise en base' as the first of those regimes: being under the VAT threshold sets the frequency, it does not remove the obligation. This hits shape (a) — a B2C learning path sold in France and elsewhere in the EU — head on. One consolation that also serves his RGPD posture: for non-taxable customers what is transmitted is daily aggregate turnover split by VAT rate, and the fiche states that no personal data is requested and none must be transmitted.
findings.source_quote: Lorsque les opérations sont réalisées avec des personnes non assujetties, aucune donnée personnelle n'est demandée et ne doit être transmise.
findings.when: document marked 'Mise à jour juin 2026'; fetched 2026-09-15
findings.cost_eur: cost of an approved platform — not researched

ordered_steps: Before the first euro, and not a day after: register the micro-entreprise at the guichet unique (INPI), free, and collect the SIREN/SIRET that INSEE returns. Stripe's form will not stop him, but selling repeatedly without immatriculation is dissimulation d'activité at 3 years and 45 000 €. This single step also unlocks everything below — franchise en base, invoicing, the DPA analysis.

Decide the rail before building a checkout. Stripe direct: cheapest per transaction, but he is the seller and owns EU VAT himself — which under franchise en base (37 500 € services, 2026) and below the 10 000 € cross-border B2C digital threshold is close to trivial, and gets much less trivial above either. Merchant of record (Paddle 5% + $0.50, Polar 5% + 50¢ +1.5% on non-US cards, Gumroad 10% + $0.50): 3 to 8 extra points buys the VAT problem disappearing at every future scale. At 10-19 EUR the arithmetic favours Stripe direct while he stays small; note Paddle pushes sub-$10 products to custom pricing.

Write the registre des activités de traitement the same week the first customer pays — not later. Start from CNIL's free simplified .ods model. The under-250-employees derogation does not help him: CNIL's own example of a cancelling non-occasional processing is 'gestion des clients/prospects'.

Record the payment provider in that registre as a dual role, not a single one: sous-traitant for operating the platform and delivering the service, and independent responsable de traitement for its own fraud, security, AML and KYC purposes. Nothing to sign — Stripe's DPA is an integral part of the Services Agreement (version of 18 November 2025). For a merchant of record, read that provider's own DPA first: the buyer's counterparty is the MoR, not him, and the controller analysis for transaction data probably differs.

Rewrite the privacy notice before the checkout goes live, changing five things against the free-site version: add the order-and-delivery purpose; state performance of the contract as the legal basis and do not dress it as consent; name the payment provider as recipient and say it also acts on its own account; give two retention tiers instead of one; and declare the transfer outside the EU, since Stripe, Paddle and Polar all process in the US. No DPO needed.

Build retention as two zones from the start rather than retrofitting it. Base active purged at the end of the commercial relationship, with marketing use capped at 3 years from the last contact. Archivage intermédiaire holding invoices and accounting records 10 years from the close of the exercice (Code de commerce L123-22), logically or physically separated, access restricted, resting on legal obligation (art. 6.1.c) rather than on the contract. The two duties are sequential phases, not a conflict.

Open a dedicated account only when turnover passes 10 000 € for two consecutive years — and remember it need not be a professional account, though the mandatory 'EI' mention is what makes ordinary banks refuse a personal one.

Choose an approved e-invoicing platform ahead of the deadlines if he is trading by then: reception capability by 1 September 2026, emission and B2C e-reporting by 1 September 2027. Franchise en base sets the e-reporting periodicity, it does not exempt him — and late 2027 is exactly when this bites.

Flagged, out of this lane's scope but caused by it: the moment he publishes à titre professionnel, LCEN art. 1-1 II lapses and the GitHub-address arrangement stops working. Full mentions légales in his own name and address become due the same day the first product goes on sale.
unknowns: Lemon Squeezy's fee structure — every URL I tried returned HTTP 403 (pricing page, both docs paths). The commonly cited 5% + $0.50 with stacking surcharges comes only from third-party blogs, which I did not open and am not asserting. Also unverified: whether Lemon Squeezy still onboards new sellers after the Stripe acquisition.

Stripe's France-specific accepted-document list. The per-country rows on docs.stripe.com/acceptable-verification-documents render client-side and returned placeholder headings in both the HTML and .md?country=FR variants. That CNI, passeport and permis de conduire are accepted is probable from the Stripe Identity country list, but the authoritative France row is unread.

Whether Stripe France in practice demands a SIRET or a professional RIB at risk review despite not asking for either in its requirements schema. Stripe's KYC page reserves the right to collect more, and the field list is not a promise.

2027 thresholds. The 203 100 € / 83 600 € micro ceilings and the 37 500 € franchise en base figure are the published 2026 numbers; I found no 2027 publication. The micro ceilings revalue on a three-year cycle so they probably hold, but that is inference.

Shape (b), the licence to a lycée or CFA: whether invoicing a public établissement requires Chorus Pro, and whether a région's appel à projets imposes its own contracting or data terms. Not researched in this lane.

Whether a merchant of record actually accepts a French seller who is a private individual with no SIRET at all. Paddle waives business verification for 'individuals or sole traders', but that phrase does not settle whether an entirely unregistered French individual passes — and it would not cure the French-law problem anyway.
The cost of an approved e-invoicing platform for a micro-entreprise. The DGFiP fiches name the obligation and point to the approved-platform list but publish no price.
