Student-specific tax detail: the income ceiling for rattachement to the parents' foyer fiscal under 25, and whether micro-enterprise income affects a bourse. The Service-Public page on combining the statuses does not cover either.

research.lane: Lane 6 — Selling to a French public lycée or a Région (Copius, horizon late 2027)

findings.claim: The no-procedure ceiling is now 60 000 € HT, not 40 000 €. It changed on 1 April 2026.
findings.detail: Décret n° 2025-1386 du 29 décembre 2025 (JO 30/12/2025) rewrote article R2122-8 of the code de la commande publique: for fournitures et services the dispense de publicité et de mise en concurrence rose from 40 000 € HT to 60 000 € HT, applicable to consultations engagées à compter du 1er avril 2026. Travaux went to 100 000 € HT on 1 January 2026. Any figure of 40 000 € you see in a 2022-2025 guide (including the EPLE vademecums still circulating) is stale. Below 60 000 € HT a lycée can simply order from him — no advert, no tender, no competitor.
findings.source_quote: L'acheteur peut passer un marché sans publicité ni mise en concurrence préalables […] inférieure à 60 000 euros hors taxe
findings.when: service-public.fr page vérifié le 21 août 2026; décret du 29/12/2025, effet 01/04/2026

findings.claim: Below the ceiling the buyer still owes three duties, one of which bites on a repeat supplier.
findings.detail: R2122-8 al. 2: the acheteur must choisir une offre pertinente, faire une bonne utilisation des deniers publics, and ne pas contracter systématiquement avec un même opérateur économique lorsqu'il existe une pluralité d'offres. Practical effect for Copius: a single lycée can buy year after year without a procedure, but the gestionnaire will want a devis and ideally a second comparable quote in the file. It also means his own lycée buying from him is not illegal, but should be documented against at least one alternative — favoritisme is the risk the buyer, not he, carries.
findings.source_quote: ne pas contracter systématiquement avec un même opérateur économique lorsqu'il existe une pluralité d'offres

findings.claim: The signature is the proviseur's, as pouvoir adjudicateur — but the conseil d'administration must have authorised it first.
findings.detail: Article R.421-20 6° d) of the code de l'éducation: the CA gives its accord on la passation des marchés, contrats et conventions dont l'établissement est signataire. Three carve-outs: marchés inside an adopted décision modificative; in case of urgency, gestion courante below 5 000 € HT for services; and marchés à incidence annuelle for which the CA has delegated to the chef d'établissement. A one-year licence renewed expressly can be treated as annual (so covered by a standing délégation); a multi-year or tacitly-renewed subscription is pluriannuel and needs its own CA vote. Sell a 12-month licence with express renewal, not an auto-renewing subscription — that is the difference between a signature and a CA agenda item.
findings.source_quote: La passation des marchés, contrats et conventions dont l'établissement est signataire
findings.when: vadémécum MAPA en EPLE, février 2022 (mechanics current; its 40 000 € figures are superseded)

findings.claim: The money comes from the EPLE's service AP, inside a budget the CA votes before 30 November for the following calendar year.
findings.detail: The EPLE budget's section de fonctionnement is split into three services — activités pédagogiques (AP), vie de l'élève (VE), administration et logistique (ALO) — plus services spéciaux. A pedagogical digital licence sits in AP. The dominant resource is the dotation globale de fonctionnement from the collectivité de rattachement (the Région for a lycée), notified before 1 November; the CA then votes the budget before 30 November so it is executable on 1 January. Selling window: a lycée's appetite for a new AP line is highest September-November, for money it will spend the following year.
findings.source_quote: activités pédagogiques (AP) ; vie de l'élève (VE) ; administration et la logistique (ALO)
findings.when: IH2EF page mise à jour 11 février 2026

findings.claim: No supplier is legally required to be in LDE, PopLab or any catalogue. That constraint is specific to manuels and to the funding channel, not to selling.
findings.detail: Nothing in the code de la commande publique conditions a sale on catalogue referencing; the arrêté du 22 mars 2019 lists what a buyer may demand, and catalogue membership is not on it. Two real constraints wear the costume of one: (i) manuels scolaires in Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes are bought by the Région itself under its own marché and distributed to pupils — a lycée does not buy them, so that lane is genuinely closed to a non-titulaire; (ii) a Région that wants to fund resources centrally procures a plateforme unique d'acquisition (Normandy ran exactly such a tender in 2026), and everything it funds flows through that holder. Copius sold directly to a lycée on the lycée's own AP credits needs no catalogue at all.
findings.source_quote: Déclarations appropriées de banques ou, le cas échéant, preuve d'une assurance des risques professionnels pertinents
findings.when: arrêté du 22 mars 2019, art. 2; Normandy platform tender indexed 2026 (notice itself not opened, 403)

findings.claim: The GAR is the real gate, and it is an engineering project, not a form.
findings.detail: If pupils reach the resource through the ENT médiacentre in a public établissement — which is how AURA lycées consume digital resources — the supplier must adhere to the Gestionnaire d'Accès aux Ressources. Adhesion means signing a contrat d'adhésion with the ministry (dne-gar@education.gouv.fr), declaring technical and commercial distributors, and building three interfaces: moissonnage of resource descriptions, a webservice for subscription management, and SSO for access management. Legal frame: arrêté du 18 décembre 2017 (JO 23/12/2017), CNIL délibération n° 2017-253. A static PWA with no per-pupil accounts is not GAR-shaped; making Copius GAR-compatible is a rewrite, not a config change. The AURA appel à projets states flatly that its eligible resources are GAR-compatible for public établissements.
findings.source_quote: L'éditeur de ressources numériques signe le contrat d'adhésion et déclare ses opérateurs techniques et commerciaux

findings.claim: The AURA appel à projets is not open to him. Only lycées apply — a supplier is named inside a school's dossier, never a candidate.
findings.detail: Full 2025-2026 text read. Bénéficiaires: les lycées publics et privés du territoire régional, généraux, technologiques, professionnels ou agricoles. The dossier de candidature asks for the establishment's UAI-RNE, its référent numérique, the number of pupils concerned — and, for each resource wanted, an identifiant de la ressource souhaitée. Calendar: open 22 septembre – 17 octobre 2025, dotations from December 2025, valid one year. Envelope 190 K€. Two exclusions matter: les licences numériques de manuel scolaire ne sont pas éligibles, and no matériel or software without pedagogical purpose. Scoring is 40 % on the pedagogical project as judged by the autorités académiques. So the only way in for Copius is for a teacher in a lycée to want it enough to write it into their school's dossier — and for the resource to have an identifier and GAR compatibility.
findings.source_quote: Les lycées publics et privés du territoire régional Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes

findings.claim: I could not find a 2026-2027 edition of that appel à projets published as of today.
findings.detail: Checked: the Région's aides listing (JS-rendered, returns no usable content to a fetcher), targeted searches on auvergnerhonealpes.fr and ent.auvergnerhonealpes.fr, DRANE and académie relays, and general search for the 2026 dossier. Only the 2025-2026 document surfaces. Given the 2025 edition opened on 22 September, a 2026 edition — if the experiment is renewed — would plausibly appear in the next two to three weeks. This is an absence of evidence in sources I could reach, not evidence of absence. The reliable check is the address the Région itself publishes for the scheme: gratuite_manuels_scolaires@auvergnerhonealpes.fr, chef de projet François Tessier.

findings.claim: URSSAF attestation de vigilance is required from 5 000 € HT, and it is renewed every six months for the life of the contract.
findings.detail: The donneur d'ordre must obtain it at signature and every six months until the contract ends; the attestation is valid 6 months and carries a security number the buyer verifies on urssaf.fr. It applies to travailleurs indépendants sans salarié, not only employers — so a solo micro-entrepreneur is squarely in scope. Legal frame: code du travail L8222-1 to L8222-7. A new business gets a provisional attestation until its creation formalities are complete. Below 5 000 € HT — which is where a first lycée licence will sit — it is not legally required, though some gestionnaires ask anyway.
findings.source_quote: L'attestation est valable 6 mois

findings.claim: The standard pre-signature pack is social attestation, fiscal declaration on honour, and proof of registration — plus SIREN on every invoice.
findings.detail: Formulaire NOTI1 practice, per code du travail D.8222-5: an attestation de fourniture de déclarations sociales less than six months old; an attestation sur l'honneur that all mandatory fiscal declarations have been filed; an extrait K or Kbis less than three months old, or a récépissé de dépôt de déclaration auprès d'un centre de formalités des entreprises for a business still being registered. The buyer must give at least the candidate a deadline no shorter than 10 days. Separately, every invoice must carry the numéro SIREN, and an entrepreneur individuel must show his name preceded or followed by « Entrepreneur individuel » or « EI ». Practical consequence: with no SIRET there is no sale to a public body at all — not a hard sale, no sale. The récépissé line is the useful one: he can bid while registration is still processing.
findings.source_quote: Nom et prénom de l'entrepreneur individuel précédé ou suivi de la mention « Entrepreneur individuel ou EI »
findings.when: page vérifiée le 7 août 2026; NOTI1 list from the EPLE vadémécum, février 2022

findings.claim: Invoices to any public body go through Chorus Pro. That has been true since 2020 and survives the 2026 e-invoicing reform.
findings.detail: Administrations are required to use Chorus Pro to receive and process invoices; all suppliers to the public sphere, micro-entreprises included, send through it. From September 2026 suppliers may instead route via an agreed plateforme agréée (except travaux, mémoires de frais de justice, demandes de remboursement), with Chorus Pro remaining the reference platform. Separately, on the general B2B e-invoicing reform, PME and micro-entreprises must comply with the new invoice mentions from 1 September 2027. Cost implication: zero — Chorus Pro is free — but it is a portal to learn, not an email attachment.
findings.source_quote: Les administrations sont tenues d'utiliser Chorus Pro pour la réception, le traitement […] de ces factures

findings.claim: RC pro is not legally required for a non-regulated digital activity — but a public buyer is allowed to demand proof of it, so budget for it anyway.
findings.detail: Two separate facts. (1) Obligation: insurance is mandatory only for activités réglementées, for the bâtiment (décennale), health, vehicles used professionally and rented premises. Selling digital educational content is none of these. (2) Procurement: the arrêté du 22 mars 2019 art. 2 lets the acheteur require « preuve d'une assurance des risques professionnels pertinents » as a capacité économique et financière document — so in a real MAPA he may be asked. Price: an insurance broker's July 2026 tariff page puts low-risk conseil/numérique at 13-20 €/month, i.e. roughly 160-240 €/year; a marketing consultant at 40 000 € revenue is quoted 17 €/month, 200 €/year. That figure is a broker's commercial page, not an official statistic — treat it as an order of magnitude, and get two real quotes before budgeting.
findings.source_quote: Si vous exercez une activité réglementée, vous devez souscrire un contrat d'assurance responsabilité civile professionnelle (RCP)
findings.when: service-public fiche vérifiée le 22 septembre 2023 (dated — re-check before relying); price page Orus, 27 juillet 2026

findings.claim: RGAA does not bind him as a seller. It reaches him through the buyer's contract clauses instead — and that is the harder version.
findings.detail: Article 47 of loi n° 2005-102 covers personnes morales de droit public, private bodies delegated a mission de service public, private bodies created to meet besoins d'intérêt général non commercial, and entreprises from a 250 M€ annual French turnover threshold (three-year average). A solo seller is outside all four. But article R2111-6 of the code de la commande publique says: « Sauf cas dûment justifié, les spécifications techniques sont établies de manière à prendre en compte des critères d'accessibilité pour les personnes handicapées ». It carries no threshold, so it applies to a 3 000 € MAPA as much as to a formalised tender. DINUM's own guidance to buyers recommends a critère éliminatoire spécifique for accessibility and a commitment to 100 % of RGAA criteria. So the practical obligation is real and contractual: for a public sale he can expect to be asked for an accessibility statement and a conformity rate, with no legal floor protecting him. The Ministry also maintains accessibility expectations for suppliers of educational digital services in its Doctrine technique du numérique pour l'éducation — I did not open that document (education.gouv.fr blocks automated fetches).
findings.source_quote: Sauf cas dûment justifié, les spécifications techniques sont établies de manière à prendre en compte des critères d'accessibilité
findings.when: R2111-6 CCP; RGAA scope page read 15/09/2026; DINUM buyer guidance read 15/09/2026

findings.claim: On the private-sale side the European Accessibility Act already applies, and he is exempt as a microentreprise — for now.
findings.detail: The directive (UE) 2019/882, transposed in France, applies since 28 June 2025 and covers commerce électronique among its services. The exemption: fewer than 10 salariés with annual chiffre d'affaires or total de bilan under 2 million euros. Copius shape (a) — a paid tier sold to individuals — is e-commerce and would be in scope but for that exemption, which he meets by a wide margin and will for years. Note the asymmetry this creates: selling to individuals carries no accessibility obligation, selling to a lycée does, through R2111-6. I could not open EUR-Lex to quote article 4(5) of the directive directly (the server returns 202 with an empty body to automated clients), so the exemption wording here is the French administration's restatement, not the directive's own text.
findings.source_quote: L'entreprise concernée compte moins de 10 salariés avec un chiffre d'affaires annuel ou un total de bilan inférieur à 2 millions d'euros
findings.when: actualité publiée le 27 novembre 2025; directive applicable depuis le 28 juin 2025

findings.claim: There is a national scheme that funds producing the resource rather than buying it — Édu-Up — and its eligibility wording would cover him once he has an entity.
findings.detail: Édu-Up is the Ministry's support for producing digital educational resources. Reported eligibility: entities exercising an economic activity regardless of legal form, plus associations; support up to 50 % of total project cost; a cash apport propre of at least 25 % of the project; at most two grants to the same entity. Reported commission calendar running into 2027 with dossier deadlines (16 October 2026, 12 March 2027, 18 June 2027). I could NOT open the source pages — education.gouv.fr returns a Cloudflare block and eduscol returned 403 — so every figure here comes from search summaries and none of it is verified. Flagged because it is the only route found where an author, rather than a school, is the applicant. Verify directly before acting on any of it.
findings.when: search results read 15/09/2026; deadlines reported for 2026-2027

findings.claim: His age is not an obstacle; his status as a student is not either. The foyer fiscal is the only place his situation changes anything, and that is a tax question this lane did not verify.
findings.detail: At 18 he is majeur, so he can register an entreprise individuelle without parental authorisation — the capacity questions that apply to a mineur (émancipation, or authorisation for acts of administration) do not arise. No rule in the code de la commande publique treats a student candidate differently, and the vadémécum records that lack of prior public-contract references cannot on its own eliminate a candidate. Two cautions I did not verify in this lane: (i) while he is rattaché to his parents' foyer fiscal, micro-entreprise turnover is declared within that foyer and can raise their tax — arithmetic worth doing before the first invoice; (ii) his own lycée buying from an enrolled student is not prohibited by the CCP, but it puts the chef d'établissement in an awkward spot and the file should show a compared alternative. Both belong to a different lane.
findings.when: reasoning as of 15/09/2026, not separately sourced

research.bottom_line: Selling to a lycée is legally easy and structurally hard. Easy: since 1 April 2026 a public buyer can order anything under 60 000 € HT with no advert, no tender and no competitor — a 300 € or 800 € licence is a devis, a bon de commande and a signature by the proviseur. Hard: three gates stand before that signature. He must exist as an opérateur économique (no SIRET, no sale — the invoice legally requires a SIREN); invoices go through Chorus Pro; and if pupils are to reach Copius through the ENT médiacentre, the supplier must adhere to the GAR, which means a ministry contract plus three built interfaces (moissonnage, subscriptions webservice, SSO) — a rewrite of a static PWA, not a setting. The Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes appel à projets is not a door for him at all: only lycées apply, they name a resource by identifier inside their own dossier, and the eligible resources are GAR-compatible ones. I found no 2026-2027 edition published as of today, though last year's opened on 22 September, so it may be days away. The catalogue question resolves cleanly: LDE/PopLab referencing is not a legal requirement, it is the shape of the funding channel — manuels are bought by the Région under its own marché, and regionally-funded digital resources flow through whatever platform holds the regional contract. Sold directly to one lycée on its own crédits pédagogiques, no catalogue is needed. Accessibility inverts the usual intuition: selling to individuals carries no obligation (the European Accessibility Act exempts him as a microentreprise, under 10 salariés and 2 M€), while selling to a public body does, because R2111-6 of the code de la commande publique makes the buyer write accessibility into the specifications with no threshold below which it stops applying. RC pro is not mandatory for a non-regulated digital activity but a buyer may demand proof of it; budget roughly 160-240 €/year. The realistic 2027-2028 sequence is individuals first, then one lycée at a time on its own budget — and only if institutional demand proves real does the GAR investment make sense.
ordered_steps: Before touching any of this: nothing here is actionable without a legal entity. Registering a micro-entreprise is what turns Copius from a free site into a supplier, and it is also the moment LCEN art. 1-1 II lapses. Keep that decision in its own lane and after June 2027.

Between now and 30 September 2026, send one email — gratuite_manuels_scolaires@auvergnerhonealpes.fr, chef de projet François Tessier — asking whether a 2026-2027 edition of the appel à projets ressources numériques complémentaires is planned and what the identifiant de la ressource field expects. Costs nothing, requires no entity, and answers the one question I could not close.

Ask the same question the other way round, at his own lycée: whether the établissement has ever applied to that AAP, and who its référent numérique is. A teacher who wants the resource is the only mechanism that gets Copius into a school's dossier.

Decide early whether the institutional shape is worth the GAR. Adhesion is a ministry contract plus three built interfaces against a static site with no user accounts. If the answer is no, the institutional lane collapses to direct sales of a non-ENT licence on a lycée's own credits — which is a perfectly real market and needs none of this.
When the entity exists, register on Chorus Pro the same week. It is free and it is the only channel a public body can pay through.

Price the first institutional licence as a 12-month licence with express renewal, not an auto-renewing subscription. Annual incidence lets the proviseur sign under a standing CA délégation; tacit renewal makes it pluriannuel and forces a CA agenda item every time.

Keep the first sale under 5 000 € HT while he is new. Below that the URSSAF attestation de vigilance is not legally required of the buyer, which removes a six-monthly administrative loop from the relationship.

Time the approach to the budget cycle, not the school year: the Région notifies the dotation before 1 November and the CA votes the budget before 30 November for the following calendar year. September to November is when a new AP line can still be created.

Before quoting to any public buyer, have an accessibility answer ready — a declaration and a measured RGAA conformity rate. R2111-6 has no threshold, and DINUM tells buyers to make accessibility an eliminatory criterion. This is the requirement that will actually decide whether a serious institutional sale closes.
Get two real RC pro quotes rather than relying on the 160-240 €/year indicative figure, and only buy when a buyer asks or the first institutional contract is imminent.
unknowns: Whether a 2026-2027 edition of the AURA appel à projets exists. Not published in anything I could reach as of 15 September 2026; the Région's aides listing is JS-rendered and returns nothing to a fetcher. Last year's opened 22 September, so this may resolve within weeks.

Whether the AURA AAP requires the resource to be in the LDE/PopLab catalogue. The 2025 text points to app.poplab.education only as examples and asks for an identifiant de la ressource — which implies a catalogue entry somewhere, but the document never names a required one. Unresolved; only the Région can answer.

Who holds the current AURA marché for ressources numériques éducatives. The 2023 consultation exists and an avis d'attribution was published 06/10/2023, but the attributaire is behind a login on the platforms I reached. Matters because that holder is the gatekeeper for anything the Région funds centrally.
Whether GAR adhesion carries any fee, and how long the three interfaces actually take to build. gar.education.fr states no cost and gives no timeline; the answer comes from dne-gar@education.gouv.fr.

Édu-Up in full. Every figure I have for it — eligibility open to any entity exercising an economic activity, 50 % ceiling, 25 % apport propre, the 2026-2027 commission dates — comes from search summaries. education.gouv.fr is Cloudflare-blocked and eduscol returned 403. Verify before relying on any of it; it is the only scheme found where an author rather than a school applies.

The exact text of article 4(5) of directive 2019/882 on the microentreprise services exemption. EUR-Lex returns HTTP 202 with an empty body to automated clients; the exemption is quoted here from the French administration's restatement, not the directive itself.

Whether the buyer requires a RIB as such, and in what form. Not verified — payment obviously needs bank details, but I found no source stating it as a procurement requirement, so it is listed here rather than asserted.
The tax effect of micro-entreprise turnover declared inside his parents' foyer fiscal while he is rattaché. Real and potentially material to the family, but a different lane — not researched here.
The service-public fiche on micro-entrepreneur insurance was last vérifiée 22 septembre 2023. Old enough to re-check before relying on it for the obligation question.

audits.overall:
Audited all 43 claims against their cited sources. The file is unusually well-sourced — most quotes are genuinely on the page and genuinely support the claim, and several claims (the impots.gouv.fr staleness catch, the LCEN article 19 "repeal" false positive, the 25 000 € TVA abandonment) are correct and well-made. Six problems, three of them decision-changing:

1. WRONG — the BNC rate trajectory (claim 3). 25,6 % is not a waypoint on a rising path. 26,1 % was the scheduled 2026 endpoint of the LFSS-2024 trajectory, and décret n° 2025-943 du 8 septembre 2025 cut it to 25,6 %. The trajectory ENDED in 2026; no further step is programmed. The cited Bpifrance page still carries the stale forward-looking sentence "Au 1er janvier 2026, il évoluera encore pour atteindre 26,1 %", so the claim's quote does not read as written there. The 25,6 % figure itself is correct and confirmed by service-public F36232.

2. OVERSTATED — the CFP cadence (claim 4). "Versement unique en novembre" is the entrepreneur individuel rule (a fixed 120 €/139 € payment), not the micro-entrepreneur rule. A micro-entrepreneur's CFP is computed and paid with each monthly or quarterly déclaration. The rate (0,2 % BNC) and the all-in 25,8 % arithmetic are right.

3. OVERSTATED — e-invoicing (claim 28). The 1 September 2027 emission obligation covers B2B invoices between French assujettis. Sales of a digital learning path to individuals are OUTSIDE the emission scope — they fall under e-reporting instead. Presented as if it governs his main product. The B2G route to a lycée via Chorus Pro is right.

4. OVERSTATED — registre des achats (claim 31). Required only of commerçants and fournisseurs d'hébergement. A BNC/prestations activity keeps the livre des recettes only. Stated as if it binds him.

5. OVERSTATED + internal contradiction — declare-zero strategy (claim 5). The 90-day rule is verbatim correct, but "create the entity, declare zero for several periods, and owe nothing" directly burns the ACRE window that claim 10 tells him to protect: the window runs from the DECLARED START DATE, not from first revenue. Two claims in this file give opposite instructions on when to file. Also unmentioned: 24 consecutive zero-CA months triggers radiation d'office.

6. UNVERIFIABLE — guichet unique specifics (claim 40). The justificatif list and the "locked fields" detail are not on the cited Bpifrance page.

Cross-cutting, and not in any claim: nothing in this file addresses (a) EU VAT on electronically supplied services — above 10 000 € of cross-border B2C e-services the place of supply moves to the customer's country and the French franchise stops shielding him, which a public website selling a course will hit; (b) the droit de rétractation on digital content, art. L221-28 13° — without an explicit pre-download waiver he owes 14-day refunds; (c) the micro thresholds are prorated temporis in the creation year, so a 1 October 2027 start gets roughly 21 000 €, not 83 600 €. One genuinely good piece of news he should bank: 83 600 € is frozen for 2026, 2027 and 2028, so it is the figure that actually applies to him.

Figures to re-derive rather than inherit before he files: every euro amount here is a 2026 amount and he starts in late 2027 — the VFL RFR ceilings, the CAF 55 %-of-SMIC figure, the ¾-SMIC association ceiling, the 81 051 € association franchise and the CFE minimum base all reindex annually.

verdicts.claim: Creating a micro-entreprise is free and done online at the guichet unique (INPI), and it is the only legal route since 2023.
verdicts.why: "L'immatriculation d'un micro-entrepreneur est gratuite" is on the cited Bpifrance page (dated October 2025), as is the 23,86 € RSAC fee. The guichet unique has been the sole mandatory channel since 1 January 2023 (loi PACTE n° 2019-486, art. 1), and formalities feed the RNE. Two gaps: the cited page contains no mention of the guichet unique, INPI, SIRET or the RNE, so the second half of the claim rests on nothing at that URL; and the page presents the SPI as optional ("vous avez la possibilité de suivre un stage"), not as a required cost.
verdicts.correction: The SPI has been optional since the loi PACTE (2019) — it is not a paid exception for artisanal activities, it is a voluntary 260 € course. Cite a source that actually covers the guichet unique for the sole-route and RNE points.

verdicts.claim: Cotisations URSSAF from 1 January 2026: 12,3 % vente de marchandises, 21,2 % prestation de services BIC, 25,6 % activité libérale non réglementée BNC — a flat percentage of revenue, not of profit.
verdicts.why: All three rates are verbatim on service-public F36232, vérifié le 01 janvier 2026, and the page adds 23,2 % for Cipav. Independent sources corroborate 25,6 % for micro-BNC in 2026. The rates are on chiffre d'affaires, not profit.
verdicts.correction: The classification lean may be backwards for his main product. A pre-recorded, packaged learning path sold repeatedly online reads more naturally as prestation de services BIC (21,2 %) than BNC; BNC fits training or consulting he delivers personally. The claim's advice to settle the classification before filing is right, but the default it assumes is the expensive one.

verdicts.claim: The BNC rate rose from 24,6 % in 2025 to 25,6 % in 2026 — this rate is on a rising path, so do not plan against a remembered figure.
verdicts.why: The figures are right but the direction of travel is not, and the quote is not on the page as given. 26,1 % was the scheduled 1 January 2026 endpoint of the trajectory programmed by the LFSS for 2024; décret n° 2025-943 du 8 septembre 2025 reduced it to 25,6 %. 2026 was the final tier, and no further increase is programmed. The cited Bpifrance page still carries the stale forward-looking sentence "Il est passé à 24,6 % au 1er janvier 2025. Au 1er janvier 2026, il évoluera encore pour atteindre 26,1 %" — so the page contradicts the claim's own quote. The page also does not discuss any assiette sociale / CSG-CRDS reform for 2026.
verdicts.correction: 25,6 % is the END of a completed trajectory, reached only because a décret cut the scheduled 26,1 %. It is not climbing. Plan on 25,6 % and treat any further move as a new political decision, not a scheduled step — and do not cite that Bpifrance page, which carries both figures.

verdicts.claim: The contribution à la formation professionnelle is charged ON TOP of the cotisation rate: 0,2 % for a liberal activity, 0,3 % artisanal, 0,1 % commercial.
verdicts.why: The rates are right and on service-public F23459 (vérifié 01 janvier 2026), and the all-in 25,8 % arithmetic holds. But the quoted November sentence belongs to the entrepreneur individuel paragraph, where the CFP is a fixed euro amount (120 € commercial/liberal, 139 € artisanal, set as a percentage of the plafond annuel de la sécurité sociale). For a micro-entrepreneur the CFP is calculated on turnover and settled with each monthly or quarterly déclaration, not as a single November payment.
verdicts.correction: A micro-entrepreneur pays the CFP inside every URSSAF échéance, so his forecast should carry 25,8 % on every declaration period — not 25,6 % all year with a November top-up. The cash-flow shape the claim describes is the classic EI's, not his.

verdicts.claim: Cadence: monthly or quarterly, chosen at creation, declared online — and the first declaration cannot be filed until at least 90 days after the start of activity.
verdicts.why: The rule is verbatim on F36232: "La première déclaration peut être effectuée au minimum 3 mois (90 jours) après le début de l'activité", and the September-start worked example is arithmetically right. The problem is the strategy built on it. "He can create the entity, declare zero for several periods, and owe nothing while the first offer is built" contradicts claim 10 in this same file: the ACRE window runs from the declared start date, so every zero-revenue quarter spends ACRE he cannot get back. The claim also omits that 24 consecutive months of zero CA triggers radiation d'office.
verdicts.correction: Creating early is not free — it is paid for in ACRE. Either create early and accept that the 6,4-point reduction burns on empty quarters, or create on the first day of the quarter in which he actually starts selling. The two cannot both be optimised, and this file tells him to do both.

verdicts.claim: The micro regime's revenue ceilings were raised for 2026: 83 600 € for prestations de services and for BNC, 203 100 € for vente de marchandises.
verdicts.why: Both figures are verbatim on service-public F32353, vérifié le 21 février 2026, measured on CA HT of N-1 (2025) or N-2 (2024). The page also says what happens on a crossing — two consecutive years above and you leave the regime on 1 January of the following year, a single year above has no automatic consequence. The loi de finances pour 2026 froze 83 600 € for revenues 2026, 2027 and 2028, so it is the figure that applies to his actual start.
verdicts.correction: One caveat the 'non-constraint' framing misses: in the creation year the threshold is ajusté prorata temporis. A 1 October 2027 start faces roughly 21 000 €, not 83 600 €. Still not binding at his scale, but it is not the headline number.

verdicts.claim: ACRE still exists, and Gabriel qualifies on age alone — but the exoneration was cut from 50 % to 25 % for micro-entreprises created on or after 1 July 2026.
verdicts.why: service-public Entreprendre A18795 (published 11 February 2026) carries "passe de 50 à 25 %", "Décret n° 2026-69 du 6 février 2026", and the split application dates: 1 January 2026 for entrepreneurs individuels, SASU and SA, 1 July 2026 for micro-entreprises. The 18-25 age criterion is confirmed separately on F11677. The claim's own warning that the rule moved twice in one year and that any 2027 figure is provisional is the right posture.

verdicts.claim: Under ACRE the micro-entrepreneur pays 75 % of the normal rate — BNC 19,2 % instead of 25,6 %, BIC services 15,9 % instead of 21,2 %.
verdicts.why: F11677 (vérifié le 01 juillet 2026) gives "un taux minoré de cotisations sociales égal à 75 % du taux normal" and the 15,9 % worked example against 21,2 % for a BIC service activity. The 960 € on 15 000 € of BNC revenue is arithmetically right.
verdicts.correction: 19,2 % is the claimant's own multiplication, not a figure published anywhere — it is only as good as the 25,6 % it derives from, and it assumes he holds BNC classification. The page's other worked example shows 12,3 % for commerce, which is the full vente rate, so do not treat that page's example list as an ACRE rate table.

verdicts.claim: ACRE conditions in 2026: one qualifying situation — being aged 18 to 25 is itself one — plus no ACRE in the previous three years, and the request must reach URSSAF within 60 days of the start of activity.
verdicts.why: The 60-day deadline is verbatim in A18795 and repeated on F11677. F11677 carries the eligibility list including aged 18-25 (29 if disabled), under 30 without sufficient work history, and the no-ACRE-in-3-years bar. The claim's emphasis that the 60-day deadline is the binding one is right — it was 45 days historically, so a remembered figure would cost him the whole benefit.
verdicts.correction: Two attributions are off. A18795, the URL cited, contains only the deadline and the rate change — not the age list or the three-year rule; those come from F11677. And "URSSAF rules within 30 days and silence is acceptance" appears on neither page.

verdicts.claim: The ACRE window runs to the end of the 3rd civil quarter following the declared start date — so starting on the FIRST day of a quarter is worth up to three extra months of reduced rate.
verdicts.why: F11677 carries "jusqu'à la fin du 3e trimestre civil suivant la date de début d'activité déclarée". Both worked examples check: a 1 October 2027 start sits in Q4 2027 and runs through Q3 2028 (twelve months); a 20 December 2027 start sits in the same quarter and ends on the same date (about nine months). The start date is his to choose on the creation form.
verdicts.correction: This is the claim that claim 5's declare-zero strategy quietly destroys. Reconcile the two before he files.

verdicts.claim: Versement libératoire: 1 % vente, 1,7 % prestation de services BIC, 2,2 % BNC — paid with the cotisations, and it settles income tax on that revenue entirely.
verdicts.why: All three rates are on service-public F23267, vérifié le 13 mai 2026, along with the 30 September deadline for the following year and the three-month window for a new business, and the symmetric renunciation procedure. The 28 % all-in BNC arithmetic (25,6 + 0,2 + 2,2) holds.

verdicts.claim: The versement libératoire is gated on the revenu fiscal de référence of the FOYER FISCAL, year N-2 — which, while Gabriel is rattaché, means his parents' income decides whether he can have it.
verdicts.why: F23267 carries all four ceilings verbatim — 29 579 € / 59 158 € / 73 947,50 € / 88 737 € — measured on the foyer fiscal's RFR of year N-2. The 2,5-parts arithmetic is right. While he is rattaché the foyer fiscal is his parents', so their RFR is the gate. This is genuinely the sharpest hidden consequence of rattachement in the file.
verdicts.correction: These are 2026 ceilings. An option taking effect in 2028 tests the 2026 RFR against reindexed 2028 ceilings. Check the parents' avis now for the order of magnitude, then re-derive the ceiling in the year he actually opts.

verdicts.claim: The impots.gouv.fr page on the versement libératoire is stale — it still shows the 2024 ceiling of 27 478 € per part and the old 77 700 €/188 700 € thresholds.
verdicts.why: Re-opened today: the page shows "27 478 € pour une part de quotient familial" for 2024 applicability on 2022 income, and 188 700 € / 77 700 € as the turnover thresholds. Header reads "Publié le 03/08/2016, modifié le 07/01/2026" with "MAJ le 10/10/2024" — a January 2026 modification date sitting over October 2024 content, exactly as the claim describes. Use F23267 and F32353 for figures.

verdicts.claim: Student status is not an activity and buys no relief: cotisations are due from the first euro of revenue.
verdicts.why: F36612 (vérifié le 07 avril 2026) states cotisations are payable on the chiffre d'affaires realised in the micro-entreprise and sets out no student exemption, franchise or reduced rate. ACRE is the only reduction available, and it turns on his age, not his enrolment.

verdicts.claim: Health cover does not change in practice: the separate student social security regime was abolished at the 2019-2020 rentrée, and both students and new travailleurs indépendants sit in the régime général at the CPAM of residence.
verdicts.why: The substance is well established — the separate student regime was wound down between 2018 and the 2019-2020 rentrée and students moved to the régime général. The claim's own warning is validated: F36612, verified 7 April 2026, still reads "Un étudiant est en principe affilié à la sécurité sociale des étudiants", which is the outdated phrasing. The claim's recommendation to confirm directly with his CPAM is the right call.
verdicts.correction: The cited ministère FAQ returned HTTP 403 today, so the specific quote could not be re-read at that URL. The conclusion stands on the abolition itself and on F36612's contradicting text, not on that page.

verdicts.claim: The bourse sur critères sociaux is set from the REVENU BRUT GLOBAL of the reference foyer fiscal, two years back — so income he declares in 2027 sets his échelon for 2029-2030.
verdicts.why: F12214 (vérifié le 10 avril 2026) carries "Les revenus pris en compte figurent à la ligne revenu brut global de l'avis d'imposition ou de non-imposition" and, for 2026-2027, income "perçus en 2024 (avis fiscal de 2025) par la famille ou le tuteur légal". The only exceptions listed are marriage, PACS or a dependent child. The N-2 pattern gives 2029-2030 for 2027 income.
verdicts.correction: An angle worth checking rather than assuming: the bourse reads revenu brut global, while the versement libératoire keeps the bénéfice out of the revenu brut global and puts it in the RFR instead. If that holds, VFL could shield his échelon as well as settle his income tax — a second reason to want the option, and a reason to confirm with the CROUS rather than infer it.

verdicts.claim: While rattaché, his micro-entreprise income goes on his parents' tax return — and even under the versement libératoire it raises their tax on their own income through the taux effectif.
verdicts.why: Both quotes are on the impots.gouv.fr page (published 03/08/2016, modified 16/06/2026): the net profit after the micro-BIC or micro-BNC abattement "est retenu pour le calcul du taux effectif appliqué pour l'imposition des autres revenus du foyer", and "est également retenu pour le calcul du revenu fiscal de référence". The 34 % micro-BNC and 50 % micro-BIC services abattements are confirmed as unchanged for 2026 by the loi de finances pour 2026. The conclusion that there is no configuration in which his revenue is invisible to his parents' tax position is correct.

verdicts.claim: Rattachement is available until 21, or until 25 for a student — so he has the choice every year, and it is a genuine annual decision, not a permanent state.
verdicts.why: The age rule is correct law (CGI art. 6-3: under 21, or under 25 if a student), rattachement requires his written request, and the parents choose annually between the extra part of quotient familial and deducting a pension alimentaire. The advice to compute the flip on the parents' actual avis rather than assume it is right.
verdicts.correction: The cited page, F36612, carries the quote about income going on the parents' return but does not state the 21/25 age limits. Cite the CGI or a fiche that covers rattachement itself.

verdicts.claim: For CAF purposes a child stops counting as "à charge" above 55 % of the SMIC — 1 104,25 € per month for October 2025 to March 2026 — and the limit runs to 20 (21 for complément familial and aides au logement).
verdicts.why: F16947 (vérifié le 01 juin 2026) gives 55 % du SMIC, 1 104,25 € net per month for October 2025 to March 2026 (1 082,87 € for the preceding half-year), and the age limits of 20, or 21 for the complément familial and aides au logement. The window is indeed live when commercialisation starts.
verdicts.correction: The page does address the self-employed case the claim says it omits: students and boursiers are assessed on a six-month average, while apprentices, employees and travailleurs indépendants are assessed month by month, with a breach costing only that month. What remains genuinely unresolved is which basis CAF applies to a micro-entrepreneur's income — chiffre d'affaires or the profit after abattement. Also: 1 104,25 € is a half-year figure that will have moved several times before he sells.

verdicts.claim: The statut national étudiant-entrepreneur is free, has no age limit, and can substitute an entrepreneurial project for a mandatory internship — the one student-specific advantage worth chasing.
verdicts.why: F32313 (vérifié le 23 juin 2026) states "Il n'y a pas de limite d'âge pour candidater au SNEE", requires the baccalauréat and enrolment in a course preparing a diplôme de l'enseignement supérieur, and confirms he can "remplacer le stage obligatoire dans votre cursus de formation par le travail sur votre projet de création d'entreprise". The D2E is optional but recommended for an enrolled student.
verdicts.correction: Two corrections. The page does not say the SNEE is free, so cost_eur 0 is unsourced. And the claim's open question is largely closed by the page itself: "Le candidat ne choisit pas son Pépite. Il lui est attribué d'office soit en fonction de l'établissement d'enseignement où il est inscrit, soit de son lieu de résidence" — so residence provides a route even if his lycée has no PEPITE convention, and a BTS is a diplôme de l'enseignement supérieur, which is the eligibility test.

verdicts.claim: An association loi 1901 can legally sell, but it cannot distribute anything to anyone — no profit in any form, no share of the assets to members.
verdicts.why: BOI-IS-CHAMP-10-50-10-20 (7 June 2017, still the version in force) carries "l'organisme ne procède à aucune distribution directe ou indirecte de bénéfice, sous quelle que forme que ce soit" as one of the three cumulative conditions of gestion désintéressée, alongside bénévole management without direct or indirect interest in results and no attribution of assets to members beyond the return of contributions. The structural conclusion — the association essentially cannot pay him — follows.

verdicts.claim: The tolerance that lets an association pay its dirigeant stops at ¾ of the SMIC — 1 400,26 € brut per month — and going beyond needs 200 000 € of average annual resources and a fourth year of existence.
verdicts.why: F1927 (vérifié le 01 juin 2026) carries "La rémunération de chaque dirigeant ne doit pas dépasser les ¾ du Smic, soit 1 400,26 € brut par mois", the 200 000 € average over three closed exercices excluding public subsidies, and "La rémunération n'est possible qu'à partir de la 4e année d'existence de l'association", with one paid dirigeant at 200 000-500 000 €, two above 500 000 €, three above 1 000 000 €. The conclusion that the association cannot be how he earns is right at his scale.
verdicts.correction: 1 400,26 € tracks the SMIC and will be a different number by 2028.

verdicts.claim: An association becomes fiscally commercial when it competes with business under the règle des 4 P — Produit, Public, Prix, Publicité, weighed in that decreasing order.
verdicts.why: The same BOFiP document lists the criteria in decreasing order of importance — "le « Produit » proposé par l'organisme, le « Public » bénéficiaire, les « Prix » qu'il pratique et la « Publicité »" — and confirms the faisceau d'indices reading: "il n'est pas exigé que tous les critères soient remplis pour que les conditions d'exercice soient considérées comme différentes". The claim's application — a market-priced learning path marketed to the general public scores badly on all four, a below-market resource for lycées and CFAs does not — is a sound reading of the test.

verdicts.claim: The franchise that lets an association run accessory commercial activity untaxed is 81 051 € for exercices closed from 31 December 2025 — and service-public still publishes the stale 78 596 €.
verdicts.why: BOI-IS-CHAMP-10-50-20-20 (version in force 5 August 2026) carries "Le seuil de la franchise prévu au 1 bis de l'article 206 du code général des impôts (CGI) est porté à 81 051 € pour les exercices clos à compter du 31 décembre 2025", with the three cumulative conditions as stated and annual indexation on the forecast consumer price index. Corroborated independently: 81 051 € for 2026 against 80 011 € for 2025.
verdicts.correction: The service-public half could not be checked — F34104 returns HTTP 404 today, so that fiche appears to have been withdrawn. And 78 596 € is not one revaluation stale but two: it is the 2024 figure, with 80 011 € in between.

verdicts.claim: Declaring an association is free and fast: the greffe issues a récépissé within 5 days of a complete file, and publication in the Journal officiel costs nothing.
verdicts.why: F1119 carries "Le greffe des associations délivre un récépissé dans les 5 jours suivant la remise du dossier complet", free JOAFE publication, the signed procès-verbal, statuts "daté et signé, par au moins 2 dirigeants", and the RNA as "la lettre W suivie de 9 chiffres". The claim's own framing — the association is no heavier to create, the weight is in running it and in what it forbids — is right.
verdicts.correction: The fiche is vérifiée le 05 novembre 2024, the oldest verification date in the file; the claim states this honestly. Alsace-Moselle is the exception on both cost and signatures (7 members), irrelevant unless he registers there.

verdicts.claim: The single 25 000 € VAT franchise threshold from the 2025 finance law was ABANDONED — franchise en base stays at 37 500 € (N-1) with a 41 250 € tolerance for services.
verdicts.why: F21746 (vérifié le 01 janvier 2026) carries the sentence verbatim: "La proposition issue de la loi de finances pour 2025 visant à instaurer un seuil unique de franchise en base de TVA de 25 000 € a été abandonnée." Services and unregulated liberal activities are both at 37 500 € / 41 250 €. The page also states the crossing consequence the claim gives: "la franchise en base de TVA cesse de s'appliquer dès le 1er jour du dépassement". This one is stated as settled and is settled.
verdicts.correction: The shield is narrower than 'no VAT at all' suggests. It covers French VAT on sales to French customers. For a digital learning path sold to consumers elsewhere in the EU, the place of supply moves to the customer's country above 10 000 € of cross-border B2C e-services, and the French franchise stops protecting him — he would need OSS registration. A public website will find those buyers.

verdicts.claim: Every invoice under the franchise must carry the exact mention "TVA non applicable, art. 293 B du code général des impôts" — and showing any VAT amount makes him liable for it.
verdicts.why: F31808 (vérifié le 11 août 2026) carries the mention verbatim, along with the invoice date and unique number, seller identity and SIREN, buyer identity, designation and unit prices HT, totals, payment terms, late-payment penalties and the "indemnité forfaitaire de 40 €" for professional clients. The second half is correct law — CGI art. 283-3 makes anyone who shows VAT on an invoice liable for it by the sole fact of invoicing it.
verdicts.correction: The cited page does not state the consequence of showing VAT; that rule comes from CGI art. 283-3. Cite the article, not the fiche, for that half.

verdicts.claim: From 1 September 2027 micro-entreprises must ISSUE electronic invoices — which is exactly when he plans to start selling.
verdicts.why: The dates are right and verbatim on the impots.gouv.fr page (modified 16/01/2026): reception by all businesses from 1 September 2026, issuance by grandes entreprises and ETI from that date, by PME and micro-entreprises from 1 September 2027. Micro-entrepreneurs under the franchise en base are in scope as assujettis non redevables. But the emission obligation covers B2B invoices between French assujettis. Sales of a digital learning path to private individuals are outside it — B2C falls under e-reporting, the separate duty to transmit transaction data to the DGFiP. The claim applies a B2B rule to his main product.
verdicts.correction: For selling a course to individuals he does not need to issue structured electronic invoices; he needs to e-report the transaction data. The platform requirement bites on invoices to professional clients and, via Chorus Pro, on a lycée. Two things the claim omits and he should budget for: a plateforme agréée is generally a paid service, and this reform has already been postponed twice, so a 2027 plan should not treat the date as immovable.

verdicts.claim: CFE is waived in the creation year only if form 1447-C-SD is filed before 31 December, and is waived permanently while revenue stays at or below 5 000 €.
verdicts.why: F23999 (vérifié le 26 mars 2026) confirms the first-year exemption, the 1447-C-SD filed "au plus tard le 31 décembre" of the creation year, the 50 % base reduction in the first taxed year, the 250-597 € minimum base bracket for turnover at or below 10 000 €, and payment by 15 December. The practical conclusion — a small first paid year may cost nothing — holds.
verdicts.correction: Two corrections. The first-year exemption is automatic, "quelle que soit la date de création" — the 1447-C-SD is a separate declaratory obligation, not the condition the claim makes it. And the 5 000 € test runs on N-2, not on the current year: "L'entreprise est exonérée de CFE si le CAHT qu'elle a réalisé l'avant-dernière année (N-2) n'a pas dépassé 5 000 €". That two-year lag decides which year he actually pays.

verdicts.claim: A dedicated bank account only becomes mandatory above 10 000 € of revenue for two consecutive years, and it need not be a paid "compte professionnel".
verdicts.why: F35991 (vérifié le 28 mai 2026) carries the threshold sentence verbatim and confirms the dedicated account may be "soit un compte bancaire personnel" kept separate, "soit un compte bancaire professionnel". There is no fixed monthly banking cost to starting at his scale.

verdicts.claim: Accounting is a livre des recettes kept chronologically, plus a registre des achats, with supporting documents held for 10 years.
verdicts.why: The livre des recettes, its contents (amount and origin of receipts with client identity, payment method, references of supporting documents), the under-76 € daily total for retail sales and services to individuals, and 10-year retention from the close of the exercice are all on F23266 (vérifié le 07 septembre 2026). The registre des achats is not his obligation: the page restricts it to commerçants and fournisseurs de prestations d'hébergement. A BNC or prestations de services activity keeps the livre des recettes only.
verdicts.correction: Drop the registre des achats from his checklist unless he starts reselling goods or providing accommodation. The rest stands, and no accountant is needed at this scale.

verdicts.claim: Once he publishes 'à titre professionnel', LCEN article 1-1 I 1° requires his name, first names, DOMICILE and telephone number, plus his registration number if he is registered at the RCS or at the RNE as an artisan.
verdicts.why: Re-read on Légifrance: article 1-1 of loi n° 2004-575, version in force since 23 May 2024, modified by loi n° 2024-449 du 21 mai 2024 (SREN). Paragraph I requires for personnes physiques their "nom, prénoms, domicile et numéro de téléphone", plus the registration number where subject to RCS or RNE artisan registration, and also the publication director and the hosting provider's identity. The post-SREN renumbering from article 6 III to article 1-1 is correct, and the observation that the statute says domicile — not adresse de l'établissement — is accurate and load-bearing.

verdicts.claim: Article 1-1 II — the anonymity shelter he uses today — is drafted for 'les personnes éditant à titre NON professionnel', so it stops applying to him the day the site becomes professional.
verdicts.why: Paragraph II reads as quoted: non-professional publishers may hold out only the hosting provider's name and address, conditional on having given that provider their personal identification details, with the provider then bound by professional secrecy. The qualifier attaches to the publisher, and the paragraph offers no partial or transitional version for a mostly-free site with one paid tier. The claim's reading is correct.

verdicts.claim: 'Domicile' in article 1-1 is not defined by the LCEN, and I found no text or case law saying a declared business or domiciliation address discharges it for a personne physique. This is the single genuine gap in the chain.
verdicts.why: The three-way contrast that makes this a real question is verified word for word. Article 1-1 I says "domicile". Article 19 point 2° says "L'adresse où elle est établie". Code de la consommation article R221-2 point 1° says "l'adresse géographique où le professionnel est établi". Two establishment-based formulations and one domicile-based one, inside the statutes that all bind him at once. The claim reports an absence of contrary evidence rather than a source that settles it, and flags it as the one point worth a paid hour of a French lawyer — that is the correct handling of a gap of this kind, and it is the right place to spend the money.

verdicts.claim: The penalty service-public attaches to missing mentions légales is one year's imprisonment and a 75 000 EUR fine.
verdicts.why: F31228 carries "Le manquement à cette obligation d'information est puni d'1 an d'emprisonnement et 75 000 € d'amende", with the entrepreneur individuel mention list including name, first name and address with "entrepreneur individuel" or "EI". The claim is honest that it rests on the fiche and not on the statute's own sanctions article.
verdicts.correction: The fiche is vérifiée le 31 juillet 2023 — before the SREN renumbering the file relies on elsewhere — and its list names an RCS number, which a BNC micro-entrepreneur does not have. Treat the figure as indicative and read the sanctions article before quoting it as his exposure.

verdicts.claim: The earlier review's alarm was a false positive. Article 19 LCEN is NOT being repealed on 1 January 2027 — it gets a new version that day, created by article 43 of an ordonnance that recodifies VAT.
verdicts.why: Fetching the article at a March 2027 date returns a live article headed "Version en vigueur à partir du 01/01/2027" and "Modifié par Ordonnance n°2025-1247 du 17 décembre 2025 - art. 43", with all four points intact. The current version is headed "Version en vigueur du 01/07/2016 au 01/01/2027" — an end date that marks the next version's start, not an abrogation. The correction of the earlier review is right, and the method (query the article at a future date) is the right way to tell the two apart.

verdicts.claim: The only thing that changes in article 19 on 1 January 2027 is the VAT cross-reference in point 4°: article 286 ter of the CGI becomes article L. 215-27 of the code des impositions sur les biens et services. The address duty in point 2° is word-for-word identical before and after.
verdicts.why: I compared both versions. Point 2° reads "L'adresse où elle est établie, son adresse de courrier électronique, ainsi que des coordonnées téléphoniques permettant d'entrer effectivement en contact avec elle" in each, identical. Point 4° references "l'article 286 ter du code général des impôts" before and "l'article L. 215-27 du code des impositions sur les biens et services" after. Points 1° and 3° are unchanged. The practical consequence the claim draws is right, including that under the franchise en base he may have no individual VAT number to publish at all.

verdicts.claim: What article 19 makes an online seller publish, in easy, direct and permanent access: identity, the address where he is established, email and a working phone, his registration number and siège social if registered, and his VAT number if assujetti.
verdicts.why: The opening sentence reads "toute personne qui exerce l'activité définie à l'article 14 est tenue d'assurer à ceux à qui est destinée la fourniture de biens ou la prestation de services un accès facile, direct et permanent utilisant un standard ouvert aux informations suivantes", followed by the four points as the claim summarises them. The article also requires prices to be indicated "de manière claire et non ambiguë", and enforcement runs through the consumer code's agents.

verdicts.claim: Even if article 19 disappeared entirely, the address duty would survive untouched in the Consumer Code, which requires 'l'adresse géographique où le professionnel est établi' before any distance contract.
verdicts.why: Article R221-2 of the code de la consommation, in force since 28 May 2022, carries at point 1° "Son nom ou sa dénomination sociale, l'adresse géographique où le professionnel est établi, son numéro de téléphone et son adresse électronique", and at point 3° the siège commercial address where it differs, as the address for complaints. The duty is genuinely double-sourced, which is why the repeal scare never mattered.

verdicts.claim: At the INPI guichet unique he declares two distinct things: the address of the business (where the activity is carried on) and his own identity and personal address — and he must upload a justificatif de jouissance des locaux for the business address.
verdicts.why: The cited Bpifrance page (updated January 2026) supports only part of this. It carries "Les entrepreneurs individuels, même sous le régime du micro-entrepreneur, peuvent domicilier leur entreprise chez eux si aucune disposition contractuelle ou législative ne s'y oppose" and the attestation d'hébergement requirement when the declarant is not the lease holder. It does not carry the list of accepted justificatifs (lease, contrat de mise à disposition, sublease, domiciliation contract, electricity bill, rent receipt), and nothing at that URL supports the assertion that the guichet unique now locks fields for data already held and not published such as date of birth and personal address. The claim's `when` field also references a service-public fiche verified 2 July 2026 that is not among the URLs given.
verdicts.correction: Before he files, read the guichet unique's own documentation for the current list of accepted proofs — this is the step that decides which address ends up in the public record, so it should not rest on a secondary summary. Check the lease and any copropriété rules first: they are the condition the quoted sentence turns on.

verdicts.claim: What becomes PUBLIC in the RNE is everything filed, free and in electronic form — except that for a natural person the identity and domicile data published are capped at name, name in use, pseudonym, first names, MONTH and YEAR of birth, and COMMUNE of residence.
verdicts.why: Article L123-52 of the code de commerce, in force since 3 May 2025 (modified by loi n° 2025-391 du 30 avril 2025), carries the capping sentence verbatim: "La mise à disposition des informations inscrites relatives à l'identité et au domicile des personnes physiques mentionnées dans le registre est limitée aux nom, nom d'usage, pseudonyme, prénoms, mois, année de naissance et commune de résidence." His exact home address and day of birth are outside the public RNE view; his commune is inside it.
verdicts.correction: The second half — that the declared business address escapes the cap because it is company information rather than identité et domicile — is the claimant's inference, not something the article says. It is a plausible reading and it matters enormously if he declares the family home, so treat it as the thing to verify rather than as established. The INSEE non-diffusion request in the next claim is the available remedy if the inference is right.

verdicts.claim: INPI states as policy that the RNE does not diffuse the personal addresses of company representatives, which is consistent with the statutory cap.
verdicts.why: The INPI page carries "Le RNE ne diffuse pas les adresses personnelles des représentants d'entreprises", together with the three confidentiality levers the claim lists — the tickbox "Je demande que ce document ne soit pas diffusé publiquement", the dépôt d'acte à substituer, and the request to occult addresses at the RCS — each requiring a justificatif de confidentialité on a downloadable model. The legal basis cited is décret n° 2025-840 du 22 août 2025, on protecting the home address of certain natural persons listed at the RCS.
verdicts.correction: The claim is right that this decree does not reach him, and for the reason implied: it operates on the RCS, where a BNC micro-entrepreneur is not registered. Note also that the three levers are drafted around filed acts and the KBIS, which is a société's world — so the binding protection in his case is the L123-52 cap, not this page's policy statement.

verdicts.claim: The INSEE non-diffusion request is free, made online through FranceConnect, and takes effect in 48 hours for an entreprise individuelle.
verdicts.why: The INSEE page (dated 02/12/2025) confirms the online route via FranceConnect for entreprises individuelles taking effect within 48 hours, against a 10-working-day response for other entities. For an entreprise individuelle it covers the nom, prénoms, pseudonyme, enseigne and nom commercial plus the exact address within the commune and the geolocation variables; for a personne morale only the address and geolocation. Legal basis as cited: articles R123-222, R123-223, R123-232 and R123-232-1 of the code de commerce together with article 21 of the GDPR, which is why it is framed as a right of opposition. No fee is mentioned.
verdicts.correction: Scope worth being explicit about, since it is easy to over-read: this suppresses diffusion of the Sirene data. It does not touch the RNE, and it does not relieve him of publishing an address in his mentions légales under LCEN article 1-1 and article 19. It solves the database-scraping problem, not the published-website problem.

audits.overall:
43 claims audited against re-opened primary sources. The legal spine holds: the TVA thresholds, the definitive abandonment of the 25 000 € reform, the L221-28 13° waiver conditions, the withdrawal-button scope, the misleading-practice penalty tiers and the mediation duty are all confirmed verbatim, several of them against texts I opened on Légifrance rather than the commentary the research relied on. Nine claims have real defects.

The four that would cost him money or time if acted on as written:

1. The invoice-mentions list (claim 17) is the pre-2027 list. The same service-public page the claim cites says four further mentions become mandatory for micro-enterprises on 1 September 2027 — client's SIREN, delivery address where different, nature of the operation (biens/services/mixte), and the option pour le paiement de la taxe d'après les débits. That is his launch month exactly, so all four bind his first invoice.

2. The lycée rate (claim 26) is stated as settled 20%. It depends on the product's form: article 278-0 bis CGI puts livres fournis par téléchargement at 5,5%, and a downloadable guide meeting the fiscal definition of a livre takes that rate, while an interactive access product takes 20%. He chooses which he is building.

3. The first-year rule (claim 15) is stated backwards. BOFiP §285 prorates the plafonds, not the turnover. Arithmetically equivalent for the base threshold — but if the majoré plafond is prorated too, the in-year hard stop in his launch year sits below 41 250 €, which the "annualise the CA" framing hides.

4. The home-domiciliation finding (claim 6) says his situation fails. Bpifrance's own FAQ, at the cited URL, says the opposite: someone who is neither owner nor tenant can domicile there on an attestation signed by the title-holder. The practical conclusion — his family's address goes public — survives; the "fails" framing does not.

Two freshness problems the research could not have seen but should now act on. The promotional domiciliation rates (11-16 €) are gated on code SEPTEMBRE26 and expire 30 September 2026, so they cannot be planning numbers for a 2027 launch; and the honest cost is the TTC figure, because under the franchise he deducts no VAT on the fee — roughly 30 € TTC, not 25 € HT. Separately, Légifrance shows LCEN article 19 and the whole Titre II (articles 14 to 27) in a version window that ends 1 January 2027. A restructuring of the e-commerce identification duty is scheduled before he trades, and I could not identify the amending text with the tools available. Claims 10 and 30 rest on that article; re-check it before publication rather than treating it as stable.

Three claims quote sentences that are not at the URL they cite: the Sirene propagation sentence (claim 1), both OSS quotes (claim 20), and "contrat de domiciliation" as an accepted justificatif (claim 9). The substance is plausible in each case and confirmed elsewhere for OSS, but the citations do not carry it.

One caution on register, not law. Claim 40's legal analysis is correct, but its conclusion rests on facts about his own repository that no external source can check, and it quotes a 750 000 € ceiling as the cost of not fixing a word on a website. That is the statutory maximum for a criminal conviction, not an exposure estimate for a 19-year-old with no turnover. The fix is right and free; the number is not a reason for it.

One structural gap across the TVA lane: nothing in the set addresses that the old "année de tolérance", which used to let a business that crossed the ordinary limit keep the franchise for a further year, no longer exists. Crossing 37 500 € now costs him the franchise for the whole following year with no grace period, which sharpens claim 12 rather than contradicting it.

verdicts.claim: Non-diffusion hides the entrepreneur's identity, his address within the commune and his geolocation; activity, legal category, headcount bracket and administrative status stay public.
verdicts.why: The FAQ carries the quoted list verbatim for a personne physique, and names Décret n° 2022-1014 du 19 juillet 2022 as the source of the change from total concealment to partial masking. Public fields listed exactly as claimed.
verdicts.correction: Two additions. For a personne morale only the geolocation elements are masked, so the shape of the protection depends on his legal form. And the propagation sentence quoted in the detail ('Une fois votre demande envoyée, la mise à jour est faite dans le répertoire Sirene...') is not on this page — the page only says an entrepreneur individuel must make the request with INSEE directly. That sentence needs its own citation.

verdicts.claim: Non-diffusion does not bind the RNE/INPI or Infogreffe, and does not remove his own duty to publish an address in his mentions légales.
verdicts.why: Question 12588 was put by Thierry Benoit on 3 February 2026 and answered 26 May 2026. The question states the gap in the terms quoted; the answer neither denies it nor commits to a fix, describing only a general review in which 'la situation des entrepreneurs individuels sera prise en compte'. Acknowledged and unfixed, as claimed.

verdicts.claim: Décret n° 2025-840 covers dirigeants and indefinitely-liable partners of legal entities only; entrepreneurs individuels are excluded.
verdicts.why: The Objet notice names the beneficiaries as physical persons who are dirigeantes or associés indéfiniment responsables of personnes morales in the RCS. It creates R. 123-54-1 and R. 123-54-2 and amends R. 123-3, and enters into force the day after publication, so 24 August 2025.
verdicts.correction: The exclusion is read off the Objet notice, which is a presentational summary rather than enacting text. The government's own announcement (next claim) states the exclusion directly, so the conclusion is sound — but cite that, not the notice.

verdicts.claim: The government's announcement of the decree states the exclusion of entrepreneurs individuels in plain terms.
verdicts.why: Published 27 August 2025. Beneficiaries are physical persons who are legal representatives of a société and indefinitely-liable partners of personnes morales; entrepreneurs individuels are excluded and pointed instead to the INSEE opposition route. The sentence 'seule la commune de résidence fait l'objet d'une publication' is present and concerns natural persons in the RNE, as claimed.

verdicts.claim: An entrepreneur individuel can buy a commercial domiciliation; the provider needs a prefectoral agrément and the contract runs a minimum of three months. Home domiciliation requires being propriétaire or locataire of a résidence principale.
verdicts.why: Fiche vérifiée le 02 juillet 2026. It requires 'un agrément préfectoral' and states 'Ce contrat doit être d'une durée de 3 mois minimum'. For the home route it requires 'propriétaire ou locataire de votre logement' and that the home be the résidence principale.
verdicts.correction: Only the code de commerce L123-10 to L123-11-8 reference surfaced on the fiche; the R123-167 to R123-171 and CCH L631-7-3 references cited in the detail were not visible and should be checked if they are doing any work in the argument.

verdicts.claim: His personal situation fails the home-domiciliation test: living with family, he is neither owner nor tenant.
verdicts.why: The cited Bpifrance page addresses this exact scenario in its FAQ and answers the other way: an entrepreneur who neither owns nor rents can domicile the business at that address provided the actual tenant or owner signs an attestation d'hébergement. The route is open, not closed. The underlying rule in the code de commerce keys on the entrepreneur's domicile, not on holding title to it, so the service-public 'propriétaire ou locataire' wording is a simplification rather than a gate.
verdicts.correction: Three fixes. The route does not fail — it works on an attestation. The page's worked example is an attestation signed by a concubin holding the lease, not a parent; substituting a parent is a reasonable read but is not what the quoted sentence says. And the 'proof of address less than three months old in the host's name' detail is not on this page. The conclusion that actually matters is untouched and is the one to keep: the address that goes public is his family's, and it is his parents' consent being documented in a public-facing filing.

verdicts.claim: Domiciliation pricing 2026: 20 EUR/month with no commitment, 14 EUR/month on three years, promotional 16 and 11; tiers 18 and 16; mail 2,50 per item, +10/month, +40/month; no deposit; not tiered by legal form.
verdicts.why: Every figure matches the grid on the article dated 8 July 2026, including 'Aucune caution ni dépôt' and the statement that 'le tarif de domiciliation ne dépend pas de la forme juridique'.
verdicts.correction: Two corrections that change the planning number. The promotional rates are gated on code SEPTEMBRE26 and expire 30/09/2026, so 11-16 EUR cannot be used for a 2027 launch — the standing rates are 14-20 EUR. And the grid is HT, contrary to the claim's note that HT/TTC is not stated: the page marks € HT. Since he deducts no VAT under the franchise, his real cost is the TTC figure, about 20% above every number here.

verdicts.claim: A second provider puts the market band at 10 to 70 EUR HT per month, average 25 EUR HT, entry price 19 EUR/month; three-month minimum, mail and parcels included, 1 EUR/month for three months introductory.
verdicts.why: All four figures are on the page, updated 18 March 2026, in the words quoted: 'entre 10 € et 70 € HT par mois', 'tarif moyen observé ... 25 € HT par mois', 'à partir de 19 €/mois', 'durée minimale de 3 mois', and the 1 EUR introductory offer under code KAND1EU.
verdicts.correction: The derived planning band of 11-25 EUR HT leans on the expiring promotional rate from the other provider. A defensible band is 14-25 EUR HT with a three-year commitment, or 19-25 EUR HT without one — and because the franchise blocks deduction, budget it TTC: roughly 200 to 360 EUR a year, not 130 to 300. That strengthens the pricing point the claim is making rather than weakening it.

verdicts.claim: A domiciliation satisfies the RNE declaration cleanly — the domiciliation contract is on the accepted list of justificatifs de jouissance des locaux.
verdicts.why: The cited fiche does not list justificatifs de jouissance des locaux at all, so the 'contrat de domiciliation' quote is not carried by this source. The fiche establishes that a domiciliation is a lawful establishment address and that the contract must run three months minimum; it does not establish what the guichet unique accepts as proof.
verdicts.correction: Verify against the guichet unique's own document list (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) before relying on this. The claim's own reservation — that article 1-1 LCEN says 'domicile' where the selling-specific texts say 'établi', and that nothing official confirms a domiciliation address discharges the article 1-1 wording for a personne physique — is correctly stated and remains open. Article 1-1 I 1° does read 'nom, prénoms, domicile et numéro de téléphone', confirmed on Légifrance.

verdicts.claim: There is no lawful route to selling online in France with no postal address publicly readable anywhere.
verdicts.why: LCEN article 19 requires easy, direct and permanent access to, among other things, 'L'adresse où elle est établie, son adresse de courrier électronique, ainsi que des coordonnées téléphoniques'. No carve-out for small sellers, students, digital goods or low turnover. The consumer-side duty is independently confirmed by the CGV fiche, which lists the professional's identification among the pre-contractual information owed before a distance B2C contract.
verdicts.correction: A timing flag the research could not have seen. Légifrance shows this version of article 19 running only to 1 January 2027, and the whole Titre II of the LCEN (articles 14 to 27) carries the same end date — a restructuring of the e-commerce identification duty is scheduled before his late-2027 launch, and I could not identify the amending text. The conclusion that some address must be published is very unlikely to change, but the article number and its penalty almost certainly will. Re-check before he publishes.

verdicts.claim: Franchise en base: 37 500 € / 41 250 € for prestations de services, 85 000 € / 93 500 € for livraisons de biens, in force 2026; both his paid activities count against the same services line.
verdicts.why: BOFiP dated 01/07/2026 gives 85 000 / 93 500 and 37 500 / 41 250 as the second and third lines of the article 293 B table. Service-public, vérifié le 01 janvier 2026, gives the same figures with the same N-1 / in-year split. Thresholds attach to the assujetti, so two service activities under one SIRET share one ceiling, as claimed.
verdicts.correction: The source_quote is an English rendering, not text from the page. Quote the French if this is going into anything he relies on later.

verdicts.claim: Cross 37 500 € and VAT applies from 1 January of the following year; cross 41 250 € and VAT applies from the very first day of the overrun.
verdicts.why: BOFiP §130 states that exceeding the base threshold in the prior year loses the franchise for the whole following year, and that exceeding the heightened threshold in-year ends it 'à compter de la date à laquelle intervient ce dépassement'. Service-public puts it as 'dès le 1er janvier de l'année suivante' and 'dès le 1er jour du dépassement'. Both limbs verbatim.
verdicts.correction: Worth adding, because it sharpens the point: the old année de tolérance — which let a business that crossed the ordinary limit keep the franchise for a further year provided it stayed under the majoré — has been removed. There is no grace year behind the 37 500 € line any more.

verdicts.claim: The 25 000 € single threshold is definitively abandoned, deleted by article 1 of loi n° 2025-1044 du 3 novembre 2025.
verdicts.why: Service-public, published 5 November 2025, says the law 'supprime définitivement cette mesure et maintient l'application des seuils actuels' and cites loi n° 2025-1044 du 3 novembre 2025 by its full title. The decisive corroboration is that BOFiP's live doctrine of 1 July 2026 lists that law in its Actualité liée as amending article 293 B — the abrogation is reflected in the administration's own doctrine, not merely announced. Nothing in this set is stated as settled that is not.

verdicts.claim: The PLF 2026 variant (37 500 general / 25 000 for travaux immobiliers) was not enacted, and would not affect him anyway.
