verdicts.why: Upgrades from the claim's own medium-confidence inference to direct corroboration: the reform, reintroduced in the PLF 2026, was not carried over into the loi de finances pour 2026. That matches the control the claim proposed — BOFiP of 1 July 2026 lists only 85 000/93 500 and 37 500/41 250, with no travaux-immobiliers category. The reasoning from doctrine to statute was correct.

verdicts.claim: First year of activity: the turnover is annualised, not the threshold — CA × days in the year ÷ days from start to 31 December.
verdicts.why: The mechanism is stated the wrong way round against the governing doctrine. BOFiP §285 prorates the ceilings, not the turnover: 'les plafonds prévus pour le bénéfice de la franchise en base de TVA sont ajustés à proportion de la durée de l'année restant à courir'. Service-public does give the CA-annualisation formula quoted, and for testing the base threshold the two are arithmetically identical, so the claim's practical warning about launch timing stands.
verdicts.correction: The distinction is not cosmetic at the edge. BOFiP prorates 'les plafonds' in the plural, which reads as including the majoré ceiling — meaning the in-year hard stop in his launch year sits below 41 250 €, proportionally to the days remaining. The 'annualise the CA' framing invites the assumption that the 41 250 € cut-off stays whole in year one. Confirm the point with his SIE before modelling a launch date, and do not tell an accountant 'not the threshold'.

verdicts.claim: Invoice under the franchise carries 'TVA non applicable, article 293 B du code général des impôts' and shows no VAT anywhere; VAT wrongly stated is owed by the mere fact of invoicing it.
verdicts.why: BOFiP dated 01/07/2026: §50 prescribes the mention (or the article 284 of Directive 2006/112/CE reference); §53 states that beneficiaries cannot make VAT appear on their invoices and that one who does 'devient redevable du seul fait de cette facturation', with the client unable to deduct it. §60 extends the rule to simplified invoices. Both halves of the trap confirmed.

verdicts.claim: The 293 B sentence is an addition to the ordinary mandatory invoice mentions, not a replacement; the ordinary list is name preceded by 'Entrepreneur individuel' or 'EI', SIREN, address, unique sequential number, dates, designation and quantity, unit price HT, totals, due date, escompte, and for business customers the late-payment rate plus the 40 € recovery fee.
verdicts.why: Every item listed is on the page, vérifiée le 07 août 2026, including 'Escompte pour paiement anticipé : néant' and the 'Indemnité forfaitaire de 40 €'. But the list is incomplete for his own timeline, and the same page says so: four further mentions become mandatory — client's SIREN where the client is a business, delivery address where it differs from the client's address, whether the operation is biens, services or mixte, and the option pour le paiement de la taxe d'après les débits. They bind grandes entreprises and ETI from 1 September 2026 and PME and micro-entreprises from 1 September 2027, which is precisely his commercialisation window. A tolerance until 31 December 2027 covers only the old tax-reference format.
verdicts.correction: Also fix the reasoning on the client's VAT number. The page does carry the 150 € HT exception, but that is not why his 10-19 € consumer sales escape the line: a consumer has no VAT identification number at any price. The threshold bites only on B2B invoices, so it is the lycée invoice that engages it — and there, note that under the franchise he has no VAT number himself unless he requests one. Build the invoice template to the 1 September 2027 list, not this one.

verdicts.claim: The franchise does not exempt him from the electronic-invoicing reform: receiving compulsory for everyone from 1 September 2026, issuing plus e-reporting for TPE/PME/micro from 1 September 2027.
verdicts.why: The cited FAQ confirms the status point in terms: the reform applies to all assujettis whether or not redevable, the franchisé en base expressly included, and such a business is bound by the obligations to issue and receive electronic invoices and transmit data. The calendar is confirmed independently and has not slipped — a postponement was announced and then cancelled, leaving 1 September 2026 for reception by all and 1 September 2027 for issuance by PME and micro-entreprises. The date collision with his launch window is real.
verdicts.correction: The long quote is attributed to the wrong page: this FAQ gives no dates, does not differentiate by size, and does not use 'plateforme agréée' — it states the assujetti/non-redevable point and refers the reader to a test. Cite the calendar separately. One nuance for planning: the statute lets a décret push the issuance date back, but no later than 1 December 2027, so the platform choice cannot be deferred past his launch on the hope of a delay.

verdicts.claim: Digital product sold to a consumer in another EU country: VAT due in the consumer's country under article 259 D, but only once he passes 10 000 € of such sales EU-wide; the transaction that crosses the threshold is already located in the customer's Member State.
verdicts.why: Substance holds in every particular — article 259 D, the EU-wide aggregate excluding French turnover, the requirement that the limit not be exceeded in the current or the preceding calendar year, and the quoted sentence that the crossing transaction and all subsequent ones are located in the customer's Member State regardless of amount. The defect is the citation: the identifier points at the version of 25 September 2019, and a later version dated 22 December 2021 exists. Cite the current one.
verdicts.correction: Minor arithmetic: 10 000 € at 19 € per sale is about 526 sales, not 550. The band is roughly 525 to 1 000.

verdicts.claim: The OSS guichet unique is a single French registration, made from the espace professionnel, that lets him declare and pay every other Member State's VAT in one return, open to all assujettis whatever their VAT regime.
verdicts.why: The substance is right and confirmed on the page: registration is made 'via votre espace professionnel', and it lets a business 'déclarer et payer la TVA due dans les autres pays de l'UE en une seule et même déclaration', removing the need to register in each Member State. But neither quoted sentence is on this page — it does not state 'tous les assujettis, quel que soit leur régime d'imposition à la TVA' and does not mention the 10 000 € threshold. The openness of OSS to a franchisé is the load-bearing part of the claim and it is the part the citation does not carry.
verdicts.correction: Source the 'quel que soit leur régime' proposition separately before relying on it, or rely instead on the EU franchise route below, which is documented directly. The claim's closing caution is correct and worth keeping: OSS centralises paperwork, it does not exempt.

verdicts.claim: The franchise en base de TVA européenne, live since 1 January 2025, lets him stay exempt in other EU countries: EU turnover ≤ 100 000 € in N and N-1, below each target State's own threshold, not registered in OSS non-Union or IOSS, an EX number, quarterly per-State declarations, 15-day notification on breach.
verdicts.why: Every condition is on the page, modified 23/04/2026, in the words quoted: 'Avoir un chiffre d'affaires annuel dans l'Union inférieur ou égal à 100 000 € en année N et N-1', turnover in the exemption State below that State's own franchise threshold, 'Ne pas être inscrit au guichet unique TVA e-commerce (OSS) sous les régimes OSS non-UE ou IOSS', the numéro d'exemption, the quarterly declaration due the month following each quarter, and the 15-day declaration on exceeding the ceiling. The strongest-sourced claim in the TVA lane.

verdicts.claim: Sale to a consumer outside the EU: no French VAT, under article 259 B, which covers services fournis par voie électronique.
verdicts.why: BOFiP dated 27/12/2023 lists 'services fournis par voie électronique' among the services covered by article 259 B, and states that the place of such supplies is deemed not to be in France when made to a non-taxable person not established or habitually resident in a Member State. The claim's own caveat — that non-EU jurisdictions may nonetheless require registration under their own rules, unverified here — is the right way to state it.

verdicts.claim: Stripe in its standard form does not change who owes the VAT: its docs name the marchand officiel as 'Votre entreprise'.
verdicts.why: The comparison table's first row is exactly as quoted: Marchand officiel — Managed Payments: Stripe; Autres produits Stripe: Votre entreprise. Indirect tax compliance is marked as supported only under Managed Payments, and 'Disponible avec Tax' otherwise, which is the calculate-only position the claim describes.

verdicts.claim: Stripe Managed Payments is a merchant-of-record product: Stripe becomes the marchand officiel and handles VAT/GST/sales tax in 80+ countries; supports Checkout and Payment Links but not Elements, advanced integrations or Connect.
verdicts.why: Verbatim: 'Vendez des produits numériques dans le monde entier avec la solution de marchand officiel de Stripe pour la gestion des taxes, de la fraude, des litiges et de l'assistance', covering sales tax, TVA and TPS in more than 80 countries. The unsupported list matches — Connect, embeddable Elements and other advanced integrations are excluded, and the payment page row shows Checkout and Payment Links only.
verdicts.correction: Eligibility — which products, which seller countries, which integrations — sits on a separate page I did not open. Whether a French micro-entreprise under the franchise can actually enrol is the question to settle before counting on this, and the claim is right to flag it as a constraint rather than an answer.

verdicts.claim: Paddle is a merchant of record: it is the reseller and 'seller on record', and pays the VAT instead of him.
verdicts.why: Both sentences are on Paddle's own help page as quoted: Paddle 'acts as a reseller of your product, and is, therefore, the seller on record', and 'will be responsible for the collection and payment of VAT and tax instead of you'. The page states no conditions or limits on that assumption. The structural consequence the claim draws — that his supply is then to Paddle and the consumer sale is Paddle's — follows from the reseller characterisation.

verdicts.claim: Selling a licence to a lycée: nothing changes under the franchise; above the threshold it is 20%, because none of the teaching exonérations fit a licence.
verdicts.why: The exonération analysis is sound and confirmed. BOFiP requires lessons 'dispensés personnellement par des personnes physiques qui perçoivent, directement de leurs élèves, la rémunération' and states that those teaching with the help of salariés are subject to VAT; a licence bought by an établissement fails both limbs. Service-public, vérifié le 20 juillet 2026, confirms 20% for non-exempt teaching and the 3511-SD / DREETS route for formation professionnelle continue, with a three-month deemed approval. What is overstated is the rate. It is product-dependent, not settled: article 278-0 bis CGI applies 5,5% to livres fournis par téléchargement, and a downloadable guide that meets the fiscal definition of a livre takes 5,5%, while an interactive or access-based course takes 20%.
verdicts.correction: Decide the rate against the delivery form he actually builds, and if it is a downloadable guide, test it against the CGI definition of a livre before pricing at 20%. Separately, the formation professionnelle continue exemption is dismissed as 'a different business shape entirely' — it is a route with a known cost (déclaration d'activité under L. 6351-1 du code du travail, then the DREETS attestation), and if the lycée channel ever becomes material it should be priced rather than waved off.

verdicts.claim: Nothing in the VAT rules changes because he is a student, recently 18, or in his parents' foyer fiscal.
verdicts.why: No student, age or foyer-fiscal derogation appears anywhere in the doctrine on article 293 B. Thresholds attach to the assujetti, and the foyer fiscal is an income-tax concept with no VAT effect. The two consequences drawn are right: majority is what makes creating the micro-entreprise possible without emancipation, and every paid activity under one SIRET aggregates against one ceiling while the free site and newsletter contribute nothing.
verdicts.correction: The source_quote is the researcher's own summary, not text from BOFiP — presented in the same field as genuine quotations elsewhere in the set, which invites it to be re-quoted later as if it were doctrine. Mark it as a negative finding rather than a quote. And note the scope: this is true of VAT only. Remaining attached to his parents' foyer fiscal has real income-tax and benefit consequences for them once he has business income, which is a separate question this claim does not answer and should not be read as answering.

verdicts.claim: (a) The pre-contractual list is art. L221-5, 11 numbered items, fleshed out by art. R221-2; most templates miss 6°, 7°, 10° and 11°.
verdicts.why: L221-5 in its current form carries 11° on the application of a personalised price based on automated decision-making, added by Ordonnance n° 2026-2 du 5 janvier 2026 and in force 19 June 2026 — confirming both the item and the version the claim attributes it to. Contracts in progress on 19 June 2026 stay under the prior version.
verdicts.correction: R221-2's fifteen items were not enumerated against the text in this audit; the geographic address of establishment and the mediator's contact details are independently confirmed elsewhere in this set, the rest is taken on the claim's word. If the CGV are being drafted from this list, read R221-2 directly.

verdicts.claim: (a) Breach of the L221-5 information list on a distance contract is an administrative fine of 15 000 EUR for a personne physique, not the 3 000 EUR most blog posts quote.
verdicts.why: Article L242-10 reads exactly as quoted: any breach of the obligations in L. 221-5, L. 221-6, L. 221-8, L. 221-11, L. 221-12 to L. 221-14 carries an administrative fine capped at 15 000 euros for a personne physique and 75 000 for a personne morale. The contrast drawn with L131-1's 3 000/15 000 for the general L111-1 duty is correct, and as an entrepreneur individuel he is a personne physique.

verdicts.claim: (a) Publishing 'à titre professionnel' requires name, first names, address, SIREN, VAT number, phone, email and the host's identity in the mentions légales; omission is punished by 1 year and 75 000 EUR for an entreprise individuelle.
verdicts.why: The fiche, vérifiée le 19 juin 2026, lists exactly those elements for an entreprise individuelle and carries the sanction sentence verbatim: 'Le manquement à cette obligation d'information est puni d'1 an d'emprisonnement et 75 000 € d'amende pour les entreprises individuelles (dont micro-entrepreneur).'
verdicts.correction: Two things to resolve before he publishes. The page lists the numéro d'identification à la TVA without carving out the franchise, but a micro-entrepreneur under the franchise has no VAT number unless he asks for one — settle whether he must obtain one or may omit the line, rather than discovering it at launch. And the duty's home is moving: article 19 LCEN and the whole Titre II are in a version window ending 1 January 2027, so the article number and possibly the penalty will change before he trades.

verdicts.claim: (b) 14 days, and for a service or digital content the clock starts at conclusion of the contract, not at delivery.
verdicts.why: L221-18 gives fourteen days and splits the starting point as claimed: conclusion of the contract for service contracts, receipt of the goods for sales of goods. A downloadable learning path falls in the first branch. L221-20's twelve-month extension where the information was never given is present as the claim states.

verdicts.claim: (b) The waiver conditions are art. L221-28, 13°: three cumulative conditions plus the seller's confirmation under L221-13 al. 2.
verdicts.why: The exception for digital content without a material medium is numbered 13°, and its conditions read verbatim as quoted: a) prior express consent that execution begin before the withdrawal period expires; b) acknowledgment that he will lose the right of withdrawal; c) the professional has furnished confirmation of the consumer's agreement under the second paragraph of L. 221-13. The practical translation — two separate unticked boxes and a confirmation on a durable medium, archived — follows from the text and from L221-26 putting the consequence on the seller.

verdicts.claim: (b) If the waiver is botched, the buyer withdraws within 14 days, keeps the content and owes nothing, under art. L221-26.
verdicts.why: L221-26 reads as quoted: the consumer who withdraws from a contract for digital content without a material medium 'n'est redevable d'aucune somme' where the professional did not collect the prior express agreement and the proof of acknowledgment, or where the contract does not carry the mentions of the third paragraph of L. 221-9 and the second paragraph of L. 221-13. No pro-rata, unlike L221-25 for services, as claimed.
verdicts.correction: The quotation is cut with an ellipsis exactly where 1° continues 'après que le contrat aura été pleinement exécuté à la demande expresse de celui-ci'. Keep that clause when the text is reused — it is part of the condition, and dropping it makes 1° look broader than it is.

verdicts.claim: (b) Since 19 June 2026 an online withdrawal button is mandatory for distance contracts concluded through an online interface; it does not apply to a product with a valid waiver.
verdicts.why: This was the claim most at risk, because Ordonnance n° 2026-2 is titled for the distance marketing of financial services and transposes a financial-services directive. It survives: article 3 of the ordonnance adds to L. 221-21 a paragraph reading 'Pour les contrats conclus à distance au moyen d'une interface en ligne, le professionnel met à la disposition du consommateur, sans frais pour ce dernier, une fonctionnalité lui permettant d'exercer gratuitement son droit de rétractation avant l'expiration du délai prévu à l'article L. 221-18' — cross-referring to the general 14-day period, in the general provisions, not to the financial-services timetable. D221-5, created by Décret n° 2026-3 article 2 and in force 19 June 2026, prescribes 'renoncer au contrat ici', permanent visibility, the fields, the 'confirmer la rétractation' control, and an accusé de réception on a durable medium stating the declaration's content and the date and time of sending. All verbatim.
verdicts.correction: Two things are the claim's own reasoning rather than sourced text, and should be labelled as such: that a valid L221-28 13° waiver removes the functionality duty (it follows from the text conditioning the function on exercising the right, but no source says it), and the L242-13 sanction figure, which I did not verify.

verdicts.claim: (c) CGV are not a code-mandated document, but the information they carry is mandatory and must reach the buyer before the contract.
verdicts.why: The fiche, vérifiée le 1er juillet 2026, states that where the client is a particulier 'le vendeur a l'obligation de fournir les CGV avant la conclusion du contrat', that they 'peuvent être indiquées par tout moyen sur un support durable', and that for a professional buyer they need only be communicated on request. The required content for a distance B2C contract matches the list given, including mediation access and the 14-day withdrawal right with its model form.

verdicts.claim: (c) Active acceptance is required, and it is art. 1119 of the Code civil that requires it, not the consumer code; a footer link alone does not bind the buyer.
verdicts.why: Article 1119 al. 1 reads as quoted: general conditions have effect against the other party only if they were brought to that party's knowledge and that party accepted them. Al. 3 gives conditions particulières priority over conditions générales in case of conflict, as claimed.
verdicts.correction: One inference is presented as text. Article 1119 requires knowledge and acceptance; it does not prescribe an unticked checkbox, and acceptance may be express or, in some circumstances, tacit. The checkbox is sound practice under the caselaw, not a statutory requirement — state it that way so the CGV rationale does not rest on a misreading. The L121-17 / L132-22 point about pre-ticked boxes was not verified here.

verdicts.claim: (d) The double-clic is two rules, and the button wording is sanctioned by nullity of the contract, not a fine.
verdicts.why: Article L242-2 reads: the provisions of the second paragraph of article L. 221-14 are prescribed 'à peine de nullité du contrat conclu par voie électronique'. So the 'commande avec obligation de paiement' wording is indeed a nullity-sanctioned requirement, with the L242-10 administrative fine available on top. The article 1127-2 recap-and-correct rule and the 1127-3 derogation between professionals are correctly described, though I did not open them individually.

verdicts.claim: (e) A practice is misleading under art. L121-2 when it rests on false claims about essential characteristics, expressly including 'qualités substantielles' and 'mode et date de fabrication'.
verdicts.why: L121-2 2° b) lists the essential characteristics as 'ses qualités substantielles, sa composition, ses accessoires, son origine ... sa quantité, son mode et sa date de fabrication, les conditions de son utilisation et son aptitude à l'usage, ses propriétés' — the two limbs the argument turns on are in the text. L121-3 deems substantial, in any invitation to purchase quoting a price, the main characteristics, the professional's identity and address, the all-taxes price and the existence of a withdrawal right, as claimed.

verdicts.claim: (e) The penalty is criminal, and online the tier is 5 years and 750 000 EUR, not the 2 years / 300 000 EUR usually quoted; publication of the conviction is mandatory.
verdicts.why: L132-2 sets two years and 300 000 euros, with the fine raisable to 10% of average annual turnover over the last three years or 50% of the expenditure on the practice, and raises the penalties to five years and 750 000 euros where the offence is committed through an online public communication service or by digital means. L132-2-1 raises imprisonment to three years where the practices were followed by the conclusion of one or more contracts, as claimed. L521-1's astreinte of up to 3 000 euros per day capped at 300 000 euros is confirmed, including its amendment by loi n° 2025-594 du 30 juin 2025.
verdicts.correction: Worth knowing so the figure is not misquoted upward later: a seven-year tier exists but belongs to L132-2-2 and requires commission en bande organisée. The claim does not assert it, which is correct.

verdicts.claim: (e) 'Original hand-drawn illustration' beside a price is a false claim about the mode de fabrication; the exposure is the aggravated online tier and the proof is served by his own site.
verdicts.why: The law is right and is confirmed above: 'mode et date de fabrication' is named in L121-2 2° b), the aggravated online tier exists, and a pratique commerciale requires a professional acting in relation to the promotion or sale of a good, so the free atlas sits outside and a paid tier inside. What cannot be verified from any source in this audit is the factual premise the conclusion rests on — that the site says 'hand-drawn', that there are 1 838 SVGs of 654 to 1 118 bytes sharing one style block, and that this makes them machine-generated 'by any reading'. Those are assertions about his repository, checkable only against the repository.
verdicts.correction: Separate the register from the finding. The remedy is right, costs nothing and should be done: say 'illustrations vectorielles originales' or 'pictogrammes dessinés pour Copius', drop 'hand-drawn', 'dessiné à la main', 'fait main' and 'artisanal' from alt text, manifest, Open Graph and any press kit, and claim hand-made only where a source file proves it. But quoting a 750 000 EUR ceiling as the cost of not fixing it overstates the exposure by orders of magnitude: that is a statutory maximum for a criminal conviction, and the realistic first step for a 19-year-old with de minimis turnover is a DGCCRF injunction to bring the wording into line under L521-1. The word should change because it is untrue, not because of the number. The article liminaire 16° quotation was not verified verbatim.

verdicts.claim: (f) Naming a mediator is compulsory for any seller to consumers, with no size exemption.
verdicts.why: L612-1 reads as quoted: every consumer has the right to free recourse to a consumer mediator, and 'à cet effet, le professionnel garantit au consommateur le recours effectif à un dispositif de médiation de la consommation'. R616-1 requires the professional to communicate the mediator's contact details visibly and legibly on his website, his CGV, his order forms or failing those by any other appropriate means, and to state the mediator's own website address. No size or status exemption appears.

verdicts.claim: (f) Cost: free for the buyer by law, about 30 EUR for three years for him at his turnover, plus about 150 EUR HT per case.
verdicts.why: The SMP grid, effective 20 April 2026, reads: under 60 000 EUR turnover, '25€ht pour 3 ans (paiement unique à la signature de 30€TTC)'; the 60 000 to 999 999 EUR band as turnover divided by 2 000 for both entry fee and annual subscription; 'Médiation simple : 150 € HT' and 'Médiation complexe : 350 € HT'. The claim's own caution — one dated data point from one body, compare two or three and check whether the per-case fee is capped — is the right framing and should be kept.

verdicts.claim: (f) Penalty for not having one: an administrative fine of up to 3 000 EUR for a personne physique, 15 000 EUR for a personne morale, under art. L641-1.
verdicts.why: L641-1 sanctions breach of the information obligations of L. 616-1 and L. 616-2 with an administrative fine capped at 3 000 euros for a personne physique and 15 000 for a personne morale. The claim is also right about what it does and does not cover: it punishes failing to inform the consumer who the mediator is, which is checkable by loading the site.
verdicts.correction: The directory detail — sector codes B01 and O02, 21 and 9 referenced bodies, the named list — was not verified in this audit. Check it against the CECMC directory when he actually signs up, since the roster changes.

audits.overall:
I re-opened every cited source that was reachable. The corpus is unusually well-sourced: 34 of 43 claims check out verbatim, including the ones I most expected to fail (the 750 000 € online tier of L132-2 is real; the 60 000 € HT procurement threshold, the décret 2025-1386 dates, the 203 100 / 83 600 micro ceilings, the 37 500 / 41 250 TVA thresholds and the "25 000 € abandonnée" sentence, both DGFiP e-invoicing fact sheets, all three CNIL référentiel retention rules, and the Stripe requirements field list all reproduce word-for-word). Nine claims have defects, and four of them would actually change what he does.

The four that matter:
1. TVA — "0 EUR of VAT collected below 37 500 €" is wrong for his exact product. The French franchise en base does not cover B2C electronically-supplied services to consumers in other EU member states once the €10 000 pan-EU threshold is crossed; VAT is then due in the buyer's country through OSS. For a digital learning path sold across the EU, this is the live risk, and the claim states the French threshold as if it were the whole answer. It also quotes 37 500 / 41 250 without saying what crossing does: service-public says the franchise ends "dès le 1er jour du dépassement" — mid-year, not next year.
2. E-invoicing — the 1 September 2027 emission deadline does not bind the lycée sale as "B2B". Sales to a public EPLE run through the pre-existing Chorus Pro / secteur public channel (mandatory since 2020), not the new B2B mandate, which covers transactions between assujettis établis en France. A private CFA may be different. The claim merges two regimes.
3. Stripe — the field-list finding is real and I re-derived it, but it does not answer "can he onboard". Stripe's own SSA says users "must not ... use the Services for personal, family, or household purposes", and Stripe's "individual" entity type means sole trader, not private person. Combined with the dissimulation-d'activité claim, which is correct, the honest answer is: register first, then open the account.
4. Favoritisme is not only the buyer's risk. "Favoritisme is the risk the buyer, not he, carries" ignores complicity (art. 121-7 C. pén.), under which private contractors are routinely prosecuted alongside the official. That matters because he is a student in the BTS MHR lane he would be selling into.

Smaller but real: the Kbis line in the pre-signature pack is stale (since 1 November 2021 a candidate supplies a SIREN, not a Kbis); Polar's +1.5% turns on the buyer's card country, not the seller's; the Paddle "Sumsub / 1–3 business days" detail is not on the cited page, which says 2–4 days and does not name the provider; the student-status claim carries a guillemeted quote that does not exist on the page, plus a defunct concept (the régime étudiant de sécurité sociale was abolished in 2018–19); and the 10-year accounting basis (C. com. L123-22) binds commerçants — if his activity is BNC, his binding floor is LPF L102 B at 6 years.

Two process notes. The corpus says he is 18; your brief says 19. Nothing legal turns on it (both are majeur) but the "he turned 18 before any sale" reasoning should be restated. And the whole corpus is a September 2026 snapshot for a late-2027 decision: the micro ceilings hold to 2028 by the three-year revalorisation cycle (the author correctly flags this as inference, not something read), but the TVA thresholds, the procurement ceiling and the AURA appel à projets figures are all annual and will need re-checking.

One thing nobody claimed that he is leaving on the table: at 19 he is in the 18–25 bracket eligible for ACRE, worth a 50% exonération of cotisations in year one.

verdicts.claim: (f) Do NOT copy the ODR-platform link from any CGV template. The European ODR platform was shut down on 20 July 2025.
verdicts.why: The Commission page carries the sentence verbatim — "The European Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Platform is discontinued as of 20 July 2025" — and cites Regulation (EU) 2024/3228. It names the replacement routes the claim describes: the consumer-redress site, the list of dispute-resolution bodies, and Your Europe. The dead art. L616-2 cross-reference is a fair reading.

verdicts.claim: (g) Selling to a lycée removes almost the entire consumer layer — no 14-day withdrawal, no L221-5 regime, no mediator obligation.
verdicts.why: L221-3 reads as quoted: it extends sections 2, 3 and 6 only to contracts "conclus hors établissement" between professionals where the object falls outside the solicited professional's main activity and it employs five or fewer. An online distance sale never reaches those conditions. Worth adding for his benefit: even if L221-3 did apply it would protect the lycée, never him — it shields the solicited party.

verdicts.claim: (g) The misleading-practice exposure follows him into the B2B sale. Art. L121-5 extends arts. L121-2 to L121-4 to practices aimed at professionals and non-professionals; the 750 000 EUR online tier of L132-2 still applies.
verdicts.why: L121-5 carries the quoted sentence. I specifically went after the 750 000 € figure expecting it to be invented, and it is real: where the offence is committed through an online public communication service or a digital medium, L132-2 raises the penalty to five years and 750 000 €, up from two years and 300 000 €. The claim understates it if anything — it omits the prison tier.

verdicts.claim: (g) Below 60 000 EUR HT a lycée can buy with no publicity and no competitive tendering; invoicing goes through Chorus Pro, so a SIRET is a hard precondition.
verdicts.why: Service-public, vérifié 21 août 2026, gives 60 000 € HT for fournitures et services and 100 000 € HT for travaux as the current figures. The Chorus Pro leg holds: administrations are required to use it, e-invoicing to the public sector has bound suppliers of every size since 2020, and from September 2026 a supplier may route via an approved platform instead. The SIRET-as-precondition conclusion follows.

verdicts.claim: Student, age and foyer fiscal: none of this changes a line of consumer law. He is 18 and legally capable.
verdicts.why: The legal reasoning is sound — the code keys on "professionnel", a student selling a paid tier is one, and foyer fiscal rattachement bites on tax and cotisations, not on the Code de la consommation. The art. 19 LCEN address point is right and is the real consequence. One correction that changes nothing legally: your brief describes him as 19, this claim says 18, so the "turned 18 before any sale" argument should be restated on the correct age.

verdicts.claim: Source-access note: legifrance, DGCCRF and EUR-Lex refused automated access; code articles come from the droit.org PDF mirror built from the Legifrance API.
verdicts.why: I could not test the author's tooling, but I could test the output, which is the material point: I re-derived L221-3 and L121-5 from independent sources (Doctrine, Légifrance search) and both match the mirror's text and dating. The mirror is not introducing errors. The author's closing instruction — re-check every figure before acting, this is a 2026 snapshot for a 2027 decision — is correct and should be kept.

verdicts.claim: Stripe requires no SIRET, no registration number and no tax ID from a French INDIVIDUAL account.
verdicts.why: The field list is real — I re-ran the endpoint and got exactly the 17 fields claimed, with no company.tax_id, no registration_number, no id_number and no documents.* entry. But that is the onboarding schema, not his eligibility, and the claim is used elsewhere to conclude "the onboarding form will let him through". Stripe's own SSA forbids it independently of French law.
verdicts.correction: Stripe's Services Agreement states users "must not ... use the Services for personal, family, or household purposes". Stripe's "individual" legal entity type means sole trader — someone doing business without a company — not a private person. So the honest sequence is immatriculation first, then the Stripe account: French law and Stripe's own contract point the same way, and the empty SIRET field does not create a route around either.

verdicts.claim: The real bar is French, not Stripe's: repeated selling with no immatriculation is dissimulation d'activité — up to 3 years and 45 000 €.
verdicts.why: Service-public, vérifié 3 juillet 2026, gives the quoted example — "absence d'immatriculation au RCS ou au RNE" — and 3 years plus 45 000 € for a personne physique, aggravated to 5 years and 75 000 € where a minor or vulnerable person is involved, under L8224-1 to L8224-6. The page adds a tier the claim omits: 10 years and 100 000 € en bande organisée, irrelevant here.

verdicts.claim: Stripe's minimum age is 13, with an adult representative required only under 18 — he is clear.
verdicts.why: The SSA carries both sentences: "Only people 13 years of age or older may open a Stripe Account and use the Services", and the under-18 adult-representative requirement naming a parent or legal guardian, with Brazil carved out at a hard 18. At 19 none of it binds him, so this claim is accurate and inert.

verdicts.claim: Stripe's document rules are strict on form; the France-specific accepted-document row did NOT render and is unverified.
verdicts.why: I did not re-open this page, so I am neither confirming nor refuting the common-requirement list. The claim's own verdict is the right one and should be left standing: treat "CNI or passport or permis de conduire" as probable but unconfirmed. Note the next claim partly closes this gap from a different Stripe page.

verdicts.claim: Stripe Identity covers French government documents and runs an anti-spoofing liveness check.
verdicts.why: The page carries the quoted availability sentence naming carte nationale d'identité, permis de conduire and passeports, and FR appears in the supported-country list. The anti-spoofing statement is there too — computer vision and AI to confirm a real document rather than images from stolen documents or someone else's face — as is the real-time expiry warning.

verdicts.claim: Paddle waives business verification entirely for individuals and sole traders; identity verification runs through Sumsub, typically instant, 1-3 business days on manual review.
verdicts.why: The load-bearing sentence is verbatim on the page: "Please note, this step is not required for individuals or sole traders." The supporting detail is not.
verdicts.correction: The cited page does not name Sumsub — it says only that signup information goes to "a third-party tool" and explicitly does not disclose which. It also gives 2-4 business days for manual review, not 1-3. And it details only the business step; the identity-document and proof-of-address list attributed to it is not on that page. Keep the exemption sentence, drop the provider name and the timescale, or re-source them.

verdicts.claim: Paddle: 5% + $0.50 per checkout transaction, and products under $10 are pushed to custom pricing.
verdicts.why: Both quotes are on the page: "5% + 50¢ per Checkout transaction" and "If you're selling products under $10 or require invoicing contact us for custom pricing". No publication date is shown, as the claim says. One arithmetic wrinkle: the floor is $10, not €10, so a €10 price point is roughly $11.7 and sits above the floor, not "at or below" it.

verdicts.claim: Polar: free tier 5% + 50¢, +1.5% on non-US cards; for a French seller every card is 'international', so read the free-tier rate as 6.5% + 50¢.
verdicts.why: The fee table is exactly as quoted — Starter free 5% + 50¢, Pro $20/mo 3.8% + 40¢, Growth $100/mo 3.6% + 35¢, Scale $400/mo 3.4% + 30¢, plus the $15 dispute fee and the payout costs. The surcharge sentence is verbatim. The inference from it is not.
verdicts.correction: "+1.5% for international cards (non-US)" turns on the country that issued the buyer's card, not on where the seller sits. A French seller taking a US buyer's card pays no surcharge. The 6.5% figure happens to hold for a French audience, but the stated reason — "for a French seller every card is international" — is false and will misprice any US traffic.

verdicts.claim: Gumroad: 10% + $0.50, merchant of record for tax since 1 January 2025; 30% through Discover.
verdicts.why: All three figures are verbatim on the pricing page, including "Since January 1, 2025, Gumroad handles ALL your tax obligations" and the 30% Discover rate. The ~1.96 EUR / ~13% arithmetic on a 15 EUR sale is right, which does make it the worst of the three at his price point.

verdicts.claim: FastSpring is a merchant of record but publishes no rate.
verdicts.why: The page publishes no percentage and no fixed fee, only "simple, flat-rate pricing based on transaction type and your volume of business" negotiated with sales. It does assert the MoR role and responsibility for collecting and remitting sales tax and VAT and responding to audits. Unusable for comparison without contacting them, as the claim says.

verdicts.claim: The registre des traitements becomes mandatory the day he has his first customer — CNIL's own example kills the under-250 exemption.
verdicts.why: CNIL states the obligation "concerne tous les organismes, publics comme privés et quelle que soit leur taille", and the under-250 derogation is cancelled for three categories of which the first is traitements non occasionnels, whose stated example is "gestion de la paie, gestion des clients/prospects et des fournisseurs". A customer file is non-occasional by construction. The claim's aside is also right: the free newsletter list already triggers this today.

verdicts.claim: He signs no DPA with Stripe — it is already part of the contract — and Stripe is BOTH his processor and an independent controller.
verdicts.why: The DPA states it "est soumis au Contrat, dont il fait partie intégrante", so accepting the SSA accepts it and there is nothing to sign separately. The dual-role split is as described: processor for operating the platform and delivering the services, independent controller for fraud detection, AML/KYC compliance, loss prevention, billing and product development. Last updated 18 novembre 2025, as claimed.

verdicts.claim: He is the controller for his customer file; the provider is processor for the platform only — and with a merchant of record the roles change.
verdicts.why: CNIL's definition is verbatim: the sous-traitant "traite des données pour le compte d'un autre organisme". The dual-role registre entry the claim prescribes follows from the Stripe DPA, which I confirmed separately. The claim's own caveat is the right one to keep: with an MoR the buyer's counterparty is Paddle/Polar/Gumroad, which likely shifts the controller analysis for transaction data, and that needs confirming in each provider's DPA before it is relied on.

verdicts.claim: Accounting retention is 10 years from the close of the financial year, under Code de commerce L123-22.
verdicts.why: The page carries the 10-year figure and the L123-22 citation for factures, livres et registres and pièces justificatives, and the L213-1 / 120 € consumer rule is correctly described and correctly dismissed for a 10-19 EUR product. The problem is which taxpayer L123-22 binds.
verdicts.correction: L123-22 sits in the Code de commerce's accounting obligations for commerçants. If his activity is BNC — selling content he authored himself, which is the likely characterisation for a learning path — he is not a commerçant and the binding floor is instead Livre des procédures fiscales L102 B at 6 years, which the same service-public page gives. Keeping 10 years is safe either way, so nothing he does changes; but "only the accounting rule bites" asserts a basis that may not be his, and he should settle BIC vs BNC before writing it into a retention policy.

verdicts.claim: The 10-year duty and the minimisation duty do not collide — CNIL sequences them into base active then archivage intermédiaire, on different legal bases.
verdicts.why: I extracted the référentiel and the passage is verbatim, including the part the claim leans hardest on: archived data "sont traitées pour une autre finalité que l'exécution du contrat" and must rest on another legal basis, "tel que l'intérêt légitime prévu à l'article 6.1.f ou l'obligation légale prévue à l'article 6.1.c". The dedicated archive database or logical separation after sorting is there too. The operational conclusion — purge live, keep the invoice separated for 10 years under 6.1.c, restrict access — is exactly what the document says.

verdicts.claim: Customer and prospect data for marketing: 3 years, with the clock defined precisely; 2 years of inactivity for abandoned accounts.
verdicts.why: Verbatim in the référentiel, down to the detail the claim singles out: a click on a hyperlink in an email counts as contact from the prospect, "en revanche, la simple ouverture d'un courriel ne devrait pas être considérée comme un contact". The 3-year clock examples (purchase, warranty expiry, contract term, last contact) and the re-permission step at 3 years are there. The inactive-account rule is too: "un délai de deux ans apparait proportionné".

verdicts.claim: An identity document copy is kept only as long as the verification needs it — 6 years maximum, and never in the live base.
verdicts.why: The référentiel says a copy may be kept "pour une durée maximale de 6 ans" where needed for evidence or a legal obligation, with reinforced security measures, and that "ces informations ne doivent pas être conservées en base active mais doivent être stockées en base d'archivage intermédiaire". The claim's scoping is also right — this bites only if he collects ID himself, not on the ID he hands Stripe, which Stripe holds under its own AML duty as controller.

verdicts.claim: What changes in the privacy notice on day one of paying customers: five specific lines.
verdicts.why: CNIL's mandatory list matches: controller identity and contact, purposes, legal basis, obligatory-or-optional character, recipients or categories, retention duration or the criteria setting it, rights, DPO contact, right to complain to the CNIL, plus transfers outside the EU and withdrawal of consent where applicable, and the re-information duty on substantial modification. He needs no DPO. One thing to keep straight: "legal basis is contract, not consent" holds for order and delivery management only — his newsletter still runs on consent under art. L34-5 CPCE, which CNIL's own table confirms.

verdicts.claim: 2026 micro-entreprise ceilings: 203 100 € goods, 83 600 € services — his lane is the 83 600 €.
verdicts.why: Service-public gives both figures for turnover received in 2026, exactly as quoted, and all three of his shapes are prestations de services, so 83 600 € is the operative one. The loss-of-regime rule (exceeded in both N-1 and N-2, switch on 1 January following) is correctly stated. The 2027-2028 projection is explicitly flagged by the author as inference from the three-year revalorisation cycle rather than something read, which is the right level of confidence.

verdicts.claim: The 25 000 € single VAT threshold was ABANDONED — franchise en base for services is 37 500 € in 2026, so 0 EUR of VAT collected below 37 500 €.
verdicts.why: The abandonment sentence is verbatim on service-public, vérifié 1 janvier 2026, and the 2026 thresholds are as quoted: 37 500 / 41 250 for services, 85 000 / 93 500 for commerce. So the contested reform is genuinely settled and the claim is right to say so. Two gaps make the cost line unsafe for his product.
verdicts.correction: First, the French franchise does not cover B2C electronically-supplied services to consumers in other EU member states. Below the €10 000 pan-EU threshold those sales are taxable in France and the franchise absorbs them; above it, VAT is due in the buyer's country and must be declared through OSS, whatever his French turnover. A learning path sold EU-wide is precisely the product that hits this, so "0 EUR of VAT collected below 37 500 €" is true only of his French sales. Second, the claim quotes 41 250 € without saying what crossing it does: the same page says the franchise ceases "dès le 1er jour du dépassement" — VAT starts mid-year, not the following January.

verdicts.claim: Student and micro-entrepreneur are compatible; at 18+ every activity type is open to him, and he keeps his student social security affiliation.
verdicts.why: The substance holds — the page says "Un étudiant ayant atteint la majorité peut exercer n'importe quelle activité (commerciale, libérale, artisanale)", subject to qualification conditions for regulated ones, and the minor/emancipated-minor rules are as described. The foyer fiscal point is on the page. Two defects.
verdicts.correction: The guillemeted source_quote — "Étudiant majeur : toute activité — commerciale, libérale ou artisanale — sous réserve des qualifications requises" — does not appear on the page in that form; it is a reconstruction presented as a quotation, which is exactly the kind of thing that collapses if anyone checks it. And "he keeps his student social security affiliation" describes a regime that no longer exists: the régime étudiant de sécurité sociale was abolished in 2018-19 and students are on the régime général; a micro-entrepreneur simply adds cotisations under the régime micro-social. The page says nothing about bourses either, as the claim concedes.

verdicts.claim: A dedicated bank account is required only above 10 000 € of turnover for 2 consecutive years, and need not be a professional account.
verdicts.why: Service-public, vérifié 28 mai 2026, gives the threshold verbatim and confirms it may be a separate personal account rather than a compte professionnel. The claim's third element also checks out and is the one that bites in practice: "le compte bancaire dédié à l'activité professionnelle doit contenir la mention « entrepreneur individuel » ou « EI »", which is what makes banks decline an ordinary personal account for the purpose.

verdicts.claim: His likely commercialisation date lands exactly on the e-invoicing emission deadline, 1 September 2027 — this binds shape (b), the licence sold to a lycée or CFA, which is B2B.
verdicts.why: I extracted the DGFiP fact sheet and every date and quotation is verbatim, including "Mise à jour juin 2026", the 1 September 2026 reception duty, the 1 September 2027 emission duty for micro and PME, and the sentence that reception "n'induit pas obligatoirement" emission with the supplier bearing the knowledge burden. The categorisation of the lycée sale is where it goes wrong.
verdicts.correction: The fiche scopes the emission duty to invoices "à destination des professionnels établis en France", and the reform covers transactions between assujettis établis en France. A public EPLE is a non-assujetti public buyer: invoices to it run through the Chorus Pro / secteur public channel, which has bound suppliers of every size since 2020 and which the DGFiP confirms continues alongside the reform. So the 2027 date does not gate the lycée licence — Chorus Pro already does, today. A private CFA that is an assujetti is a different case and may genuinely fall under the 2027 mandate; the claim should split them.

verdicts.claim: Selling to individuals triggers e-reporting from 1 September 2027, and franchise en base does NOT exempt him.
verdicts.why: Fiche 7, extracted in full, confirms every element. B2C is defined as sales to personnes physiques or personnes morales non assujetties, "en France comme à l'étranger", with private individuals and non-profit associations as the examples; B2B international is the separate limb; the start date is 1 September 2027; and the periodicity depends on the VAT regime with "franchise en base" named first, so being under the threshold sets the frequency and does not remove the duty. The privacy consolation is verbatim: "aucune donnée personnelle n'est demandée et ne doit être transmise", only daily aggregate turnover split by rate.

verdicts.claim: The no-procedure ceiling is now 60 000 € HT, not 40 000 €. It changed on 1 April 2026; travaux went to 100 000 € HT on 1 January 2026.
verdicts.why: Décret n° 2025-1386 du 29 décembre 2025 modified R2122-8 and R2132-2, raising fournitures et services from 40 000 to 60 000 € HT effective 1 April 2026 and travaux from 40 000 to 100 000 € HT effective 1 January 2026, applying to consultations engagées from those dates. Both staggered dates are right, which is the detail most secondary guides get wrong. The warning that any 40 000 € figure in a 2022-2025 guide is stale is well taken.

verdicts.claim: Below the ceiling the buyer still owes three duties — and favoritisme is the risk the buyer, not he, carries.
verdicts.why: The three duties are the real text of R2122-8 al. 2: choose a relevant offer, make good use of public money, and not contract systematically with the same operator where there is a plurality of offers. The practical advice — a devis and ideally a second comparable quote in the file — follows correctly. The allocation of criminal risk does not.
verdicts.correction: Favoritisme (art. 432-14 C. pén.) and prise illégale d'intérêts (art. 432-12) are offences of the public official, but a private contractor who participates is routinely prosecuted as complice under art. 121-7 C. pén. Saying the risk is the buyer's "not he" is the kind of reassurance that should not be in a document he acts on — particularly since the scenario under discussion is him selling into the BTS lane he is himself enrolled in, which is a governance problem before it is a procurement one. Note the cited source is a commercial site whose own page slug still reads "inférieurs à 40 000 € HT"; the duties are right, but cite R2122-8 directly.

verdicts.claim: The signature is the proviseur's, but the conseil d'administration must have authorised it first; sell a 12-month licence with express renewal, not an auto-renewing subscription.
verdicts.why: R421-20 gives the CA accord on "la passation des marchés, contrats et conventions dont l'établissement est signataire", with the carve-outs described: markets inside an adopted décision modificative, urgent gestion courante below 5 000 € HT for services, and marchés à incidence annuelle where the CA has delegated to the chef d'établissement. The commercial conclusion — annual express renewal keeps it inside a standing délégation, a pluriannuel or tacitly-renewed subscription needs its own CA vote — follows. The carve-out also carries 15 000 € HT for travaux et équipements, which the claim omits as irrelevant here.

verdicts.claim: The money comes from the EPLE's service AP, inside a budget the CA votes before 30 November for the following calendar year.
verdicts.why: The IH2EF page, updated 11 February 2026, gives the three services of the section de fonctionnement as activités pédagogiques (AP), vie de l'élève (VE) and administration et logistique (ALO), the dotation notified before 1 November, and the CA vote before 30 November so the budget is executable on 1 January. The selling-window inference — September to November, for money spent the following year — is sound and is the most actionable thing in the procurement lane.

verdicts.claim: No supplier is legally required to be in LDE, PopLab or any catalogue.
verdicts.why: Article 2 of the arrêté du 22 mars 2019 lists what an acheteur may demand, and neither catalogue referencing nor platform membership appears anywhere in it. The claim's two real constraints are correctly separated from the imaginary one. Worth noting against it, though, that the AURA appel à projets points candidates at a PopLab reference list for examples, so the catalogue is a practical channel even where it is not a legal condition — which is roughly what the claim's medium confidence already concedes.

verdicts.claim: The GAR is the real gate, and it is an engineering project, not a form.
verdicts.why: The adhesion page confirms all four elements: the éditeur signs a contrat d'adhésion, declares its technical and commercial distributors and a valideur technique, and must build three interfaces — moissonnage of resource descriptions, a webservice for subscription management, and SSO for access management — with dossiers requested at dne-gar@education.gouv.fr. The conclusion that a static PWA with no per-pupil accounts is a rewrite rather than a config change is fair. The arrêté du 18/12/2017 and CNIL délibération 2017-253 are cited on linked pages rather than this one, so those two references are unconfirmed but immaterial.

verdicts.claim: The AURA appel à projets is not open to him. Only lycées apply — a supplier is named inside a school's dossier, never a candidate.
verdicts.why: I extracted the 2025-2026 document. Bénéficiaires: "Les lycées publics et privés du territoire régional Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes qu'il s'agisse de lycées généraux, technologiques, professionnels ou agricoles." The 190 K€ envelope, the exclusion of licences numériques de manuel scolaire, the exclusion of matériel or software without pedagogical purpose, the 40% weighting on pedagogical quality as judged by the autorités académiques, and the GAR-compatibility note for public établissements are all there. The strategic conclusion — the only way in is a teacher writing it into their school's dossier — is exactly right. Note this is the 2025-2026 edition and he is targeting late 2027, so the envelope and dates will move.

verdicts.claim: URSSAF attestation de vigilance is required from 5 000 € HT, valid 6 months, renewed every six months for the life of the contract.
verdicts.why: Service-public, vérifié 6 juillet 2026, gives "montant égal ou supérieur à 5 000 € hors taxes" and "valable 6 mois" with periodic renewal through the contract, cites L8222-1 to L8222-7, and confirms it applies to a "travailleur indépendant qui n'emploie pas de salarié" — so a solo micro-entrepreneur is in scope, as the claim says. The practical point that a first lycée licence will sit below 5 000 € HT is right, and so is the warning that gestionnaires may ask regardless.

verdicts.claim: The standard pre-signature pack is social attestation, fiscal declaration on honour, and proof of registration — an extrait K or Kbis less than three months old — plus SIREN on every invoice.
verdicts.why: The invoice half is confirmed on service-public, vérifié 7 août 2026: the numéro SIREN, and for an entrepreneur individuel "Nom et prénom de l'entrepreneur individuel précédé ou suivi de la mention « Entrepreneur individuel ou EI »". The conclusion that no SIRET means no sale to a public body is right. The Kbis element is out of date, and its source is a February 2022 vademecum.
verdicts.correction: Since 1 November 2021 a company no longer supplies a Kbis extract in a public-procurement candidature: it gives its SIREN and the buyer retrieves the data itself from annuaire-entreprises.data.gouv.fr, with the INPI/RNE extract having replaced the Kbis in administrative use since 2023. Supplying one remains a fallback if the directory lookup fails. Keep the récépissé de dépôt point — that is still the useful one, since it lets him bid while registration is processing.

verdicts.claim: Invoices to any public body go through Chorus Pro. That has been true since 2020 and survives the 2026 e-invoicing reform.
verdicts.why: The impots.gouv article, published 18/07/2025 and modified 09/09/2025, states administrations "sont tenues d'utiliser Chorus Pro" for receiving and processing these invoices, and confirms that from September 2026 suppliers may instead route via a plateforme agréée while Chorus Pro remains the reference platform — with travaux, mémoires de frais de justice and demandes de remboursement staying Chorus-Pro-only, as the claim says. The phase-in reached microentreprises on 1 January 2020, so "every company regardless of size since 2020" is right.

verdicts.claim: RC pro is not legally required for a non-regulated digital activity — but a public buyer is allowed to demand proof of it.
verdicts.why: Both legs hold. Service-public confirms RCP is mandatory for activités réglementées, with décennale for bâtiment and medical liability for health, and merely recommended otherwise. Article 2 of the arrêté du 22 mars 2019 does let the acheteur require "preuve d'une assurance des risques professionnels pertinents" as a capacité économique document — I read that clause directly. The claim's own two caveats are the right ones and should be kept: the service-public fiche is dated 22 September 2023, and the 160-240 €/an figure is a broker's commercial page, so get two real quotes.

verdicts.claim: RGAA does not bind him as a seller. It reaches him through the buyer's contract clauses instead — and that is the harder version.
verdicts.why: Article 47 of loi 2005-102, as implemented by décret 2019-768, reaches public bodies, delegated public-service missions, bodies created for non-commercial general-interest needs, and companies from 250 M€ of French turnover — a solo seller sits outside all four. And R2111-6 reads exactly as quoted, with no monetary threshold and only a "cas dûment justifié" escape, so it applies to a 3 000 € MAPA as much as to a formal tender. The asymmetry the claim identifies is real: no accessibility floor protects him on the public route.

verdicts.claim: On the private-sale side the European Accessibility Act already applies, and he is exempt as a microentreprise — for now.
verdicts.why: Service-public, published 27 November 2025, gives the exemption as quoted — fewer than 10 salariés with annual turnover or balance-sheet total under 2 million euros — and the 28 June 2025 application date. E-commerce is in scope of directive (UE) 2019/882 and he clears the exemption by a wide margin. The claim correctly flags that it could not open EUR-Lex, so the wording is the French administration's restatement rather than article 4(5) itself; the substance matches the directive as I understand it.
